00. Start here: BLADUS backend blueprint

In plain words
BLADUS has a finished-looking website and admin, but no real backend: data lives in memory and the two apps do not share it.
This folder is the complete plan for that backend, built with Django and PostgreSQL, designed for Algeria.
It was written before any backend code: what exists, what to build, the rules, the database, the API, security, hosting, tests and the plan.
Verdict: ready to start the first milestone now; real customer data waits for two legal answers on hosting.
New to these topics? Read explain-like-im-new.md first. Everything in one file: dist/BLADUS-backend-blueprint.pdf.

Terms used here (all in glossary.md): backend (the server program that stores data and applies rules), API (the list of addresses the apps call), schema (the design of the database tables), milestone (a 3 to 5 week block of work).

Prepared 2026-11-04 to 2026-11-09. Documentation only: no backend code exists yet.

1. The plan in ten lines

  1. Stack: Django 6.1, Django REST Framework, PostgreSQL with PostGIS, Redis and Celery, django-allauth (email and phone codes, two-factor login). The two Next.js apps stay and call the API through their server (02-research.md B, 07-architecture.md).
  2. Money (DEC-001): guests pay hosts directly; hosts keep a prepaid deposit; BLADUS deducts its commission (12% individual, 15% agency, 18% hotel, 10% hostel) on each confirmed booking. Guests pay no BLADUS fee. Everything is recorded in a double-entry ledger.
  3. No double booking: the database itself refuses overlapping stays and over-selling of rooms, beds and seats (05-database-schema.md).
  4. Who publishes what (DEC-014): solo hosts publish homes and vehicles, agencies publish experiences and trips, hotels and hostels publish their property.
  5. Types (DEC-015): 8 experience types and 8 trip types, one shared list.
  6. Moderation (DEC-003): new listings and trips are reviewed by staff before going live.
  7. Algeria: hosting in Algeria and a .com.dz domain are likely required; personal data should not leave the country without authorisation (VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL).
  8. Size: 147 requirements (126 in the first release), 77 tables, 266 API operations.
  9. Plan: 8 milestones (M0 to M7, about 29 weeks plus a 2-week buffer) for a team of 2 backend developers and 1 part-time frontend developer, then R2 (11-roadmap.md).
  10. Open: 48 decisions remain, most of them for the lawyer and accountant (13-decisions-needed.md).

Explain it like I'm new

In plain words
This page explains the whole BLADUS backend plan with no jargon, as a story.
Read it first if words like "API", "database" or "ledger" feel unclear.
It follows one guest, one host and one staff member through the system.
Every other document goes deeper into one part of this story.
Words in bold are explained in glossary.md.

1. What we have today, and what is missing

BLADUS already has two websites:

  • the website where travellers search and book, and where hosts manage their places (the frontend folder);
  • the admin where BLADUS staff check hosts, listings, bookings and money (the admin folder).

Both look finished, but behind the screens there is no real storage. Every booking, every host, every message lives in the computer's memory and disappears when the server restarts. The two websites also do not talk to each other: a booking made on the website never appears in the admin.

The missing piece is the backend: one program, running on a server, that keeps all the data safely in a database and is the single source of truth for both websites. We will build it with Django (a Python framework the owner already knows).

2. The main idea in one picture

Traveller / Host browser ──> Website (Next.js) ──┐
                                                 ├──> Django API ──> PostgreSQL database
Staff browser ───────────> Admin (Next.js)  ─────┘          │
                                                           └──> SMS, email, file storage
  • The websites stay as they are. Only the inside of their "data" functions changes: instead of reading memory, they ask the API.
  • The API is a list of addresses like POST /api/v1/bookings ("create a booking"). The full list is in 06-api-design.md and openapi.yaml.
  • The database is PostgreSQL. It has 77 tables (like 77 spreadsheet tabs) described in 05-database-schema.md.

3. A guest books a villa

Yacine wants 3 nights in a villa in Tipaza.

  1. Search. The website asks the API for villas in Tipaza for his dates. The API looks in the database and only returns villas whose nights are free.
  2. Price. He opens the villa. The API calculates the price itself (3 nights x 18,500 DZD + 4,000 cleaning = 59,500 DZD). Guests pay no BLADUS fee.
  3. Book. He clicks Reserve. The API saves the booking. The database has a built-in rule that refuses two bookings on the same night for the same villa, so even if two people click at the same second, only one wins.
  4. Pay. At launch Yacine pays the host directly (cash or transfer). BLADUS does not touch the guest's money. (This is decision DEC-001; the reason is Algerian payment law, see 02-research.md section C.1.)
  5. Messages. He and the host chat in the app. Phone numbers are hidden until the booking is confirmed, to stop scams.

4. How BLADUS earns money

BLADUS takes a commission from the host, not from the guest:

Host type Commission
Individual 12%
Agency 15%
Hotel 18%
Hostel 10%

Each host keeps a deposit with BLADUS (like a prepaid phone card). When a booking is confirmed, the commission is taken from that deposit. For Yacine's villa: 12% of 55,500 = 6,660 DZD.

Every money movement is written in a ledger: a notebook where lines are only added, never erased. If there is a mistake, a correcting line is added. This makes it easy to prove where every dinar went.

5. A host joins

Amina wants to rent her home.

  1. She signs up and verifies her phone with a code by SMS.
  2. She fills the "become a host" steps. Her answers are saved on the server, so she can continue on another device.
  3. She uploads her ID and proof of ownership. These files go to private storage that only staff can open, and every opening is recorded.
  4. A moderator checks the documents and approves her.
  5. She creates a listing. It is checked by staff before it appears in search (DEC-003).

What each host type can publish is fixed (DEC-014): individuals publish homes and vehicles, agencies publish experiences and trips, hotels and hostels publish their property with its rooms.

6. Staff work in the admin

Nadia, a moderator, opens the admin. She sees queues: hosts to verify, listings to review, reported reviews. Each item shows how long it has been waiting. When she approves or refuses, the reason is saved and the host is notified. Every action she takes is written in an audit log that nobody can edit.

Finance staff record host deposits (for example a transfer to BLADUS's CCP account). Above 500,000 DZD a second person must approve, to prevent mistakes and fraud.

7. Things that happen by themselves

Some work runs in the background on a schedule (jobs):

  • a request that the host does not answer within 24 hours expires and both sides are told;
  • after check-out, the booking becomes "completed" and the review window opens;
  • SMS and emails are sent after a change is saved, and retried if they fail.

8. Why Algeria matters in the design

  • Hosting: Algerian law likely requires an e-commerce site hosted in Algeria with a .com.dz name, and personal data should not leave the country without permission. So the plan puts the servers in Algeria (VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL).
  • Payments: collecting guests' money and paying hosts may need a payment licence, which is why we start with the deposit model.
  • Geography: 69 wilayas and 1,541 communes, in Arabic, French and English.
  • Formats: weekend is Friday and Saturday, Latin digits even in Arabic, phone numbers start with +213 5, 6 or 7.

Glossary

In plain words
Every technical or business word used in the blueprint, explained in one or two sentences.
If a document uses a word you do not know, look here first. The list grows with each phase.

Term Meaning
ActionResult What a Next.js server action returns today: success with data, or an error code.
lib/data seam The folder of data functions both apps call; each becomes an API call.
ADR Architecture Decision Record: a short note saying what was decided, why, and what else was considered.
Allauth (headless) A Django library for sign-up, login, phone codes and two-factor login, used through an API.
ANPDP Algeria's personal data protection authority (Autorité nationale de protection des données à caractère personnel).
API The set of web addresses (endpoints) the apps call to read and change data.
Audit log A list of who did what and when; never edited, only added to.
BFF Backend for frontend: the Next.js server keeps the login cookie and calls Django on the browser's behalf.
Booking / Reservation One guest's purchase of a unit for a time. The admin calls it Booking, the website Reservation.
Celery A Python tool that runs background jobs (expire requests, send SMS) outside the web request.
Centimes Hundredths of a dinar. We store money as whole centimes to avoid rounding errors.
CI/CD Continuous integration and delivery: every code change is automatically checked (tests, lint) and, if green, deployed to staging.
CIB / Edahabia Algeria's bank card and postal card, accepted online through SATIM.
Commission The percentage BLADUS earns on a booking, paid by the host. Guests pay no BLADUS fee.
Cursor (pagination) A bookmark returned by the API (for example the last message id) so the next request asks only for what came after it.
Double-entry ledger Money records where each movement has lines that add up to zero, so money is never created or lost by mistake.
DPIA Data protection impact assessment: a written analysis of the risks of a sensitive processing (here: host ID documents).
DRF Django REST Framework, the library that turns Django into an API.
Endpoint One API address with one method, for example POST /api/v1/bookings (create a booking).
ETag / If-Match A version tag returned with a record; sending it back with a change makes the API refuse the change if someone else edited the record meanwhile.
Exclusion constraint A PostgreSQL rule that refuses overlapping date ranges for the same unit.
Feature flag A setting that turns a feature on or off without changing code (for example the dormant payment endpoints).
Gantt chart A timeline chart showing each milestone as a bar between its start and end dates.
Gate A decision or legal answer that must exist before a milestone can finish.
Half-open range A date range that includes the first day and excludes the last: [check-in, check-out). Check-out day is free for the next guest.
HMAC hash A one-way fingerprint made with a secret key; used to compare ID or phone numbers without storing them in clear.
Hold A short reservation of inventory while a guest pays; it expires automatically.
Host type individual, agency, hotel or hostel.
Idempotency key A unique request ID; repeating the request with the same key does not repeat its effect.
import-linter A tool that fails the build if one Django app imports another it is not allowed to use.
k6 A load-testing tool that simulates many users to check response times.
KYC Know your customer: checking identity and business documents.
MFA / TOTP / passkey Two-step login. TOTP is a 6-digit code from an authenticator app; a passkey uses the phone or computer's fingerprint or PIN.
Milestone A block of work of 3 to 5 weeks with clear done criteria (M0 to M7, then R2).
Mock store Data kept in server memory for demos; lost on restart.
Modular monolith One application split internally into separate parts with clear rules about who talks to whom.
OpenAPI A standard file (openapi.yaml) describing every endpoint, from which typed client code is generated.
Organisation An agency, hotel or hostel business with team members.
Outbox A table where the backend writes 'send this email' or 'refresh search' in the same save as the change; workers send them afterwards, so nothing is lost.
OWASP API Top 10 The ten most common security mistakes in APIs, published by the OWASP foundation; used as a checklist.
PITR Point-in-time recovery: restoring the database to any minute in the past from continuous backups.
PostGIS The map and geography extension for PostgreSQL.
Presigned URL A temporary, signed web address that lets a browser upload or download one file directly from storage.
Property-based test A test that checks a rule on thousands of random inputs (for example: lines of a price always add up to the total).
PSP Payment service provider: a licensed company that holds and moves other people's money.
RBAC Role-based access control: rights come from a role (owner, manager, moderator...).
REST A common style of API where each address names a thing (/bookings) and the method says what to do (GET read, POST create, PATCH change, DELETE remove).
Risk score Likelihood x impact (each 1 to 5); used to sort the risk register.
Room type A kind of room or bed in a hotel or hostel, with a count of identical units.
RPO / RTO Recovery point objective (how much data we may lose, here 15 minutes) and recovery time objective (how long until service is back, here 4 hours).
SATIM The interbank company that runs card payments in Algeria.
Schemathesis A tool that reads the OpenAPI file and sends many generated requests to check the API keeps its contract.
Server action A Next.js function that runs on the server when a form is submitted.
Snapshot A copy of a value (price, rate, policy) saved on a booking so later changes do not affect it.
Soft delete Marking a row as deleted instead of removing it, so it can be restored.
State machine The allowed list of statuses and the allowed moves between them.
STRIDE A checklist of six threat kinds: spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, elevation of privilege.
Taxe de séjour Tourist tax per person per night, depending on the hotel's star rating.
Traceability matrix A table linking each requirement to its rules, tables, endpoints, tests and milestone, so nothing is forgotten.
Vertical A product family: homes, hotels, experiences, vehicles, trips.
Webhook A call that another service (for example a payment gateway) makes to our API to tell us something happened.
Wilaya / commune Algerian province / municipality. Today 69 wilayas and 1,541 communes.
Workspace (host) The host account a user is acting for right now: themselves as a solo host, or one of their organisations.

01. System inventory: what BLADUS does today

In plain words
BLADUS has two web apps and no real backend yet. Everything is kept in memory and resets when the server restarts.
This document lists what each kind of user can do, what data exists, and which functions the future Django API must replace.
It also lists the rules hidden in the code and every place where the two apps, or the original spec, disagree.
The disagreements matter most: a few of them (money model, statuses, who is a host) must be decided before any table is designed.
Raw, line-by-line notes are kept in the appendices so nothing is lost.

Date: 2026-11-04. Scope: frontend/ (guest and host website) and admin/ (back office). Method: reading the code, comparing it with the recovered spec (_sources/darna_spec.md), and clicking through the main flows on a local dev server.

Terms used in this document (all also in glossary.md):

  • Mock store: data kept in a JavaScript object in server memory (globalThis). It disappears on restart and is not shared between servers.
  • lib/data seam: the folder of functions every page calls to read or write data. It is the bridge: each function there becomes one API call later.
  • Server action: a Next.js function that runs on the server when a form or button is used. It returns ActionResult (success, or an error code).
  • Host type: individual, agency, hotel or hostel.
  • Vertical: a product family: homes, hotels, experiences, vehicles, trips.
  • Ledger: a list of money movements that is only ever added to; a balance is the sum of its lines.

1. The system at a glance

Part What it is Users Session
Website (frontend/) Next.js 14 App Router, next-intl (en, fr, ar with right-to-left), Tailwind Visitors, guests, hosts (individual and organisation teams) Signed cookie darna_session (HMAC)
Admin (admin/) Same stack, separate app Staff with 5 roles: super_admin, moderator, support, finance, analyst JWT cookie darna_admin_session, 8 hours, HS256
Backend None. Each app has its own in-memory mock store with its own seed data

The two apps do not share data. A booking made on the website never appears in the admin, and an approval in the admin never reaches the website. The Django backend will become the one shared source of truth.

5. Business rules found in the code

These rules are real today, even though no one wrote them down. The backend must keep them or change them on purpose.

5.1 Money

  1. All amounts are whole Algerian dinars (DZD) in the apps. The backend will store centimes (see 02-research.md B.10).
  2. Guests pay no platform fee. Both apps set the guest service fee to 0. BLADUS earns only the host commission. (admin/docs/DATA-MODEL.md still says 7%: stale.)
  3. Default commission by host type: individual 12%, agency 15%, hotel 18%, hostel 10%. The admin also allows a per-host override.
  4. Commission base differs: website uses the accommodation subtotal (no cleaning fee, no taxes); admin uses the base price. Spec says "booking total".
  5. The commission rate is copied onto the booking when it is created (snapshot), so later rate changes do not reprice old bookings.
  6. Website price = nights x nightly price (with per-day overrides) + cleaning fee + taxes; weekly 10% and monthly discounts exist for display.
  7. Website wallet: the host pre-pays a commission deposit; BLADUS deducts the commission on every confirmed booking and gives it back on decline or cancel. The balance may go negative; the host then sees a warning banner.
  8. Admin wallet recharge needs a receipt reference and an amount between 1 and 10,000,000 DZD. The same receipt can be credited twice (no duplicate check).
  9. Payout approval debits the wallet and refuses when the balance is too low. There is no "money actually sent" step.
  10. Refunds: partial refunds add up; a refund takes back the host share proportionally; the platform keeps its commission on refunds.

5.2 Bookings and availability

  1. Date ranges are half-open: check-in day is booked, check-out day is free. Back-to-back stays are allowed (confirmed in the click-through, O5).
  2. Overlapping stays on the same single unit are refused (O4). For hotels and hostels, the room type's inventory is counted per night; a hostel bed counts one per guest.
  3. Search keeps a listing when its availability overlaps the searched dates and shows "Available X to Y within your dates" for partial matches.
  4. Stay rules: minimum and maximum nights per listing; guest count up to capacity.
  5. Approval mode per listing: instant confirms at once; request creates a pending booking that expires after 24 hours.
  6. Website booking statuses move: pending to confirmed, declined, expired or cancelled; confirmed to completed or cancelled. Completion and expiry are applied when the data is read, not by a timer.
  7. Cancellation policies (flexible, moderate, strict) decide the refund by days before check-in.

5.3 Moderation and accounts

  1. Host lifecycle (admin): applied, under review, approved, rejected, suspended, banned, deleted (with restore). Suspending a host does not pause its listings or bookings.
  2. Listing lifecycle (admin): 8 statuses; a reason of at least 3 characters is required to reject, suspend or request changes. On the website, new listings and trips go live at once without review.
  3. Moderation waiting time and priority: hosts high after 3 days, listings after 4, documents after 3; flagged reviews and disputes always high.
  4. Organisation roles: owner, admin, manager, guide, agent. Any active member may accept or decline a booking request.
  5. Changing an organisation's legal fields should trigger re-verification.
  6. Admin login: 5 failures in 15 minutes lock for 60 seconds, per email and per IP; same error for every failure; scrypt password hashing.
  7. Admin audit log is append-only and records 53 kinds of action with actor, IP, before and after.
  8. CSV exports protect against spreadsheet formula injection and are themselves audited.

The full numbered rule lists with file and line are in Appendix A section 4 and Appendix B section 4. They are rewritten as testable rules in 04-business-rules.md (Phase 3).

7. Gaps and inconsistencies

7.1 The decisions that block the data model

These come from comparing the spec, the website and the admin (Appendix C, items D-1 to D-22). The most important:

ID Topic The conflict Why it blocks
D-16 Money model Spec section 9 and the website: host pre-pays commission, guest pays the host directly. Admin seed: BLADUS collects guest money and pays hosts out. Spec section 3 says "the moment a guest completes payment". Decides payment integration, ledger accounts, payouts and legal licensing
D-1 Who is a host Website: user plus organisations, one person can be both. Admin: one flat Host row Decides the keys for wallets, listings, commission, moderation
D-3, D-5 Commission base and override subtotal vs base vs total; override only in admin Ledger posting rules
D-9 Booking statuses two different sets of six State machine and payments
D-10 Publish requires approval? website: live at once; admin: review queue Listing status flow
D-11 Trips own table vs listing subtype; departures as strings Booking target model
D-12 Is "hotel" a vertical? yes in admin, no in spec Search filters and analytics
D-14, D-15 Onboarding 12 steps vs admin cap of 2; schemas differ; config in browser storage Config tables
D-6, D-7, D-8 Approval mode and request expiry stored in 3 places; any member may respond; expiry lazy Settings and scheduler

7.2 Mock shortcuts that will not survive production

  1. Safety against double booking and double debit relies on JavaScript running one thing at a time. A real server needs database transactions, row locks and constraints.
  2. No idempotency keys (a protection that makes a retried request harmless) on recharge, refund, payout or booking.
  3. IDs from Date.now() and Math.random(); collisions are possible.
  4. Rate limits live in process memory.
  5. Admin logout only deletes the cookie; the token stays valid until it expires.
  6. Staff are recorded by name, not ID, in the ledger, payouts, onboarding and disputes.
  7. Names, ratings and counters are copied into many rows and will drift.
  8. Expiry and completion happen only when someone reads the data.
  9. All images are two placeholder files; there is no upload, storage or virus scan.
  10. The demo password ships in the website's code.
  11. No payments, refunds as records, invoices, tax lines or payouts to banks.
  12. No review writing, no notification producers, no invitation acceptance, no organisation switcher.
  13. Three amenity vocabularies, free-text property types and cities where references are needed.
  14. Messages and broadcast in the admin need no permission.

7.3 Things that are fine and should be kept

Server-side permission checks in both apps, signed sessions, half-open date logic, commission snapshot on booking, append-only audit with before/after, CSV formula protection, generic login errors with constant-time comparison, soft delete with restore in the admin.

02. Research: what others do, which Django tools to use, and what Algeria requires

In plain words
Before designing tables we looked at how Airbnb, Booking.com, Expedia and GetYourGuide solve the same problems, and which Django tools are best today.
We also checked Algerian realities: how online payment works, SMS costs, the laws on e-commerce and personal data, maps and hosting.
Big finding: Algerian law likely requires the site to be hosted in Algeria, and collecting guest money to pay hosts may need a payment licence.
So the safest first version is "BLADUS takes only its commission", which matches what the website already does.
Every legal, tax or money point here is marked VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL. This is engineering research, not legal advice.

Research date: all sources accessed on 2026-11-04. Labels: [verified] read on an official or primary page; [secondary] press, vendor or blog; [unverified] could not confirm. Full source lists with every URL: Appendix R1 and Appendix R2.

Terms used here (also in glossary.md):

  • Exclusion constraint: a database rule that refuses two rows whose date ranges overlap for the same unit. It makes double booking impossible even if the app has a bug.
  • Idempotency key: a unique ID the client sends with a payment request; if the request is retried, the server returns the first result instead of charging twice.
  • Double-entry ledger: every money movement is written as two or more lines that add up to zero (money leaves one account and enters another), so errors are visible.
  • PSP: payment service provider, a company licensed to hold and move other people's money.
  • KYC: "know your customer", checking a host's identity and documents.
  • BFF: "backend for frontend", here the Next.js server holding the login cookie and calling Django for the browser.

A. Comparable platforms

A.1 What they publish

Platform Lesson for BLADUS Source
Airbnb Started as one big app, split into services only when hundreds of engineers needed it https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/building-services-at-airbnb-part-1-c4c1d8fa811b

Not found: Airbnb's calendar architecture, Vrbo developer docs, Airbnb's current cancellation tiers from a primary page [unverified].

A.2 One idea that covers all six products

Every bookable thing is a unit, a time shape and a capacity:

Vertical What is sold Time shape Capacity per slot
Home the whole place nights [check-in, check-out) 1
Hotel a room type (pool of N rooms) nights N per night
Hostel a bed type or dorm (pool of beds) nights beds per night
Experience an option at a start time time slot seats per slot
Vehicle a vehicle pickup to return 1
Agency trip a departure on fixed dates fixed departure seats per departure

A.3 Hard problems and our decisions

Problem Decision
Double booking Capacity 1: date range column plus exclusion constraint in PostgreSQL. Pools (rooms, beds, seats): one inventory row per unit per day or slot with a rule held + booked <= total, updated atomically inside a transaction. Holds expire by a scheduled job. Search results are re-checked inside the booking transaction.
Search at Algeria scale PostgreSQL only at first (map box, filters, availability), with a small search table per listing. An external engine only when measured slow.
Pricing Nightly prices stored per unit and date, built from rules (base, weekend, season, long stay). The server gives a quote with an ID and expiry, re-checked at booking.
Money Idempotency key on every money endpoint; append-only double-entry ledger; balances computed from entries; gateway webhooks stored raw, verified and processed once.
Cancellation Named policy templates stored as windows (hours before start, refund %); copied onto the booking at confirmation.
Fake listings and fraud Listings go through review; host KYC before any payout; rule-based flags (new account + high value, duplicate photos, phone numbers in messages) that add friction, not blanket bans.
Reviews Only after a completed booking, one per direction, 14-day window, double-blind, host can reply once.
Architecture Modular monolith: one Django project split into clear apps. Services later only if needed.

Key realities (VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL):

  1. No split payment product (no "Stripe Connect" for Algeria) was found [unverified: absence of evidence].
  2. Collecting guest money and paying it to hosts looks like a payment service. Banque d'Algérie Règlement 25-02 (April 2025) sets PSP licensing with 160 million DA minimum capital [secondary].
  3. Law 18-05 art. 27: electronic payment must go through platforms run by approved banks and Algérie Poste [verified, text read].

Payment models, from lowest to highest legal risk:

# Model Fits current website?
M1 Guest pays host directly (cash or transfer); host pre-pays commission to BLADUS; BLADUS invoices commission Yes: this is the prepaid wallet the website already has
M2 Guest pays a deposit equal to BLADUS's commission through Chargily; rest paid to host on arrival Close
M3 Professional hosts use their own gateway accounts; BLADUS creates checkouts with their keys For hotels and agencies only
M4 BLADUS collects everything and pays hosts out (Airbnb model) Needs a licensed PSP or bank partner: phase 2

Recommendation for the blueprint: design the ledger so all four models fit, launch with M1 (plus optional M2), and keep M4 behind a decision gate. This resolves disagreement D-16 in favour of the spec and the website, and makes the admin's "booking payment / host payout" flow a later phase. Decision needed from you (see 13-decisions-needed.md).

API1 object access GET /bookings/{id} of someone else Check ownership on every object; non-guessable IDs (UUIDv7)
API2 authentication OTP brute force, SMS pumping 6 digits, 5 tries, 10 min, limits per phone/IP/device; MFA for staff and hosts with payouts
API3 property access Guest sees host phone before booking; mass-assigning status or commission_rate Output fields per role; allowlist of writable fields
API4 resource use Scraping, big uploads, SMS cost Page size caps, upload limits, SMS budget alarms
API5 function access Host calling a staff refund endpoint Separate admin API, deny by default
API6 business flows Holding calendars without paying, coupon abuse, fake reviews Hold expiry, velocity limits
API7 SSRF Calendar import URL, image by URL Block private IPs, egress proxy
API8 misconfiguration Open Redis, debug on, CORS * Hardening checklist
API9 inventory Old endpoints, prod data in staging OpenAPI inventory, no prod data in staging
API10 unsafe APIs Trusting payment redirect instead of webhook Verify webhook signature, re-check status server-side

Source: https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0x11-t10/ [verified].

D.2 Fraud and abuse

  • Off-platform payment pushes (BaridiMob/CCP numbers, WhatsApp links in messages before confirmation): detect and warn.
  • Fake listings with stolen photos: perceptual hash, proof of property for the first listing, delay on first payout.
  • Duplicate accounts after a ban: phone, device and hashed NIN.
  • Account takeover via SIM swap: re-verify before payout detail changes, hold payouts 48 to 72 h after such a change.
  • Reviews only from completed bookings; watch for bursts and rings.

D.3 Data rights, backups, audit

  • Access, correction, deletion: deletion anonymises the person but keeps booking and invoice records for legal retention.
  • Append-only audit log with actor, action, object, before/after hash, IP, request ID; hash-chained for tamper evidence. KYC file views always logged.
  • Breach runbook with a 5-day ANPDP clock.

Check yourself

  • Why does an exclusion constraint matter more than a check in Python code?
  • What are the four payment models, and which one does the website already use?
  • Which Algerian law article points to hosting in Algeria, and why is it flagged "verify"?
  • Why do we store money in centimes even though prices are whole dinars?
  • Why polling before WebSockets for messages?
  • Name two fraud patterns that are specific to Algeria's payment habits.
  • How many wilayas and communes does Algeria have today, and which seed datasets will we use?

03. Requirements: what the backend must do

In plain words
This is the list of everything the Django backend must do, one line per need, each with an ID like BKG-03.
Each line says who needs it, how important it is, in which release, and how we will know it works ("accepted when").
It also says what the apps do today, so you can see the size of the gap.
The same list is in requirements.csv for spreadsheets. The rules behind the lines are in 04-business-rules.md.
The product decisions you approved on 2026-11-04 are written first, because many lines depend on them.

Terms used here (see glossary.md):

  • MoSCoW priority: Must (no launch without it), Should (important, can slip a little), Could (nice to have).
  • Release: MVP (first public launch), R2 (the next release after launch), Later (needs a legal or business decision first).
  • Acceptance criterion ("accepted when"): a sentence a tester can check with yes or no.
  • Non-functional requirement (NFR): a quality the system must have (speed, safety, backups) rather than a feature.

1. How to read the IDs

Prefix in "Source" Meaning Where to find it
R1 to R69 A requirement from the original spec _work/spec-vs-code.md section 1
D-1 to D-22 A disagreement between spec, website and admin same file, section 2
U1 to U16 A usability finding same file, section 4
O1 to O11 Something seen while clicking through 01-system-inventory.md section 6
INV-F / INV-A Website / admin inventory section Appendices A and B
RES Research section 02-research.md
DEC-001 to DEC-013 A product decision (section 2 below) here
BR-xxx A business rule 04-business-rules.md

2. Product decisions (approved 2026-11-04)

The product owner accepted the proposed defaults for all open product questions (DEC-001 to DEC-013) and later asked for two more rules, already built in the apps (DEC-014, DEC-015).

ID Question Decision Consequence for the design
DEC-001 Money model M1: prepaid commission. Guests pay the host directly (cash, transfer, or the host's own means). The host keeps a commission deposit with BLADUS, which deducts its commission on each confirmed booking. The ledger is designed so models M2 to M4 can be switched on later. No guest payment or payout in MVP; double-entry ledger with accounts ready for them
DEC-002 Commission base Accommodation subtotal: nights x nightly price (after length-of-stay discount), excluding cleaning fee and taxes. For trips and experiences: seats x price per person. One base, stored on each booking
DEC-003 Review before publishing Yes. New listings and trips go to pending_review; edits of key fields return them to review. Moderation queue drives publication
DEC-004 One person, many host roles Yes, with an active-organisation switcher. Host account = user or organisation; memberships
DEC-005 Hotel vertical Own vertical in search, rolled into the home family in analytics. vertical enum includes hotel
DEC-006 Trips Own tables with departures (dates, seats, price, status). trip, trip_departure tables
DEC-007 Individual onboarding length Keep 12 steps; drop the admin's 2-step cap. Config schema without that rule
DEC-008 Request reply window 24 hours, as a platform setting. Scheduled expiry job
DEC-009 Who may answer requests in an organisation Owner, admin, manager. Permission bookings.respond
DEC-010 When earnings count At completion (after check-out). Reporting rule
DEC-011 Cancellation policies Flexible, moderate, strict, stored as time windows. cancellation_policy table
DEC-012 Guest phone verification Required before the first booking. Phone OTP in MVP
DEC-014 What each host type may publish (2026-11-04) Individual: homes and vehicles. Agency: experiences and trips. Hotel and hostel: their property. HST-07, BR-HST-05; demo data moved accordingly
DEC-015 Experience and trip types (2026-11-04) 8 experience types and 8 trip types, one shared list used everywhere LST-12, TRP-07, BR-LST-05; enums in the schema
DEC-013 Wilaya count shown 69 (codes 59 to 69 to be confirmed against the official journal). Geography seed

Legal and accounting questions (L1 to L7, F1 to F4 in 14-open-questions.md) are still open. Every requirement that depends on them carries "VERIFY" in its source.

Check yourself

  • What is the difference between "Must / MVP" and "Should / R2"?
  • Which decision explains why there is no guest payment in the MVP?
  • Find the requirement that prevents double booking. What is its acceptance criterion?

04. Business rules

In plain words
A business rule is a sentence like "a guest cannot book nights that are already booked" or "BLADUS takes 12% from an individual host".
Each rule has an ID (BR-PAY-04), says where it is enforced (the database, the backend code, or a scheduled job) and how to test it.
Rules enforced by the database are the strongest: even a bug in the code cannot break them.
The statuses each object can have, and the allowed moves between them, are written as tables (state machines).
Money examples are worked out in full so anyone can check the arithmetic.

Terms used here (see glossary.md):

  • Enforced by DB: a constraint inside PostgreSQL (unique, check, exclusion, foreign key). Cannot be bypassed.
  • Enforced by service: a check in the Django service function that performs the action, inside a database transaction.
  • Enforced by job: a scheduled background task (Celery) that applies the rule at a given time.
  • Basis points (bp): hundredths of a percent. 12% = 1,200 bp. Used to store rates without decimals.
  • Half-open range [a, b): includes a, excludes b.

Sources: website code (Appendix A section 4), admin code (Appendix B section 4), decisions DEC-001 to DEC-013 (03-requirements.md section 2). "Today" says what the apps do now.

8. Cancellations and refunds (CAN)

Under DEC-001 the guest paid the host directly, so a "refund" is an amount the host owes the guest. BLADUS records it, shows it to both sides, and adjusts its commission. When BLADUS collects payments later (M2 to M4), the same amounts drive real refunds.

ID Rule Enforced by Today Test
BR-CAN-01 Policy templates (DEC-011); "days before" = calendar days in Algeria between today and check-in: flexible 100% if 1+ days before, 50% on arrival day; moderate 100% if 5+ days, 50% from 4 to 1 day, 0% on arrival day; strict 100% if 14+ days, 50% from 13 to 7, 0% within 6 days. Percentages apply to the accommodation subtotal; cleaning fee and its taxes are always refunded before check-in. Guests cannot cancel after check-in time on arrival day (support can). service (pure function, property tests) built (same values) table-driven tests per day
BR-CAN-02 Guest cancellation: refund = policy % x subtotal + cleaning fee + matching taxes. service built example 8a
BR-CAN-03 Host cancellation of a confirmed booking: full refund owed to the guest, full commission reversal, host cancellation counter +1; 3 in 12 months open a moderation case. service partly example 8a
BR-CAN-04 Staff refunds: amount between 1 centime and (total minus already refunded); partial refunds add up; reason required; audited. DB check refunded <= total + service admin built over-refund refused
BR-CAN-05 Disputes (R2): opened until 14 days after check-out by guest or host; resolution refund_full, refund_partial or declined; resolution note required. service admin only dispute after 15 days refused

Example 8a (Tipaza villa from the click-through, individual host, 12%):

  • 3 nights x 18,500 = 55,500 DZD subtotal; cleaning 4,000; total 59,500 DZD.
  • Commission at confirmation: 12% x 55,500 = 6,660 DZD deducted from the host's wallet.
  • Guest cancels 3 days before, moderate policy: 50% of 55,500 = 27,750 + cleaning 4,000 = 31,750 DZD owed back to the guest.
  • BLADUS keeps commission only on the part the host keeps: 12% x 27,750 = 3,330, so 3,330 DZD goes back to the wallet.
  • If the host cancels instead: the guest is owed 59,500 and all 6,660 goes back to the wallet.

9. Money, wallet and ledger (PAY)

ID Rule Enforced by Today Test
BR-PAY-01 Amounts are stored as whole centimes (BIGINT) with a currency code (DZD). Prices shown to people are whole dinars. Rates are basis points. Rounding: half up at each line; a total is always the sum of its rounded lines. DB types + Money type integer DZD property test: sum of lines == total
BR-PAY-02 Ledger: every posting is one ledger_transaction with 2+ entries; entries of a transaction sum to 0 per currency; entries are never updated or deleted (corrections are new reversing transactions). DB deferred constraint trigger + no UPDATE/DELETE grant single-sided unbalanced insert fails at commit
BR-PAY-03 Each host account has one commission wallet account in the ledger. Balance = sum of its entries (cached in a balance row updated in the same transaction). DB + service built (website) cache equals sum
BR-PAY-04 Commission = round_half_up(commission_base x rate_bp / 10,000); base per DEC-002 (subtotal after discount; trips and experiences: seats x price). Posted once per booking at confirmation (unique key booking + kind). DB unique + service built (website) confirm twice posts once
BR-PAY-05 Commission reversal: decline and expiry (nothing was posted); host cancel and staff cancel without guest fault: full; guest cancel: reverse the commission on the refunded subtotal share. service built (website) example 8a
BR-PAY-06 Rate resolution: host account override (if set) else host-type default from settings (individual 1,200 bp, agency 1,500, hotel 1,800, hostel 1,000). Changing defaults affects new bookings only. Overrides can be cleared. service two sources clearing an override returns to the default
BR-PAY-07 Manual top-up: amount 1 to 10,000,000 DZD; method in ccp_transfer, bank_transfer, baridimob, cash_office; receipt reference unique per method; top-ups over 500,000 DZD need a second finance user to approve (four-eyes). DB unique + service duplicates allowed same receipt twice fails
BR-PAY-08 Online top-up (R2): credited only from a verified gateway webhook, once per gateway event id. DB unique (provider, event_id) none replayed webhook ignored
BR-PAY-09 Changing payout or refund account details requires 2FA, notifies the old email and phone, and blocks payouts for 72 hours. service none payout during hold refused
BR-PAY-10 Credit floor: a host wallet may go below zero down to -credit_limit (setting per host type, default 20,000 DZD). Below 0: banner and admin flag. Below the floor: instant bookings become requests and the host cannot accept new requests until topped up. service banner only accept refused below floor
BR-PAY-11 Models M2 to M4 (guest payments, escrow, payouts) are switched off by a setting until legal approval; their ledger accounts exist from day one. settings admin mock endpoints return 404 when off
BR-PAY-12 Commission invoices (R2): monthly per host account, sequential numbers without gaps per year, never deleted (cancelled by a credit note). VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL. DB sequence + service none numbers continuous

BR-STF-01 Staff permissions come from the role (5 roles, matrix in Appendix B section 1.1) stored in the database; checked on every admin endpoint; deny by default. service code constants analyst refund gets 403
BR-STF-02 Audit log is insert-only (no UPDATE or DELETE grant for the app's database role); each row stores actor id, actor role, action, object type and id, before/after (personal data minimised), IP, request id, and a hash of the previous row. DB grants + trigger memory update fails
BR-STF-03 Every record of who did something stores a user id (foreign key), never a display name. DB FK names
BR-STF-04 Exports: values starting with = + - @ TAB CR are prefixed with '; need reports.export plus the view permission of the dataset; audited with filters and row count. service built formula neutralised

16. Settings and config (CFG)

ID Rule Enforced by Today Test
BR-CFG-01 Settings are one versioned record; each change creates a new version with author and time; only whitelisted keys with validated values. service shallow merge unknown key refused
BR-CFG-02 Onboarding config: one draft and many immutable published versions per host type; publishing copies the draft into the next version number for that host type. DB unique (host_type, version) global counter old version still readable
BR-CFG-03 Field types are canonical: text, textarea, number, select, multi_select, image_upload, file_upload, toggle, location, amenities. Core steps and fields cannot be removed or have their type changed. service two schemas removing a core step refused

17. Promotions (PRM), reports (RPT), privacy (PRV), system (SYS)

ID Rule Enforced by Today Test
BR-PRM-01 Coupon (R2): unique code (case-insensitive), valid dates, total and per-user limits; redemption counted when the booking is confirmed, released if cancelled before check-in. DB unique + service not used limit reached refused
BR-PRM-02 Coupon funding: BLADUS-funded reduces the commission (never below 0); host-funded reduces the subtotal. Recorded in the ledger. service n/a
BR-RPT-01 KPIs use real date windows in Africa/Algiers; gross booking value = sum of totals of confirmed and completed bookings by check-in date; revenue = net commission. service hardcoded
BR-RPT-02 Host earnings = subtotal + cleaning fee - commission - refunds owed, counted when completed (DEC-010). service shows 0
BR-PRV-01 Store the accepted terms and privacy versions with time and IP; marketing only with explicit opt-in, withdrawable any time. DB none
BR-PRV-02 Deletion request: anonymise the profile (name, contacts, photos, ID files) within 30 days; keep bookings, ledger and invoices with a pseudonymous id for the legal period. VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL. job none
BR-PRV-03 Notification preferences cannot switch off critical messages (BR-NTF-02). service none
BR-PRV-04 Personal data and its backups stay in Algerian data centres unless an ANPDP authorisation is recorded. VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL. operations n/a
BR-PRV-05 Retention: ID images deleted 90 days after the verification decision (keep the decision, document type and a hash of the number); messages 3 years after last activity; accounting 10 years. VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL. job none
BR-SYS-01 Every create or money endpoint accepts an Idempotency-Key; same key and same body returns the stored response; same key with a different body returns 422; a concurrent request with the same key returns 409. Keys kept 24 h. DB unique + service none retry returns the same booking
BR-SYS-02 Incoming webhooks are stored raw before processing, signature checked, processed once. DB unique none
BR-SYS-03 Side effects (notifications, emails, search refresh) are written to an outbox in the same transaction and sent after commit with retries and backoff. DB + job none a rolled-back change sends nothing
BR-SYS-04 API errors have a stable code, a field (if any) and a message in the requested language (en, fr, ar). service ActionResult codes
BR-SYS-05 Timestamps in UTC (timestamptz); stay dates as date in Africa/Algiers; week starts Sunday; Friday and Saturday are the weekend for pricing rules. DB types mixed

Diagrams

In plain words
Pictures of the planned system: who uses it, what runs where, how statuses change, how a booking flows step by step, and how the tables link.
Each picture has a short caption and a legend explaining its symbols.
The .mmd files are the editable sources (Mermaid text). The rendered/ folder holds SVG (sharp at any zoom) and PNG versions.
The table diagrams (erd-*) are generated from ../schema.dbml, so they always match the schema.

How to re-render: python ../_tools/build_schema_docs.py (ERD sources), then python ../_tools/render_diagrams.py (needs @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli installed in a tools folder outside the repo and a local Chrome; see the script header).

Legends

Diagram type How to read it
Flowchart (01, 02, 03, 30, 40) Boxes are systems or parts; rounded boxes are people; cylinders are data stores. A solid arrow is a call or a flow; a dotted arrow is optional, later (R2) or asynchronous. Grey frames group things that run together.
State diagram (10 to 13) Each box is a status. An arrow is an allowed move, labelled with who or what causes it. The black dot is the start; the circled dot is the end. A move not drawn is forbidden.
Sequence diagram (20 to 24) Columns are actors (people) and participants (systems). Time goes down. Solid arrows are requests, dashed arrows are replies, open arrows are messages sent later by a worker. Numbered steps match the text. alt boxes show alternative paths.
ERD (erd-*) Each box is a table with its columns (type, name, and PK = primary key, FK = link, UK = unique). A line links a table to the one it points to; the label is the linking column. `

Architecture

File Caption
01-system-context Who uses BLADUS and which outside services it talks to. Guests and hosts use the website, staff use the admin app; both call one Django API. The payment gateway is dotted because online payment comes in release R2.
02-containers What runs where. Everything holding personal data runs in Algerian data centres (research C.3, to be confirmed by a lawyer). The Next.js servers keep the login cookie and call Django on the browser's behalf (BFF). Workers send messages and run timed jobs.
03-django-apps The backend is one application split into 17 apps plus a small core, arranged in layers. An app may only use apps in lower layers (checked automatically by import-linter); for example bookings may use pricing and the ledger, never the reverse. Events (emails, search refresh) go through the outbox instead of direct calls. Details in 07-architecture.md.
30-money-flow Where money goes. At launch (M1) the guest pays the host, the host keeps a deposit at BLADUS, and BLADUS takes its commission from that deposit. M4 (BLADUS collects and pays out) is drawn for later and needs a licence.
40-document-map How the blueprint documents feed each other, from inventory to tests.

Lifecycles (state machines)

File Caption
10-booking-states Every status a booking can have. A request waits up to 24 hours for the host; a confirmed booking becomes completed automatically after check-out. awaiting_payment stays unused until online payment exists. Rules BR-BKG-01 to 07.
11-listing-states A listing or trip is checked by staff before it is published (DEC-003). Hosts can pause; staff can suspend or ask for changes. Deleting is reversible by staff.
12-host-verification-states A host (person or organisation) is approved only when all required documents are approved. Changing legal details sends it back to review.
13-review-states A review is written after a completed stay, published when both sides wrote or after 14 days, and can be hidden after a report.

Key flows (sequences)

File Caption
20-seq-instant-booking An instant booking from price quote to confirmation in one database transaction; the database itself refuses overlapping dates; the commission is posted to the host's wallet; messages go out after the save.
21-seq-request-to-book A request: the host accepts, declines, or a timed job expires it after 24 hours. Dates stay blocked while it waits.
22-seq-wallet-topup A host tops up the commission deposit by transfer; finance records it with the receipt reference; large amounts need a second person.
23-seq-host-onboarding Becoming a host: the steps come from the published configuration, the draft is saved on the server, documents go to private storage, staff verify.
24-seq-message-sync Messages are fetched with a cursor so polling is cheap; phone numbers are masked until a booking is confirmed (anti-fraud).

05. Database schema

In plain words
This is the plan for the database: which tables exist, how they link, and which rules the database itself enforces.
It has 77 tables in 14 groups. The full column list is in 05b-data-dictionary.md and the machine-readable version in schema.dbml.
The most important ideas: one "host account" for every kind of host; the database refuses double bookings; money is kept in a ledger that is never edited.
Each big choice is written as a short decision record (ADR) with the options we rejected.
At the end: how today's demo data maps onto the new tables, what to seed first, and how the busiest queries will run.

Terms used here (see glossary.md):

  • Table / row / column: a table is like a spreadsheet tab; a row is one record; a column is one field.
  • Primary key (PK): the column that identifies a row. Foreign key (FK): a column pointing to a row in another table.
  • Constraint: a rule the database checks on every write (unique, check, exclusion, foreign key).
  • Index: a lookup structure that makes searches fast, like the index at the back of a book.
  • Partial index: an index (often unique) that applies only to rows matching a condition, e.g. "only active owners".
  • GiST / GIN: PostgreSQL index types for ranges, map points, arrays and text search.
  • Migration: a versioned script that creates or changes tables. Not written yet (no backend code in this phase).

Inputs: 01-system-inventory.md, 03-requirements.md, 04-business-rules.md, research 02-research.md section B.

2. Conventions

Topic Convention Why
IDs UUIDv7 (time-ordered) made by the app; human references for people (BLD-2026-7K2M9Q, LST-...) Not guessable (BR security API1), sortable, no Date.now() collisions
Money BIGINT centimes in columns ending _minor, plus currency char(3) Exact sums (ADR-006)
Rates integer basis points _bp (1,200 = 12%) No float rounding
Time timestamptz in UTC; stay nights as date / daterange in Africa/Algiers BR-SYS-05
Names in 3 languages name_en, name_fr, name_ar columns on platform lists (django-modeltranslation) Research B.9

Soft delete deleted_at (+ status_before_delete where restore exists) Admin restore (U7)
Who did it always an FK to user.id, never a name BR-STF-03
Cached numbers ratings, counts, balances are caches recomputed by jobs; never edited by hand BR-REV-04, BR-PAY-03
Table names Django will prefix with the app (bookings_booking); this document uses short names Readability

3. Architecture decision records (ADRs)

Each ADR: the context, the decision, the options rejected, the consequences.

ADR-001: One host_account for every kind of host

  • Context: the website has users with organisations; the admin has a flat Host row; one person may host alone and also run an agency (DEC-004, disagreement D-1).
  • Decision: host_account is either one user (kind = individual) or one organisation (kind = organization). Listings, trips, wallets, commission overrides, verification and reviews point to the host account.
  • Rejected: (a) host fields on user (cannot represent organisations); (b) only organisations, with a "solo organisation" per individual (confusing for individuals, more rows, forces team concepts on solo hosts).
  • Consequences: one wallet per host account; Karim's individual hosting and his agency have separate wallets and commission rates; the API carries an "active host account" header.

ADR-002: Database-enforced availability, two mechanisms

  • Context: double booking must be impossible (AVL-01, AVL-02); today it relies on single-threaded JavaScript.
  • Decision: single units (homes, vehicles) use a daterange on booking with an exclusion constraint; pooled units (hotel room types, hostel beds, experience slots, trip departures) use counter rows (room_type_night, experience_slot, trip_departure) with CHECK (held + booked <= total) and an atomic conditional UPDATE.
  • Rejected: (a) application locks only (lost under multiple servers); (b) one row per physical room for hotels (heavier; hosts do not assign rooms at booking time); (c) Redis counters (not transactional with the booking).
  • Consequences: concurrent requests for the last unit: exactly one succeeds, the other gets 409 dates_unavailable. Counter rows are created 18 months ahead by a job.

ADR-003: One booking table with typed targets

  • Context: bookings target a listing, a room type, an experience slot or a trip departure.
  • Decision: booking has inventory_kind and four nullable target columns; a check constraint requires exactly the right ones. MVP: one room type per booking (multi-room bookings = several bookings in one checkout later).
  • Rejected: generic foreign keys (no database integrity); one table per kind (four copies of the money and status columns).
  • Consequences: every booking report reads one table.

ADR-004: Trips are their own tables (DEC-006)

  • Decision: trip, trip_itinerary_day, trip_departure. Trips share the listing_status enum and moderation flow but not the listing table.
  • Rejected: listing subtype (admin today): itinerary and departures do not fit listing columns.
  • Consequences: search runs on listings and trips separately; the website's guest "Trips" page should be renamed "My bookings" in the API (/me/bookings) to avoid the name clash (D-11).

ADR-005: Verticals

  • Decision: vertical = home, hotel, hostel, experience, vehicle (DEC-005 plus hostel split out because its unit is a bed). The search tab "Hotels" filters hotel, hostel; analytics group home, hotel, hostel as "stays".
  • Rejected: hotel as a business category of home (spec): breaks search filters and analytics (D-12).

ADR-006: Money in centimes with a double-entry ledger

  • Context: DEC-001 (prepaid commission now, maybe collected payments later); research B.17 and A.5.
  • Decision: ledger_account, ledger_transaction, ledger_entry (insert-only, sum to zero per transaction, enforced by a deferred trigger) and account_balance cache. Amounts in centimes.
  • Rejected: single-sided wallet rows (both apps today: cannot prove that money balances); DECIMAL with django-money (repository archived 2026).
  • Consequences: M2 to M4 only add accounts and transaction kinds; no schema rewrite. Corrections are reversing transactions.

ADR-007: Snapshots on the booking

  • Decision: prices, commission base, rate and amount, cancellation windows, listing title and address are copied onto the booking at creation (BR-BKG-07).
  • Rejected: read live values (old bookings would change when hosts edit).
  • Consequences: some duplication by design; editing a listing never alters a booking.

ADR-008: Statuses as PostgreSQL enums with transition checks in services

  • Decision: enum types for statuses; allowed transitions in service code with a booking_event row per change; the database rejects unknown values.
  • Rejected: transition triggers in SQL (hard to test and translate errors); free text statuses (today's three conflicting sets).
  • Consequences: adding a status is a migration (rare, deliberate).

ADR-009: Listing revisions for edits under review

  • Decision: edits to reviewed fields of a published listing go to listing_revision (JSON payload) while the live listing stays visible (BR-LST-02).
  • Rejected: unpublishing on every edit (hosts lose bookings); no review of edits (fraud path: approved listing turned into a fake one).

ADR-010: Versioned config as JSON validated by the app

  • Decision: platform_settings and onboarding_flow_version store a validated JSON document per version; old versions stay readable.
  • Rejected: one column per setting (migration per setting); key-value rows (no validation, no atomic versions).

ADR-011: Search table, PostgreSQL only

  • Decision: listing_search_doc holds one denormalised row per published listing, refreshed through the outbox; queries combine it with live availability (research B.7).
  • Rejected: external search engine at launch.

ADR-012: Audit as a hash-chained, insert-only table plus automatic row history

  • Decision: audit_event (human "who did what") with prev_hash/hash, monthly partitions, no UPDATE/DELETE grant; django-pghistory tables for automatic row history of bookings, listings, memberships, settings (research B.11).
  • Rejected: signal-based history only (misses bulk updates).

ADR-013: Geography as reference tables with provenance

  • Decision: wilaya (code PK 1 to 69), daira, commune with source and valid_from; listings store commune_id; the wilaya is derived. legacy_code_58 keeps old data mappable.
  • Rejected: free text city (today).

ADR-014: Personal data minimisation in the schema

  • Decision: document numbers stored only as HMAC hashes; payout account numbers encrypted with a key outside the database; exact listing location separate from public location; message body_masked.
  • Consequences: support cannot read raw ID numbers from the database; a key management step exists in operations (08-security-privacy.md, Phase 7).

4. The key tables in plain words

Table One sentence
user A person; may be a guest, a host, an organisation member and staff at the same time.
host_account "The one who hosts": either one person or one organisation. Owns listings, trips and a wallet.
organization / membership An agency, hotel or hostel and who works in it with which role.
listing Something to book: a home, hotel, hostel, experience or vehicle.
room_type A kind of room or bed in a hotel or hostel, with a count of identical units.
room_type_night For one room type and one night: how many units exist, are held, are booked.
listing_day For a home or vehicle: a day the host blocked or priced differently.
trip / trip_departure An agency trip and its dated departures with seats.
booking One reservation with its frozen prices, commission and policy.
booking_event Every status change of a booking, in order.
ledger_* Money movements written as balanced entries; balances are sums.
wallet_topup A host's deposit recorded by finance staff, with its receipt reference.
review A rating and comment after a completed booking.
conversation / message Message threads between guest and host.
moderation_case One item in a staff queue (a host to verify, a listing to review, a report).
audit_event A tamper-evident record of who did what.
outbox_event A message to send after a change is saved (notification, email, search refresh).

5. Booking lifecycle in the schema

  1. Guest asks for a price: a quote row (30 minutes).
  2. Guest books with an Idempotency-Key: idempotency_record locks the key.
  3. In one transaction: insert booking (status pending or confirmed), reserve inventory (exclusion constraint or counter UPDATE), insert booking_event, and if confirmed post the commission ledger_transaction (2 entries) and update account_balance; insert outbox_event rows (notify host and guest, refresh search).
  4. Commit. Workers send notifications from the outbox.
  5. Jobs later: expire pending (expired, release counters), complete after check-out (completed), open review window.

6. Constraints the database enforces (SQL sketch)

These are written as SQL for clarity; they will become Django Meta.constraints or migration operations in the build phase.

-- Extensions
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS postgis;
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist;   -- equality inside exclusion constraints
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;      -- fuzzy text search
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS unaccent;

-- BR-AVL-01: no overlapping stays on a single unit
ALTER TABLE booking ADD CONSTRAINT booking_no_overlap
  EXCLUDE USING gist (listing_id WITH =, stay WITH &&)
  WHERE (inventory_kind = 'single'
         AND status IN ('awaiting_payment','pending','confirmed','completed','disputed'));

-- ADR-003: targets match the inventory kind
ALTER TABLE booking ADD CONSTRAINT booking_target_matches_kind CHECK (
  (inventory_kind = 'single'    AND listing_id IS NOT NULL AND room_type_id IS NULL AND experience_slot_id IS NULL AND trip_departure_id IS NULL) OR
  (inventory_kind = 'room_pool' AND listing_id IS NOT NULL AND room_type_id IS NOT NULL AND experience_slot_id IS NULL AND trip_departure_id IS NULL) OR
  (inventory_kind = 'slot'      AND listing_id IS NOT NULL AND experience_slot_id IS NOT NULL AND room_type_id IS NULL AND trip_departure_id IS NULL) OR
  (inventory_kind = 'departure' AND trip_departure_id IS NOT NULL AND listing_id IS NULL AND room_type_id IS NULL AND experience_slot_id IS NULL));

ALTER TABLE booking ADD CONSTRAINT booking_money_ok CHECK (
  subtotal_minor >= 0 AND discount_minor >= 0 AND cleaning_fee_minor >= 0 AND taxes_minor >= 0
  AND total_minor = subtotal_minor - discount_minor + cleaning_fee_minor + taxes_minor
  AND refund_due_minor BETWEEN 0 AND total_minor
  AND commission_rate_bp BETWEEN 0 AND 10000 AND commission_minor >= 0
  AND NOT isempty(stay) AND lower_inc(stay) AND NOT upper_inc(stay));

-- BR-AVL-02: pooled inventory never oversold
ALTER TABLE room_type_night ADD CONSTRAINT rtn_capacity
  CHECK (held >= 0 AND booked >= 0 AND total >= 0 AND held + booked <= total);
ALTER TABLE trip_departure ADD CONSTRAINT dep_capacity
  CHECK (seats_held >= 0 AND seats_booked >= 0 AND seats_held + seats_booked <= seats_total AND ends_on >= starts_on);
ALTER TABLE experience_slot ADD CONSTRAINT slot_capacity
  CHECK (seats_held >= 0 AND seats_booked >= 0 AND seats_held + seats_booked <= seats_total AND ends_at > starts_at);

-- Reserving 2 rooms for nights [2026-12-10, 2026-12-13): one statement, all nights or nothing
UPDATE room_type_night SET booked = booked + 2
 WHERE room_type_id = :rt AND night >= '2026-12-10' AND night < '2026-12-13'
   AND held + booked + 2 <= total;
-- the service checks that the updated row count = number of nights, else rolls back (409)

-- ADR-001: host account is exactly one of user or organisation
ALTER TABLE host_account ADD CONSTRAINT host_account_one_owner CHECK (
  (kind = 'individual'   AND user_id IS NOT NULL AND organization_id IS NULL) OR
  (kind = 'organization' AND organization_id IS NOT NULL AND user_id IS NULL));

-- BR-ORG-04: exactly one active owner
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX membership_one_owner ON membership (organization_id)
  WHERE role = 'owner' AND is_active;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX membership_active_unique ON membership (organization_id, user_id) WHERE is_active;

-- BR-ACC-01
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX user_email_ci ON "user" (lower(email)) WHERE email IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX user_phone ON "user" (phone_e164) WHERE phone_e164 IS NOT NULL;

-- BR-PAY-02: balanced, insert-only ledger
CREATE FUNCTION ledger_tx_balanced() RETURNS trigger AS $$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ledger_entry WHERE transaction_id = NEW.transaction_id
             GROUP BY currency HAVING sum(amount_minor) <> 0) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'ledger transaction % is not balanced', NEW.transaction_id;
  END IF;
  RETURN NULL;
END $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER ledger_entry_balanced AFTER INSERT ON ledger_entry
  DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION ledger_tx_balanced();
ALTER TABLE ledger_entry ADD CONSTRAINT ledger_entry_nonzero CHECK (amount_minor <> 0);
REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON ledger_entry, ledger_transaction, audit_event, booking_event FROM bladus_app;

-- BR-PAY-04: commission posted once per booking
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ledger_one_commission ON ledger_transaction (booking_id) WHERE kind = 'commission';

-- BR-LST-02, BR-CFG-02, BR-MOD: one open item at a time
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX listing_one_pending_revision ON listing_revision (listing_id) WHERE status = 'pending_review';
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX flow_one_draft ON onboarding_flow_version (host_type) WHERE status = 'draft';
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX flow_one_published ON onboarding_flow_version (host_type) WHERE status = 'published';
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX case_one_open ON moderation_case (kind, subject_id) WHERE status <> 'resolved';
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX settings_one_current ON platform_settings (is_current) WHERE is_current;

Other checks (listed in each table's note in the dictionary): ratings 1 to 5, discounts 0 to 9,000 bp, min_nights <= max_nights, listing.inventory_kind consistent with vertical, favourites and photos pointing to exactly one parent.

7. Indexes and query plan for the busiest queries

Targets from NFR-01 and NFR-02. "Plan" is the expected PostgreSQL strategy; it will be confirmed with EXPLAIN ANALYZE on seeded data (20,000 listings, 1 million booking rows) in the build phase.

# Query Frequency Indexes Expected plan Target p95
Q1 Search: vertical + wilaya + guests + price + amenities + map box, page of 24 very high listing_search_doc: B-tree (vertical, wilaya_code, price_from_minor), GiST location_public, GIN amenity_ids Bitmap AND of B-tree and GIN, GiST for map box; then availability anti-join (Q2) on at most a few hundred candidates 500 ms
Q2 Availability for candidates and dates very high booking GiST from the exclusion constraint (listing_id, stay); room_type_night PK (room_type_id, night); listing_day PK NOT EXISTS probe on the exclusion index per candidate; range scan on night PK for pools inside Q1
Q3 Listing detail + calendar 90 days high PKs; room_type (listing_id); listing_photo (listing_id, sort_order) index scans 150 ms
Q4 Create booking (transaction) medium constraint indexes, idempotency_record unique row locks on counters only 600 ms
Q5 Host bookings list by host account + status + dates high booking (host_account_id, status, check_in_at) index range scan 200 ms
Q6 Guest bookings high booking (guest_id, created_at DESC) index scan 150 ms
Q7 Message sync since cursor very high (polling) message (conversation_id, id); conversation_participant (user_id) index range id > cursor 100 ms
Q8 Unread notifications very high notification (user_id, read_at, id) index only 50 ms
Q9 Moderation queue by kind, oldest first medium moderation_case (status, kind, submitted_at) index scan 200 ms
Q10 Wallet balance and last entries medium account_balance PK; ledger_entry (account_id, id DESC) PK + index scan 100 ms
Q11 Expire pending requests (job, every 5 min) job partial booking (request_expires_at) WHERE status = 'pending' index range 1 s
Q12 Complete stays (job) job partial booking (check_out_at) WHERE status = 'confirmed' index range 1 s
Q13 Outbox dispatch constant outbox_event (status, next_attempt_at) with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED index range 50 ms
Q14 Admin lists with facets (listings, hosts, bookings) medium B-tree on filter columns; counts via GROUP BY on the filtered set bitmap scans 400 ms
Q15 Commune autocomplete high GIN trigram on unaccent(name_fr), name_ar GIN 50 ms
Q16 Audit by object low audit_event (object_type, object_id, occurred_at) on monthly partitions partition pruning 300 ms

Growth estimate for capacity planning (first two years, assumption): 20,000 listings, 500,000 bookings, 5 million room_type_night rows (18 months x 10,000 room types x ~30 nights per month), 10 million messages, 20 million ledger entries. All fit comfortably on one PostgreSQL primary with 8 vCPU / 32 GB; partition audit_event and message by month when they pass 50 million rows.

05b. Data dictionary

In plain words
Every table and every column of the planned database, with what it means.
It is generated from schema.dbml, so it is always identical to the schema.
"Key" says if a column is the row's identity (PK), a link to another table (FK) or must be unique (UQ).
Money columns end in _minor (centimes). Rates end in _bp (basis points: 1,200 = 12%).
Read 05-database-schema.md first for the design and the reasons behind it.
