Check yourself

  • Which table links a host to either a user or an organisation?
  • In which column is the commission rate frozen on a booking, and in which unit?
  • Which tables are marked DORMANT, and why?
  • Where is the cursor used by message sync?

06. API design: how the apps talk to the backend

In plain words
This page explains the contract between the two Next.js apps (website and admin) and the Django backend.
The exact contract is the file openapi.yaml: 266 operations, each one linked to the requirements and rules it serves.
The browser never calls Django. The Next.js server calls Django for it, with a session token the browser never sees.
Every function the apps use today in lib/data and their server actions gets an endpoint (table in section 8), or the table says why it goes away.
Money is always in centimes, errors always have a stable code and a message in English, French or Arabic.
Guest payments and payouts are written in the contract but switched off ("dormant") until the money model changes.

Terms used here (see also glossary.md):

  • API: the list of requests one program can send to another and the answers it gets back.
  • REST: a common style of API where each thing has a web address (a URL) and you act on it with HTTP verbs: GET (read), POST (create or do an action), PUT (replace), PATCH (change part), DELETE (remove).
  • Endpoint (or operation): one verb on one URL, for example POST /api/v1/me/bookings.
  • OpenAPI: a standard file format that describes every endpoint, its inputs and outputs. Tools read it to check the API, draw documentation and generate code.
  • BFF (backend for frontend): the server part of each Next.js app. It receives the browser's requests and calls Django on its behalf.
  • Session token: a long random string that proves who you are to Django. django-allauth creates it at login; it can be cancelled at any time.
  • Idempotency key: a random value the app sends with a "create" request. If the same request arrives twice (double click, network retry), Django does the work once and returns the same answer.
  • Cursor: a bookmark returned with a page of results; you send it back to get the next page. Used for feeds that grow (messages, notifications).
  • ETag: a version label of a response. The app sends it back to ask "has this changed?" or "save only if nobody changed it meanwhile".
  • Webhook: a request that another company's server (a payment gateway) sends to us when something happens.
  • Dormant endpoint: present in the contract, but returns 404 until a feature flag is switched on (x-dormant: true).

1. The contract file

Item Value
File openapi.yaml, OpenAPI 3.1.0
Size 266 operations on 220 paths, 38 tags in 7 groups
Groups auth 15, public 22, me (guest) 26, shared (messaging 7, media 4), host 72, admin 119, webhooks 1
Dormant (money models M2 to M4) 8: createGuestPayment, listHostPayouts, requestHostPayout, receiveGatewayWebhook, adminListPayouts, adminApprovePayout, adminRejectPayout, adminMarkPayoutSent
Lint npx @redocly/cli lint openapi.yaml (recommended rules): valid, 0 errors, 0 warnings
Enums Copied from schema.dbml by name and value (each carries x-db-enum)

Every operation has: operationId, summary, tags, security, error responses, and these extensions:

Extension Meaning
x-requirements Requirement IDs from 03-requirements.md
x-rules Rule IDs from 04-business-rules.md
x-release MVP, R2 or Later
x-dormant true for the switched-off money endpoints
x-host-permission Organisation permission needed (host endpoints, table in section 4.4)
x-staff-permission Staff permission needed (admin endpoints, section 4.5)

When Django is built, drf-spectacular generates the real file from the code. CI then compares it with this one (see section 10): this file is the target, not decoration.

Requirements not cited by any operation are the ones with no endpoint of their own: jobs and quality targets (AVL-05 holds, BKG-04 completion job, NTF-02 email/SMS, NTF-04 outbox, NFR-01 to NFR-10 and NFR-13, PRV-03 to PRV-05), plus two features not designed yet: MSG-06 staff broadcast (R2) and PRV-06 foreign guest declaration (R2). They are covered by the conventions below or left for a later phase.

2. Big picture

Browser ──(cookie)──> Next.js website server (BFF) ──(X-Session-Token)──> Django /api/v1/*
Browser ──(cookie)──> Next.js admin server (BFF)   ──(X-Session-Token)──> Django /api/v1/admin/*
Payment gateway ───────────────(signature header)─────────────────────────> Django /api/v1/webhooks/*
  • Django is never exposed to browsers for app traffic. The public listing pages are rendered by Next.js, which calls the public endpoints.
  • Images and documents are the exception: the browser uploads them straight to object storage with a presigned URL (section 3.10), so big files never go through Next.js or Django.

3. Conventions

3.1 URLs and naming

  • Base path /api/v1. Production host https://api.bladus.dz.
  • Nouns in plural, lowercase, words separated by - (/room-types). Path ids in {snake_case}.
  • Groups by who is acting: /api/v1/... public, /api/v1/me/... the signed-in person, /api/v1/host/... the active host account, /api/v1/admin/... staff.
  • Actions that are not plain edits use a verb sub-path with POST: /host/bookings/{id}/accept, /admin/hosts/{id}/suspend. One action, one permission, one audit row.
  • Status changes with many targets use POST .../status with the target status in the body.

3.2 JSON

  • Field names in snake_case, both ways.
  • Missing optional values are null, not left out, in responses.
  • Text written by users comes back in its original language with source_language. Platform labels (amenities, types, wilayas) come in the language asked by Accept-Language; labels gives all three when needed.

3.3 Dates and times

  • Timestamps: ISO 8601 in UTC with Z (2026-11-09T09:30:00Z).
  • Stay dates: plain dates (2026-12-18) meaning the day in Africa/Algiers. Ranges are half-open: check_out is the day you leave, it is not a night of the stay.
  • The week starts on Sunday; Friday and Saturday are the weekend (BR-SYS-05). Digits are always Latin (0 to 9), also in Arabic.

3.4 Money

  • Always the Money object: {"amount_minor": 1850000, "currency": "DZD"} = 18,500 DZD. amount_minor is an integer number of centimes (1 DZD = 100 centimes). Never a float.
  • Inputs use MoneyInput (positive amount). Rates are basis points (1200 = 12%).
  • Query filters on prices say their unit in the name: min_price_minor.
  • Totals are sums of rounded lines (half up), so the apps never recompute prices: they show what the quote says (BR-PAY-01, BR-PRC-01).

3.5 Identifiers

  • Every id is a UUIDv7 (time-ordered, not guessable).
  • People also see short references: bookings BLD-2026-7K2M9Q, listings LST-7K2M9Q, trips TRP-.... Endpoints that show one item accept either the UUID or the reference in the path (booking_id, listing_id, trip_id).
  • Messages and notifications use growing integer ids, because they are also the sync cursor.

3.6 Pagination

Kind Used by Query Response
Cursor feeds and website lists: search, reviews, notifications, favourites, my bookings, host lists, wallet entries cursor, limit (1 to 50, default 20) results, next_cursor (null at the end), has_more
Page numbers admin tables (need "page 4 of 12") page, page_size (1 to 100, default 20) results, meta {page, page_size, total_count, total_pages}, often facets

Cursors are opaque strings: the apps must not build or read them.

3.7 Errors

All errors use application/problem+json, in the RFC 9457 "Problem Details" style:

{
  "type": "https://api.bladus.dz/errors/dates_unavailable",
  "title": "Dates unavailable",
  "status": 409,
  "code": "dates_unavailable",
  "detail": "Another booking took 2026-12-19 while you were booking.",
  "message": "Ces dates viennent d'être réservées. Choisissez d'autres dates.",
  "instance": "/api/v1/me/bookings",
  "request_id": "01933c10-77aa-7d00-9a51-5b2b0b6f3a10",
  "errors": []
}
  • code never changes once published. The apps map it to their own text when they want (the website's ActionResult codes become these codes, NFR-13).
  • message is ready to show, in the language of Accept-Language (en, fr, ar; default fr), BR-SYS-04.
  • errors lists field problems on 422: {"field": "room_types.0.unit_count", "code": "out_of_range", "message": "...", "params": {"min": 1}}.
  • Some codes add members: price_changed adds the new quote; permission_denied adds required_permission; night_booked adds dates.

Status codes used

Status When Example codes
400 Malformed request; also all login failures (same answer every time) bad_request, invalid_credentials, invalid_code, invalid_current_password
401 No valid session not_authenticated
403 Signed in but not allowed permission_denied, mfa_required, phone_verification_required, host_offer_not_allowed, agency_not_verified, cannot_book_own_listing, four_eyes_same_user, invitation_contact_mismatch, account_suspended
404 Not found, not yours, or a dormant feature switched off not_found, feature_disabled, not_an_organization
409 Conflict with the current state dates_unavailable, not_enough_units, seats_unavailable, price_changed, quote_expired, booking_not_pending, request_expired, booking_not_cancellable, refund_changed, wallet_below_credit_floor, invalid_transition, receipt_already_used, topup_not_pending, idempotency_in_progress, email_taken, phone_taken, already_member, invitation_pending, invitation_used, cannot_remove_owner, review_exists, already_reported, reply_locked, inventory_in_use, night_booked, slug_taken, in_use, has_future_bookings, case_resolved, last_super_admin
412 If-Match is stale stale_version
422 Validation failed validation_failed (with errors), idempotency_key_reused, listing_incomplete, documents_missing, documents_not_approved, reason_required, refund_exceeds_total, review_window_closed, dispute_window_closed, invitation_expired, unknown_field, unknown_setting, core_step_removed, preference_locked, min_nights, max_nights, advance_notice, capacity_exceeded, file_type_not_allowed, file_too_large
429 Rate limit rate_limited, login_locked (with Retry-After)

A host who asks for another host account's data gets 404, not 403, so ids cannot be probed (BR-ORG-01).

3.8 Filtering and sorting

  • Filters are plain query parameters named like the field (status, vertical, wilaya). Lists of values are comma-separated: ?vertical=home,hotel.
  • Free text is always q.
  • Sorting is ordering, with - for descending: ?ordering=-created. Only the values listed in the contract are accepted.
  • Facets: the admin list endpoints return facets with counts per value; public search has its own GET /listings/facets. A facet is counted without its own filter, so the user sees what they would get by changing it (BR-SRC-01).

3.9 Rate limits (per group)

Counters live in Redis, shared by all servers (ACC-07, NFR-11). Because all website traffic comes from the BFF, the BFF sends the real client IP in X-Forwarded-For; Django trusts that header only from the BFF's private network address.

Group Limit (proposal, tune after launch) Key
Login failures 5 in 15 min, then 60 s lock account and IP
One-time codes 3 sends per phone per hour, 10 per IP per hour; 5 tries per code phone, IP
Signup, password reset 10 per IP per hour IP
Public reads (search, pages) 120 per minute; search and map 60 per minute IP
Quotes 60 per minute user or IP
Booking create 10 per minute, 50 per day user
Messages 30 per minute; new conversations 20 per day user
Uploads 120 per hour user
Other user and host writes 120 per minute user
Admin 600 per minute; exports 10 per hour staff user

Responses over the limit are 429 with Retry-After. SMS sends also have a daily budget alarm.

3.10 Uploads

  1. POST /media/uploads with purpose, type, size, hash: returns media_id and a presigned URL (valid 10 minutes).
  2. The browser PUTs the file straight to storage (quarantine area).
  3. POST /media/{media_id}/complete: checks start (type sniffing, virus scan for documents, metadata removal, renditions, duplicate detection).
  4. The app polls GET /media/{media_id} until ready (or rejected with a code), then uses the media_id in a listing, room type, document or avatar. Private documents are only read through GET .../url, which returns a 5-minute link and writes an audit row (BR-MED-02).

3.11 Caching and ETags

Endpoint Caching
GET /reference, /geo/*, /onboarding-flows/{host_type}, /reference/reasons Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600, ETag; If-None-Match gives 304. Next.js caches them and revalidates by tag.
GET /listings/{id}, /trips/{id}, /organizations/{slug} ETag; public when anonymous, private when the session adds personal fields
Search, facets, map Short public cache (60 s) only for anonymous requests without dates
Everything under /me, /host, /admin Cache-Control: no-store

Optimistic locking: edits where two people may work at once (listing, trip, organisation, settings, onboarding flow draft, commission rates) need If-Match with the ETag of the last read. If someone saved in between, the answer is 412 and the app reloads.

3.12 Other headers

Header Direction Use
X-Session-Token BFF to Django Who is calling
X-Host-Account BFF to Django Active host account (section 4.3)
Accept-Language BFF to Django en, fr, ar
Idempotency-Key BFF to Django Section 5
X-Request-Id both Correlation id; created by the BFF, echoed in logs and errors (NFR-09)
Idempotency-Replayed: true Django to BFF The response is a stored replay
Deprecation, Sunset Django to BFF Section 9

4. Authentication and permissions

4.1 Website users (BFF cookie plus allauth session token)

  1. The login form posts to a Next.js route handler (today app/api/auth/login/route.ts).
  2. The handler calls POST /api/v1/auth/login (or the phone code flow POST /auth/code/request then POST /auth/code/confirm).
  3. Django (django-allauth headless, "app" client) answers with a session token. The handler stores it in an encrypted, httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookie. JavaScript in the browser cannot read it.
  4. On every server render or server action, the BFF decrypts the cookie and sends X-Session-Token to Django.
  5. Logout calls DELETE /api/v1/auth/session (the token dies at once on the server, BR-ACC-03) and deletes the cookie.

If allauth answers with a pending step (verify_phone, mfa_authenticate), the BFF shows that step. Sessions last 30 days, sliding. A password change revokes all other sessions. The website keeps its CSRF guard on its own route handlers and server actions (same-origin check); Django itself only receives server-to-server calls with a header token, so it needs no CSRF cookie.

4.2 Staff (admin BFF, mandatory second factor)

  • The admin app uses a separate, staff-only allauth mount at /api/v1/admin/auth/*. Non-staff accounts get the same invalid_credentials as a bad password.
  • Login is always two steps: password, then TOTP or passkey (POST /admin/auth/2fa/authenticate). A staff member without a second factor can only enrol it; every other admin endpoint answers 403 mfa_required (BR-ACC-04).
  • Sessions: 8 hours absolute, 30 minutes idle (settings). Cookie SameSite=Strict.
  • /api/v1/admin/* refuses website tokens, and host and guest endpoints refuse staff tokens (STF-05). A staff member who is also a host uses two separate sign-ins.
  • Deactivating a staff member or changing their role takes effect on the next request: permissions are read from the database every time.

4.3 The active host account

A host account is either one user (individual host) or one organisation (agency, hotel, hostel). One person can hold several (DEC-004).

  1. GET /me/workspaces lists the host accounts the user can act for, with role, permissions, allowed verticals.
  2. The workspace switcher calls PUT /me/workspaces/active {host_account_id}. Django stores it in the session. This replaces switchWorkspaceAction.
  3. Every /host/* request acts for the account in the X-Host-Account header if present, else the one in the session.
  4. On every request Django checks that the user owns that individual account or has an active membership in that organisation. If not: 404. Then it checks the role permission for the endpoint (403 permission_denied if missing).
  5. All lists are filtered by that host account in the query itself, never after loading (BR-ORG-01).

The header lets two browser tabs work on two organisations at once without fighting over the session value.

4.4 Host permissions (organisation roles, BR-ORG-05, DEC-009)

Permission owner admin manager agent guide
org.edit, members.manage X X
org.delete, transfer ownership, payout_details.edit X
listings.manage, trips.manage, calendar.manage X X X
bookings.view X X X X X (own departures)
bookings.respond (accept, decline) X X X
bookings.cancel_as_host X X
messages.reply X X X X X
wallet.view, invoices.view X X

An individual host has every permission on their own host account. Agents and guides get commission: null in bookings (they never see money). The offer rule (DEC-014) comes on top of permissions: individual = home, vehicle; agency = experience and trips; hotel = hotel; hostel = hostel. A forbidden vertical gives 403 host_offer_not_allowed.

4.5 Staff permissions

The 34 permissions and 5 roles of the admin app (matrix in _work/admin-inventory.md section 1.1) move into the staff_role_permission table and are checked on every admin endpoint, deny by default (BR-STF-01). Each admin operation names its permission in x-staff-permission. This contract adds three permissions that the admin app does not have yet:

New permission Why Proposed roles
reports.view Dashboard KPIs and charts were open to any staff (no check) all 5 roles
ledger.adjust Ledger corrections did not exist super_admin, finance
privacy.handle_requests Data protection requests (PRV-02) super_admin, support

5. Idempotency and concurrency

5.1 Idempotency keys (BR-SYS-01)

Required on: booking create, onboarding submit, listing and trip create, staff refunds, manual top-ups, ledger adjustments, departure cancel, online top-up and the dormant payment endpoints. Optional (recommended) on accept, decline, cancel, top-up approval and moderation decisions.

Situation Answer
First call with key K Normal processing; response stored 24 h with the hash of the body
Same K, same body, first call finished Stored response, same status, header Idempotency-Replayed: true
Same K while the first call still runs 409 idempotency_in_progress (retry after a moment)
Same K, different body 422 idempotency_key_reused

The BFF creates the key when the user opens the confirm step (not when they click), so a double click or a network retry sends the same key. Keys are per user and per endpoint (idempotency_record table).

5.2 The booking race

Two guests press "Book" for the same nights at the same second:

  1. Both requests open a database transaction and re-price their quote.
  2. Single units (homes, vehicles): both try to insert a booking. The exclusion constraint on (listing, stay) lets exactly one succeed; the other gets an error from PostgreSQL that Django turns into 409 dates_unavailable (BR-AVL-01).
  3. Pooled units (rooms, beds, slots, seats): each request runs one UPDATE ... SET held/booked = booked + n WHERE booked + held + n <= total per night. The loser updates 0 rows and gets 409 not_enough_units or seats_unavailable (BR-AVL-02, BR-TRP-02).
  4. The winner gets 201. The loser's app shows the message and reloads availability.

No application lock is needed; the database is the referee.

5.3 Other 409 cases

  • Status moves that are not allowed by the state machines: invalid_transition (listings, trips, hosts, reviews, top-ups).
  • Host accepts a request that expired a second ago: request_expired. Host accepts while the wallet is below the credit floor: wallet_below_credit_floor (BR-PAY-10).
  • Quote no longer valid at booking: price_changed (with the new quote) or quote_expired.
  • Duplicates: receipt_already_used (same receipt and method), email_taken, review_exists, slug_taken.
  • Shrinking inventory under existing bookings: inventory_in_use, night_booked.

6. Webhooks (dormant)

POST /api/v1/webhooks/gateway/{provider} receives gateway callbacks (Chargily first). It is dormant: it returns 404 until online top-up (R2, PAY-06) or guest payments (M2 to M4) are switched on.

When active (BR-SYS-02, BR-PAY-08):

  1. Store the raw body and headers in gateway_event first.
  2. Check the signature (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the provider secret, header signature), mark signature_valid.
  3. Deduplicate by (provider, event_id) (database unique key). A replay answers 200 {"received": true, "duplicate": true} and does nothing.
  4. Answer 200 within a second; a Celery worker processes the event once (credit the wallet, mark the top-up).
  5. Never trust the amount in the browser return URL; only the verified webhook credits money.

BLADUS does not send outgoing webhooks to partners in this version.

7. How the Next.js apps consume the API

Note: both apps run a Next.js version with breaking changes. Before writing the client code, read the guides in node_modules/next/dist/docs/ of each app, as frontend/AGENTS.md asks.

  1. Types: openapi-typescript openapi.yaml -o lib/api/schema.d.ts in each app (a script in package.json, run in CI). No hand-written API types.
  2. Client: one server-only module lib/api/client.ts per app with openapi-fetch's createClient<paths>(). A middleware adds X-Session-Token (from the cookie), Accept-Language, X-Request-Id, X-Host-Account (website host pages) and turns problem+json into the existing ActionResult error codes.
  3. lib/data keeps its function names: each body becomes one typed call, for example getListings(params) becomes client.GET("/api/v1/listings", { params: { query } }). Pages do not change (this was the point of the lib/data layer).
  4. Server actions stay as thin wrappers: session check, call, revalidatePath/revalidateTag. Business checks move to Django; the action no longer decides anything about money or availability.
  5. Route handlers stay only where the browser must call the BFF directly: login, logout, register, and a small proxy for message sync polling (/api/messages/sync) and upload tickets. They forward to Django and never expose the token.
  6. Mock store: lib/data/_store.ts and the seeds stay behind a flag for demos and tests; a BLADUS_API_MODE=mock|live switch picks the implementation per module, so modules can move one at a time.
  7. Contract tests: schemathesis runs against Django with this file; the apps' unit tests use MSW handlers generated from the examples.

listPromotions, createPromotion, togglePromotionStatus, deletePromotion GET / POST /admin/coupons, PATCH /admin/coupons/{coupon_id}, DELETE (R2)
unwrap (lib/actions/result.ts), DomainError, ValidationError (lib/data/errors.ts) Stay in the admin app; they now wrap Problem responses

8.18 New endpoints with no caller today

These serve requirements the apps do not implement yet: second-factor enrolment, email and phone verification, password reset, consents, data requests, notification preferences (R2), media uploads, host documents and verification submission, change requests, payout accounts, room-type and slot management, departures, review writing, replies and reports, disputes (R2), host earnings, invoices (R2), online top-up (R2), reference lists and reason codes, moderation cases and bulk decisions (R2), staff MFA reset. Each is in openapi.yaml with its requirement IDs.

8.19 Gaps found while mapping

  • The website profile edits bio, address and languages (updateProfileAction), but schema.dbml has no such columns on user. PATCH /me leaves them out. Decide: add columns or drop the fields (proposed question for 14-open-questions.md).
  • Trips are addressed by slug in the website today; the schema has only a reference. Old slugs need a redirect table or are dropped.
  • addOrganizationMember added members directly; the new flow always goes through an invitation the person accepts.

9. Versioning and deprecation

  • The major version is in the path (/api/v1). The info.version of the file follows semantic versioning (1.0.0-draft.1 today).
  • Allowed without a new major version: new endpoints, new optional request fields, new response fields, new enum values in responses that the apps already treat as "unknown" (the apps must not crash on an unknown value).
  • Breaking (needs /api/v2 for the affected endpoints): removing or renaming a field or endpoint, changing a type or unit, making an optional input required, changing an error code, changing pagination style.
  • A deprecated endpoint answers with Deprecation: true and Sunset: <date> headers (RFC 9745 and RFC 8594) and is marked deprecated: true in the file. Both apps are ours, so the notice is at least one release (minimum 30 days) before removal; any future partner API needs 6 months.
  • CI runs oasdiff breaking between the main-branch file and the pull request; a breaking change fails the build unless the version changes.

10. Worked examples

All examples use the Tipaza villa of example 8a in 04-business-rules.md: 3 nights x 18,500 DZD, cleaning 4,000 DZD, individual host at 12%. Money is in centimes. The same examples are embedded in openapi.yaml.

10.2 Quote, then booking

POST /api/v1/quotes
Content-Type: application/json

{"listing_id": "01933b80-1111-7aaa-8bbb-000000000001", "check_in": "2026-12-18", "check_out": "2026-12-21",
 "guests_adults": 4, "guests_children": 1, "units": 1}

Response 201 (shortened: three night lines of 1,850,000 and one cleaning_fee line of 400,000):

{
  "id": "01933c0f-aaaa-7bbb-8ccc-00000000a001",
  "expires_at": "2026-11-09T10:00:00Z",
  "nights": 3,
  "subtotal": {"amount_minor": 5550000, "currency": "DZD"},
  "discount": {"amount_minor": 0, "currency": "DZD"},
  "cleaning_fee": {"amount_minor": 400000, "currency": "DZD"},
  "taxes": {"amount_minor": 0, "currency": "DZD"},
  "total": {"amount_minor": 5950000, "currency": "DZD"},
  "platform_fee": {"amount_minor": 0, "currency": "DZD"},
  "approval_mode": "request",
  "cancellation_policy": {"code": "moderate", "version": 1, "label": "Modérée", "windows": [
    {"min_days_before": 5, "refund_bp": 10000}, {"min_days_before": 1, "refund_bp": 5000}, {"min_days_before": 0, "refund_bp": 0}]}
}

The guest confirms (phone already verified, DEC-012):

POST /api/v1/me/bookings
Idempotency-Key: 6f1d2c0e-5a7b-4c1e-9d3a-2b8f0e7c4a11
Content-Type: application/json

{"quote_id": "01933c0f-aaaa-7bbb-8ccc-00000000a001", "guest_message": "We arrive around 16:00 with a baby.", "terms_version": "2026-10"}

Response 201: a GuestBooking with reference: "BLD-2026-7K2M9Q", status: "pending" (request mode), request_expires_at 24 hours later (DEC-008), total 5,950,000, address_line: null (hidden until confirmed), payment_status: "not_collected" (model M1). If the guest clicks twice, the second call returns the same body with Idempotency-Replayed: true. If someone else took the nights first: 409 dates_unavailable.

10.3 Host accepts the request

POST /api/v1/host/bookings/BLD-2026-7K2M9Q/accept
X-Host-Account: 01933b7e-8a10-7c3e-9f00-1a2b3c4d5e01
Idempotency-Key: 0b9e4f7a-3c2d-4e11-8a6b-7d5c9e1f2a33
Content-Type: application/json

{"message_to_guest": "Welcome! The key box code will be sent the day before."}

Response 200 (extract):

{
  "reference": "BLD-2026-7K2M9Q",
  "status": "confirmed",
  "confirmed_at": "2026-11-09T11:02:00Z",
  "guest": {"id": "01933a00-0000-7000-8000-0000000a0001", "display_name": "Yacine M.", "avatar_url": null},
  "guest_phone_e164": "+213555123456",
  "commission": {"rate_bp": 1200,
                 "base": {"amount_minor": 5550000, "currency": "DZD"},
                 "amount": {"amount_minor": 666000, "currency": "DZD"},
                 "reversed": {"amount_minor": 0, "currency": "DZD"}},
  "allowed_actions": ["cancel", "message"]
}

In the same transaction Django posts the ledger transaction "debit host_wallet 6,660 DZD, credit commission revenue 6,660 DZD" (example 9a), writes the outbox events (notification, SMS to the guest) and the message. An agent or guide would get 403 permission_denied with required_permission: "bookings.respond". A host whose wallet is below the credit floor gets 409 wallet_below_credit_floor.

10.4 Wallet top-up with four-eyes approval

Finance user Samira records a CCP transfer of 600,000 DZD for Atlas Escapes (above the 500,000 DZD threshold):

POST /api/v1/admin/wallets/01933b7e-8a10-7c3e-9f00-1a2b3c4d5e02/topups
Idempotency-Key: 9a7c1e22-4b6f-4d0a-8e3c-1f2d3b4c5d66

{"amount": {"amount_minor": 60000000, "currency": "DZD"}, "method": "ccp_transfer",
 "receipt_reference": "CCP-0012345-2026-11-08", "note": "Transfer seen on CCP statement 08/11"}

Response 201: status: "pending_approval", needs_second_approval: true, nothing posted to the ledger yet. Using the same receipt again gives 409 receipt_already_used.

A second finance user, Nadir, approves:

POST /api/v1/admin/topups/01933d00-0000-7000-8000-0000000e0001/approve
Idempotency-Key: 2c4e6a80-1b3d-4f5a-9c7e-0d2f4a6b8c99
{
  "id": "01933d00-0000-7000-8000-0000000e0001",
  "status": "approved",
  "amount": {"amount_minor": 60000000, "currency": "DZD"},
  "requested_by": {"id": "01933a00-0000-7000-8000-0000000d0001", "display_name": "Samira (finance)"},
  "approved_by": {"id": "01933a00-0000-7000-8000-0000000d0002", "display_name": "Nadir (finance)"},
  "ledger_transaction_id": "01933d00-0000-7000-8000-0000000f0001",
  "needs_second_approval": true,
  "wallet_balance_after": {"amount_minor": 61240000, "currency": "DZD"}
}

If Samira tried to approve her own top-up: 403 four_eyes_same_user. Both actions are in the audit log with ids, not names (BR-STF-03).

10.5 Message sync (polling)

The guest's messages page first calls GET /api/v1/conversations/sync (no cursor) and gets the current cursor. Then, every poll_after_ms:

GET /api/v1/conversations/sync?after=m90398&as=guest
{
  "conversations": [{"id": "01933c10-0000-7000-8000-00000000c001", "kind": "booking", "my_role": "guest",
                     "unread_count": 1, "last_read_message_id": 90398, "muted": false,
                     "subject": {"booking_reference": "BLD-2026-7K2M9Q", "title": "Villa with sea view in Tipaza"},
                     "other_party": {"id": "01933a00-0000-7000-8000-0000000a0009", "display_name": "Karim B.", "avatar_url": null}}],
  "messages": [{"id": 90412, "conversation_id": "01933c10-0000-7000-8000-00000000c001", "sender_role": "host_member",
                "kind": "text", "body": "Welcome! The key box code will be sent the day before.",
                "is_masked": false, "created_at": "2026-11-09T11:02:05Z"}],
  "unread_total": 1,
  "next_cursor": "m90412",
  "has_more": false,
  "poll_after_ms": 10000
}

When nothing changed, conversations and messages are empty and the cursor stays the same. When the guest opens the thread, the app calls POST /conversations/{id}/read {"last_read_message_id": 90412}. Before a booking is confirmed, a phone number in a message arrives as "0555 ** ** **" with is_masked: true (BR-MSG-01). Later, Centrifugo can push the same events without changing this endpoint.

Check yourself

  • Why does the browser never hold the Django session token, and where is it kept instead?
  • A user is a member of two organisations. How does Django know which one a host request is for, and what happens if the id is not theirs?
  • Write the Money object for 12,500 DZD.
  • Two guests book the last room at the same moment. Which part of the system decides who wins, and what does the loser receive?
  • What happens when the same Idempotency-Key is sent twice with the same body? And with a different body?
  • Which website function has no endpoint any more because being a host is now a host account, and which endpoint replaces it?
  • Why is the gateway webhook marked x-dormant, and what does it answer today?
  • Which change to the API would force a /api/v2: adding a response field, or renaming one?

07. Architecture: how the Django backend is organised

In plain words
The backend is one Django application split into 17 small parts ("apps"), each owning its own tables and rules.
Parts may only call parts below them, so a change in bookings can never break accounts by accident.
Every write goes through a "service" function inside a database transaction; side effects (SMS, emails, search refresh) are queued in an "outbox" and sent after the save.
The two Next.js apps never talk to Django from the browser: their own server keeps the login cookie and calls the API (BFF).
We will move the apps from demo data to the real API one module at a time, each behind a switch, so we can always go back.
This page also lists every background job, the caching and search plan, the photo upload pipeline, and the future repository layout.

Terms used here (see also glossary.md):

  • App (Django app): a folder inside the Django project with its own models (tables), logic and API views. Here one app = one business area ("bounded context").
  • Modular monolith: one program, one database, deployed as one unit, but split inside into apps with strict rules about who may call whom.
  • Service: a Python function that changes data (create a booking, approve a host). It runs the checks and the transaction.
  • Selector: a Python function that only reads data (list my bookings). It never changes anything.
  • Transaction: a group of database changes that all succeed together or are all cancelled together.
  • Row lock (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE): while one transaction works on a row, others that want to change the same row wait.
  • Deadlock: two transactions each wait for a row the other has locked. PostgreSQL stops one of them. A fixed lock order prevents it.
  • Outbox: a table where a service writes "things to do after saving" in the same transaction; a worker reads it and does them.
  • Celery worker / Celery beat: a worker runs background jobs; beat is the clock that starts scheduled jobs.
  • Queue: a waiting line of jobs inside Redis. Different queues let slow jobs (images) not delay urgent ones (codes by SMS).
  • Cache: a fast copy of data kept in Redis memory to avoid asking the database again.
  • Presigned URL: a web address, valid a few minutes, that lets the browser upload or download one file directly to storage without seeing our keys.
  • BFF (backend for frontend): the Next.js server keeps the login cookie and calls Django for the browser.
  • Typed client: TypeScript code generated from openapi.yaml, so the apps cannot call an endpoint with the wrong fields without a compile error.
  • Feature flag: a setting that turns one part on or off without a new deployment.
  • import-linter: a tool that fails the build if one app imports code it is not allowed to import.

Inputs: 02-research.md (section B), 03-requirements.md, 04-business-rules.md, 05-database-schema.md (ADR-001 to ADR-014), schema.dbml, diagrams 01-system-context, 02-containers, 03-django-apps.

1. The big picture

2.1 Allowed dependencies

Apps are placed in layers. An app may import only the public functions (services.py, selectors.py) of apps in a lower layer, or of an earlier app in the same layer as listed. Model foreign keys follow the same direction, with one exception: every app may hold a foreign key to accounts.User (the shared identity) and to hosts.HostAccount, because "who did it" and "for which host" are everywhere.

Layer Apps (in order) May import from
L0 kernel core nothing inside the project
L1 platform geo, config, audit, media, notifications core
L2 identity accounts, then hosts L0, L1; hosts may import accounts
L3 offer catalog, then inventory, then trips L0 to L2; inventory may import catalog; trips may import catalog (shared policies, statuses)
L4 commerce pricing, then ledger, then bookings L0 to L3; bookings may import pricing and ledger
L5 after booking reviews, messaging L0 to L4
L6 oversight and read models trust, search L0 to L5

How lower apps learn about higher events without importing them: through outbox topics. For example bookings writes booking.confirmed; notifications (L1) dispatches it to handlers that higher apps registered in their apps.py (search refreshes availability, reviews schedules the review window). The handler code lives in the higher app; the dispatcher only knows topic names.

The rule is checked in CI by import-linter with one "layers" contract and one "independence" contract per layer (for example reviews and messaging may not import each other). A violation fails the build.

2.2 Inside one app (services and selectors pattern)

Each app has the same files (HackSoft Django styleguide, research B.2 and B.15):

File Contains Rules
models.py Tables, Meta.constraints, enums No business logic beyond clean() for single-field format checks
services.py Every write: booking_create(...), host_approve(...) Keyword-only arguments; opens the transaction; checks permissions passed in by the API layer; raises DomainError(code, field, params); writes booking_event / audit_event / outbox_event
selectors.py Every read used by APIs and other apps Always scoped by the caller (bookings_for_guest(user), bookings_for_host(host_account)); returns querysets or plain data; no writes
apis.py DRF views, one class per endpoint, with its input and output serializers inside Thin: parse input, call one service or selector, serialize output. Never Model.objects.create here
permissions.py django-rules predicates (is_member_with(perm), is_staff_with(perm)) Deny by default
events.py Outbox topic names this app emits, handlers it registers Handlers are idempotent
tasks.py Celery tasks Thin: load ids, call a service. No logic in the task itself, so moving to Django's built-in tasks later is easy (research B.5)
admin.py Django admin console registrations Read-mostly; any write calls a service
tests/ Factories, unit, service, API tests See 10-testing-quality.md

Other conventions:

  • No Django signals for business logic. Signals run hidden and cannot be rolled back with the outbox; we use explicit service calls and outbox topics (ADR-017). pghistory triggers are the only automatic history.
  • Errors: services raise DomainError("dates_unavailable"); one DRF exception handler turns it into {"code", "field", "message", "params"} with HTTP status from a fixed table (BR-SYS-04).
  • Time: services receive now from core.clock so tests can freeze it.
  • Money: only the core.money.Money type crosses function boundaries; raw integers only in models.

2.3 API surfaces

Prefix Who Authentication Notes
/_allauth/app/v1/... Everyone allauth headless (app client, session token) Sign-up, login, phone code, MFA, password reset
/api/v1/public/... Anyone none or session Search, listing detail, trip detail, organisation profile, geography, taxonomy
/api/v1/me/... Signed-in user session token Profile, favourites, my bookings (/me/bookings, ADR-004), conversations, notifications, privacy requests
/api/v1/host/... Host or organisation member session token + X-Host-Account header Every request is checked: the user must hold that host account (BR-ORG-01)
/api/v1/admin/... Staff only staff session token with MFA done Separate URL module and permission classes; a guest or host token never reaches it (STF-05)
/api/v1/webhooks/... Payment gateways (R2) signature check Only path exposed on the public webhook host name
/internal/healthz, /internal/readyz, /internal/metrics Monitoring private network only Not routed by the public proxy

Common headers: Accept-Language (en, fr, ar), Idempotency-Key (required on create and money endpoints, BR-SYS-01), X-Request-ID (created by the BFF if missing, logged everywhere). Pagination: cursor based, page size 24 by default, maximum 50 (SRC-05). Versioning: breaking changes go to /api/v2/ (NFR-08).

3. Transactions and locking rules

General rules:

  1. ATOMIC_REQUESTS is off. Each service that writes decorates itself with transaction.atomic(). One service call = one transaction.
  2. Isolation level stays READ COMMITTED (PostgreSQL default). Correctness comes from constraints, conditional updates and row locks, not from SERIALIZABLE.
  3. No network call inside a transaction (no SMS, no storage, no gateway). Those go to the outbox or to transaction.on_commit.
  4. Database time limits per connection: statement_timeout = 5 s for the API, 60 s for workers; lock_timeout = 2 s; idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = 30 s.
  5. A @retry_on_conflict decorator retries a whole service up to 3 times on deadlock (40P01) or serialization failure (40001), with a short random wait. Constraint violations are not retried; they become clean 409 errors.
  6. Global lock order (always take locks in this order, never the reverse, to prevent deadlocks):
    1. idempotency_record (by key)
    2. booking row (state changes)
    3. inventory rows: room_type_night by (room type, night ascending), experience_slot, trip_departure
    4. account_balance row of the host wallet
    5. inserts only: ledger_transaction, ledger_entry, booking_event, audit_event, outbox_event

3.1 Creating a booking (instant or request)

One transaction, in this order (matches 20-seq-instant-booking):

Step What Protects against Rule
1 Insert idempotency_record (user, endpoint, key) with status = in_progress. If it exists: same body hash and completed returns the stored response; still in progress returns 409 request_in_progress; different body returns 422 idempotency_key_reused Double click, network retry BR-SYS-01
2 Load and re-validate the quote (not expired, prices unchanged); recompute if changed and return 409 price_changed with the new quote Stale or tampered price BR-PRC-01
3 Resolve approval mode and check guest phone verified Wrong flow BR-BKG-01, 02, BR-ACC-01
4a Single unit (home, vehicle): insert the booking row. The exclusion constraint refuses overlap; catch SQLSTATE 23P01 and return 409 dates_unavailable Double booking under concurrency BR-AVL-01
4b Pool (room type, beds, slot, departure): one conditional UPDATE ... SET booked = booked + n WHERE ... AND held + booked + n <= total; if updated rows differ from the number of nights (or 1 for slots and departures) the transaction is rolled back with 409 dates_unavailable Overselling BR-AVL-02, BR-TRP-02
5 If instant and confirmed: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the host wallet account_balance; check the credit floor; if below the floor the booking becomes pending instead Two confirmations spending the same deposit BR-PAY-10
6 Post the commission transaction (2 entries), update the balance row Missing or double commission (unique (booking_id) WHERE kind = commission) BR-PAY-04
7 Insert booking_event, audit_event (host money effect), outbox_event rows (booking.created or booking.confirmed) Lost notifications BR-SYS-03
8 Mark idempotency_record completed with the response body Retry returns the same booking BR-SYS-01
9 Commit. The deferred ledger trigger checks the balance of every transaction at this moment Unbalanced ledger BR-PAY-02

3.2 Changing a booking status

Accept, decline, cancel, expire, complete: SELECT booking FOR UPDATE, check the transition table (BR-BKG-06, table 7a in 04-business-rules.md), check the actor's permission (bookings.respond for accept and decline, DEC-009), then release or convert inventory (pool counters booked - n; single units are freed by the status change itself because the exclusion constraint only covers blocking statuses), post commission or reversal, insert booking_event, outbox. Jobs (expiry, completion) use the same service with actor = system, and process rows in small batches with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so two job runs never fight.

3.3 Inventory counters and holds

  • Holds (held + n) are used only when a payment step exists (R2 and later) or for the 15-minute checkout of pooled inventory (AVL-05). A hold has an expiry; the job inventory.release_expired_holds turns held - n back, and reads ignore expired holds (BR-AVL-06).
  • Host calendar edits (block a night, change a price) lock the same counter rows in the same order, so a host cannot block a night while a guest books it: one of them waits, then sees the result.
  • Reducing total on a room type below held + booked is refused by the check constraint; the host sees 409 inventory_in_use with the nights in conflict.

3.4 Ledger

  • Only ledger.services writes ledger tables. Every posting function takes an idempotency source (booking_id + kind, wallet_topup.id, gateway_event.id) protected by a unique index, so a retried job never posts twice.
  • The balance row is locked (FOR UPDATE) before any posting that can reduce it. Balance = cached sum, verified nightly against the real sum (ledger.reconcile_balances).
  • Corrections are reversing transactions, never updates (BR-PAY-02). The app database role has no UPDATE or DELETE grant on ledger tables.
  • Four-eyes top-ups (BR-PAY-07): the first finance user creates the top-up in pending_approval; nothing is posted until a different finance user approves. Approval and posting are one transaction.

4. Outbox

service (one transaction) ──writes──> business rows + outbox_event(topic, payload, next_attempt_at=now)
                                      │
transaction.on_commit ──nudges──> Celery "outbox.dispatch" (also runs every 10 s as a safety net)
                                      │
dispatcher: SELECT ... FROM outbox_event WHERE status='pending' AND next_attempt_at <= now
            ORDER BY id LIMIT 100 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
            -> for each registered handler of the topic: run it (idempotent)
            -> success: status='sent'; failure: attempts+1, next_attempt_at = now + backoff
  • Backoff: 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 30 min, 1 h, then every hour; after 10 attempts the row becomes failed and an alert fires.
  • Idempotent handlers: email and SMS handlers check delivery_log (outbox_event_id, channel) before sending; search refresh is naturally idempotent (it rebuilds the row).
  • Payload: ids plus a small display snapshot (booking reference, listing title in the source language, amounts) so handlers rarely need to read other apps.
  • Retention: sent rows deleted after 14 days; failed rows kept until a person resolves them.

Main topics: booking.created, booking.confirmed, booking.declined, booking.expired, booking.cancelled, booking.completed, listing.published, listing.changed, listing.paused, host.verification_changed, review.published, wallet.below_zero, wallet.below_floor, wallet.topup_posted, message.created, media.uploaded, otp.requested, privacy.request_created, export.requested.

5. Background jobs (Celery)

Queues: critical (one-time codes and booking notifications, low latency), default (most jobs), media (image work, CPU heavy, its own worker), reports (exports, long). Beat runs as exactly one container. All schedules are in Africa/Algiers time. Every task is safe to run twice (acks_late = True, idempotent services).

Job Schedule What it does Rule / req
notifications.dispatch_outbox every 10 s + after each commit Sends pending outbox events to their handlers BR-SYS-03, NTF-04
notifications.send_email / send_sms on event (critical queue) Renders the template in the user's language and sends via the provider interface; writes delivery_log BR-NTF-02
notifications.sms_budget_check every 15 min Sums SMS spend today and this month from otp_send_log and delivery_log; compares to budget; alerts at 80%; at 100% switches OTP to email or WhatsApp where possible; flags phone or IP ranges with abnormal OTP volume (pumping) NFR-11, ACC-02, research C.2
inventory.release_expired_holds every 1 min Releases holds older than 15 minutes BR-AVL-06
inventory.extend_calendar_horizon daily 02:00 Creates room_type_night and recurring experience_slot rows up to 18 months ahead ADR-002
bookings.expire_pending_requests every 5 min Pending requests past request_expires_at become expired; counters released; both sides notified BR-BKG-04, BKG-03
bookings.complete_stays every 15 min Confirmed bookings past check-out + 2 h become completed; review window opens; earnings counted BR-BKG-05, BKG-04
pricing.purge_expired_quotes hourly Deletes quotes expired more than 24 h ago and not linked to a booking BR-PRC-01
reviews.recompute_ratings on review.* event + nightly 03:00 full pass Recomputes listing, host account and organisation ratings and counts BR-REV-04, REV-05
reviews.publish_blind_reviews hourly (R2) Publishes double-blind reviews when both are in or 14 days passed BR-REV-02
hosts.expire_invitations hourly Marks invitations past 7 days as expired BR-ORG-03
hosts.recount_host_cancellations daily 01:00 Recomputes host_cancellations_12m; opens a moderation case at 3 BR-CAN-03
ledger.reconcile_balances daily 01:30 Checks every account_balance equals the sum of its entries and every transaction sums to zero; alerts on any difference BR-PAY-02, BR-PAY-03
ledger.monthly_invoices 1st of month 03:00 (R2) Builds commission invoices with gap-free numbers BR-PAY-12
ledger.process_gateway_event on webhook (R2) Verifies and applies a stored gateway event once BR-PAY-08, BR-SYS-02
media.process_photo on media.uploaded (media queue) Validates, re-encodes, strips metadata, makes renditions, computes perceptual hash BR-MED-01
media.scan_document on media.uploaded (media queue) ClamAV scan, moves the file to the private bucket or rejects it BR-MED-02
media.purge_orphans daily 04:00 Deletes quarantined or unattached uploads older than 24 h BR-MED-01
trust.refresh_queue_priority every 15 min Raises priority of cases waiting too long BR-MOD-01
trust.evaluate_risk_rules on events (R2) Runs fraud rules, opens cases, never blocks silently BR-MOD-04
search.refresh_listing_doc on listing.*, review.published, host.verification_changed Rebuilds the listing's search row or removes it ADR-011, BR-SRC-01
search.rebuild_all weekly, Sunday 04:00 Full rebuild and comparison, alerts on drift ADR-011
accounts.purge_expired_sessions daily 02:30 Removes expired session tokens and OTP records BR-ACC-03
accounts.process_deletion_requests daily 05:00 Anonymises users whose deletion request is due; keeps legal records BR-PRV-02, PRV-02
accounts.retention_sweep daily 03:30 Deletes ID images 90 days after decision, old messages, otp_send_log rows older than 90 days, old logs per the retention table BR-PRV-05, PRV-04
audit.incident_deadline_watch hourly For open incident_record rows with personal data involved and no anpdp_notified_at: alerts the owner and super admins at day 2, day 4 and 12 hours before anpdp_deadline_at PRV-05
inventory.sync_calendar_feeds every 3 h (Later) Fetches active iCal import feeds through the egress proxy (private IPs blocked), applies blocks, records last_error AVL-06
core.purge_idempotency_records hourly Deletes idempotency records older than 24 h BR-SYS-01
audit.verify_hash_chain daily 00:30 Recomputes the chain for yesterday, stores the day's last hash as an anchor, alerts on break BR-STF-02
audit.create_next_partition monthly, 20th Creates next month's partitions of audit_event (and message once partitioned) ADR-012
audit.run_export on request (reports queue) Builds a CSV export, formula-safe, stores it privately, audits it BR-STF-04, STF-06

6. Caching strategy

Redis is used for three separate things, in separate logical databases so one cannot evict the other: db 0 Celery broker, db 1 cache, db 2 rate limits, OTP counters and login locks (with maxmemory-policy noeviction on that instance, because losing a lock counter is a security hole).

What Where Lifetime Invalidation
Geography, taxonomy lists, experience and trip type lists Redis + HTTP Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 24 h Version key bumped by the service that changes them
Current platform settings and published onboarding flows Redis 60 s Bumped on publish (BR-CFG-01, 02)
Public listing detail (without availability) Redis 5 min Outbox listing.changed deletes the key
Search results not cached at launch Measure first (NFR-02). If needed: 60 s cache on identical anonymous queries without dates
Facet counts for the home page Redis 5 min Time only
Availability, prices in a booking, balances, permissions, anything personal never cached Always read from PostgreSQL inside the transaction

HTTP rules: personal responses send Cache-Control: private, no-store. Public GET responses send an ETag; the Next.js BFF may cache them with tagged revalidation. The CDN caches only static files and public photo renditions (see 09-devops-hosting.md), never API responses.

7. Search strategy

PostgreSQL only at launch (research B.7, ADR-011, ADR-020).

  1. Candidate filter on listing_search_doc: vertical, wilaya or commune, guests (capacity_guests >= n), price range, property type, experience type, amenities (amenity_ids @> {...} with GIN), instant only, rating, map box (location_public && ST_MakeEnvelope(...) with GiST). Only published listings of approved, non-suspended host accounts have a row (BR-SRC-01).
  2. Text: tsv_fr, tsv_en, tsv_ar with the right dictionary for the request language, plus trigram similarity on search_text (unaccented title and place names) for typos and transliteration ("Tipaza", "Tipasa", "تيبازة").
  3. Availability (only when dates are given): for each candidate, a NOT EXISTS probe on the booking exclusion index (single units) or a range read on room_type_night (pools), plus host blocks from listing_day. Partial matches return the largest free sub-range (BR-AVL-05).
  4. Facets: each facet count is computed on the filtered set without that facet's own filter (BR-SRC-01), with one GROUP BY per facet on the candidate set.
  5. Sort and page: relevance, price, rating, newest; cursor pagination, 24 per page, max 50; map mode returns up to 500 pins with public points only (SRC-02, BR-SRC-03).
  6. Trips are searched separately on trip + trip_departure (departures overlapping the dates, seats left) and shown in their own tab (ADR-004, TRP-05).
  7. Place autocomplete uses commune with trigram indexes on French and Arabic names (Q15 in the schema). Free-text address lookup through Nominatim is server-side, cached, and at most 1 request per second (research C.5).

When to add an external engine (Meilisearch first): if search p95 stays above 500 ms with 20,000 listings after index tuning (NFR-02), or if Arabic typo tolerance is not good enough in user tests. The search table and outbox topics make this a new consumer, not a rewrite.

8. File upload pipeline

Step Photos (listing, avatar, logo) Private documents (KYC, message attachments R2)
Allowed types JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC PDF, JPEG, PNG
Max size 15 MB 10 MB
Checks Magic bytes, Pillow decompression-bomb limit (50 megapixels), dimensions at least 1024 px wide for listing photos Magic bytes, ClamAV scan, PDF without JavaScript or embedded files
Transform Re-encode to WebP and JPEG; renditions 320, 640, 1280, 1920 px; all metadata including GPS removed Images re-encoded and metadata removed; PDFs stored as uploaded after a clean scan
Duplicates Perceptual hash compared with other hosts' photos; a match opens a trust case (BR-MOD-04) SHA-256 stored
Final bucket public (served by CDN with random keys) private (no public access, signed GET valid 5 minutes, every view audited)
Rules BR-MED-01, MED-01, MED-03 BR-MED-02, MED-02

The browser never receives storage keys, only presigned URLs. Storage keys are random UUIDs, never file names.

9. Internationalisation (i18n)

Topic Approach
Languages en, fr, ar. Default fr (user column preferred_locale). Fallback order: requested, then fr, then en
How the API knows the language The BFF sends Accept-Language from the URL locale (/ar/...); Django LocaleMiddleware activates it. Background jobs use the recipient's preferred_locale
Platform lists (amenities, categories, property types, wilayas, communes, reason codes, experience and trip types) django-modeltranslation columns name_en, name_fr, name_ar (research B.9). The API returns the active language only, or all three on admin endpoints
Host-written text (titles, descriptions, reviews, messages) Stored once with source_language; shown as written. Machine translation is a later option
API errors Stable snake_case code (for example dates_unavailable) plus a translated message. The apps map the code to their own text (NFR-13, BR-SYS-04)
Notifications, emails, SMS Django templates per language; SMS texts kept short (Arabic SMS has 70 characters per segment)
Numbers and dates Latin digits in all languages (ar-DZ with latn); dates ISO 8601 in the API; display formatting is done by the apps
Time zone Stored in UTC; stay dates and business days in Africa/Algiers; week starts Sunday; weekend Friday and Saturday (BR-SYS-05)
Translation files .po files in the repository; CI fails if a message is missing in one language (10-testing-quality.md section 8)

10. How the website and the admin will use the API

10.1 What exists today

Both apps are Next.js 14. All data goes through lib/data/* functions that read and write in-memory mock stores on the Next.js server (frontend/lib/data/_store.ts, admin/lib/mock-data/store). Pages and server actions call only these functions; the comments say "TODO: replace with Supabase", which this blueprint replaces with "replace with the Django API". The website signs its own session cookie (DARNA_SESSION_SECRET); the admin signs a JWT (ADMIN_AUTH_SECRET). The website has a test mode (NEXT_PUBLIC_BLADUS_TEST_MODE, ON unless set to 0) that allows one-click demo login, a built-in secret and non-Secure cookies. Test mode must be OFF (0) in every environment with real people's data; the deploy pipeline refuses a production build where it is not 0 (09-devops-hosting.md section 7).

10.2 Target: BFF

  • The browser never holds the Django token in JavaScript. Next.js stores the allauth session token inside an encrypted, httpOnly cookie and sends it to Django in the X-Session-Token header from server code only (cookie flags in 08-security-privacy.md section 4).
  • Django is reachable from the Next.js servers over the private network. The public internet reaches only the Next.js apps and, in R2, the webhook path.
  • The BFF passes the real client IP in X-Forwarded-For; Django trusts that header only from the BFF and proxy addresses (TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS), so rate limits and audit logs see the real IP.
  • Client-side components that need fresh data (message polling, notifications badge) call a Next.js route handler that forwards to Django; they never call Django directly.

10.3 Typed client

  • Django generates openapi.yaml with drf-spectacular in CI (NFR-08). It is published as a build artifact and copied into both apps (lib/api/schema.d.ts) by openapi-typescript.
  • A small server-only wrapper lib/api/client.ts built on openapi-fetch adds the headers, timeouts (5 s), one retry for idempotent GETs, and turns API errors into the existing ActionResult shape. API code values are mapped to the apps' ERROR_CODES list (for example dates_unavailable to the website's existing date error codes); new codes are added to the messages/*.json files in en, fr and ar.
  • Both apps run tsc --noEmit against the generated types in CI. An API change that breaks a call breaks the app build before deployment.

10.4 Migration from mock data to the API, one module at a time

Each lib/data/<module>.ts keeps its exported function names and return types. Inside, it chooses a source:

lib/data/listings.ts           (unchanged signatures, used by pages and actions)
  ├─ lib/data/mock/listings.ts (today's code, moved)
  └─ lib/api/listings.ts       (calls Django through the typed client, maps DTOs)
switch: server-only env var BLADUS_API_MODULES="geo,taxonomy,listings"

The flag is a server-only variable (never NEXT_PUBLIC_), read at request time, so a module can be switched back without rebuilding. For each module: (1) build the Django endpoints and contract tests; (2) write the API adapter and a parity test (same fixture through mock and API gives the same DTO shape); (3) in staging, run in "shadow" mode for a few days (serve mock, call the API too, log differences); (4) switch staging, then production; (5) after two weeks without rollback, delete the mock code.

Order Website module(s) Admin module(s) Why this order
1 geo (via lib/algeria.ts), catalog type lists categories Read-only reference data, lowest risk; proves the client, headers and i18n
2 auth (sessions, OTP, profile) auth, team (staff login with MFA) Every personal module needs real users; removes the signed-cookie and JWT secrets
3 listings, experiences, vehicles, trips (read: search, detail) listings (read, moderation) Public pages; search performance can be measured
4 organizations + onboarding, documents hosts, approvals, onboarding, settings Hosts must exist and be verified before they publish
5 listings (write), calendar listings (write) Listing review flow (DEC-003)
6 reservations, wallet bookings, finance, ledger The money and availability core; needs concurrency tests green
7 favorites, notifications, conversations users, network Personal features on top of bookings
8 reviews reviews, audit, analytics, promotions, command-palette Need real completed bookings and audit data

Rules during migration: a module switched to the API never writes to the mock store again; mixed states are allowed only between modules that do not share writes (for example reservations and wallet switch together because a booking posts commission).

12. Architecture decisions (summary)

Numbering continues from 05-database-schema.md (ADR-001 to ADR-014).

ADR Decision Rejected options Why
ADR-015 Modular monolith: one Django project, 17 apps + kernel, one database Microservices; one big app without boundaries Small team, one transaction for booking + inventory + ledger; Airbnb split only at hundreds of engineers (research A.1)
ADR-016 Services and selectors (HackSoft style), thin DRF views Logic in serializers or models ("fat models"); Django Ninja Testable functions, one place per rule, known to Algerian Django developers (research B.2)
ADR-017 Transactional outbox for all side effects Django signals; calling Celery directly inside the transaction A rolled-back change sends nothing; a crash after commit still sends (BR-SYS-03)
ADR-018 Celery + Redis with 4 queues and one beat Django built-in tasks (6.x), Dramatiq, Huey Retries, schedules, monitoring today; thin tasks keep the door open to Django tasks (research B.5)
ADR-019 BFF with allauth headless session tokens in encrypted httpOnly cookies JWT in browser storage; SimpleJWT; Django cookies shared across domains Tokens never reach JavaScript; revocable server-side (ACC-03); OTP, MFA and rate limits included (research B.3)
ADR-020 PostgreSQL search (listing_search_doc + PostGIS + trigram) Meilisearch, Typesense, OpenSearch at launch One store, consistent with availability; external engine only when measured slow
ADR-021 Polling a cursor endpoint for messages (5 to 15 s) WebSockets via Django Channels or Centrifugo at launch Simplest to run; Centrifugo later (research B.6)
ADR-022 S3-compatible storage hosted in Algeria, presigned uploads, quarantine then process Uploads through Django; Cloudinary; Cloudflare R2 for personal files Data residency (BR-PRV-04), no large files in the API process, vendor-neutral
ADR-023 OpenAPI + openapi-typescript + openapi-fetch typed client Hand-written fetch calls; orval; hey-api Small, works in server components; breaking changes fail compile (NFR-08)
ADR-024 Module-by-module migration behind server-only flags with shadow reads Big-bang switch; keeping mock and API both writable Each step reversible without a rebuild; risk spread over time
ADR-025 Layered app dependencies checked by import-linter Convention only Boundaries stay real as the team grows
ADR-026 READ COMMITTED + constraints + ordered row locks SERIALIZABLE everywhere; Redis locks Constraints are the final guard (ADR-002); fewer retries; Redis locks are not transactional with the data

Check yourself

  • Which app owns onboarding_draft, and why is it not in config?
  • notifications is in layer L1. How can it send a "booking confirmed" email without importing bookings?
  • Two guests book the last hotel room at the same second. Which step of section 3.1 stops the second one, and what error does it get?
  • Why is no SMS ever sent from inside a database transaction?
  • Which job releases inventory held for an unpaid checkout, and how often does it run?
  • Which data is never cached, and why?
  • What must be true before the website's reservations module is switched to the API, and which module switches with it?
  • Where does a KYC document go after upload, and how long is a download link valid?

08. Security and privacy

In plain words
This page says what we protect (people's identities, ID documents, money records, the platform's reputation), from whom, and how.
It maps the ten most common API attacks (OWASP API Top 10) to BLADUS endpoints, and defines login, sessions, roles, secrets, encryption, file safety and rate limits.
It explains how Algerian personal data law (Law 18-07 as amended by Law 25-11) shapes the design: data stays in Algeria, a register of processing, consents, a 5-day breach notice.
It ends with a checklist to complete before launch and the questions a lawyer must answer.
Every legal point is marked VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL: this is an engineering plan, not legal advice.

Terms used here (see also glossary.md):

  • Threat model: a structured list of what could go wrong, who could cause it, and what stops it.
  • STRIDE: six kinds of threat: Spoofing (pretending to be someone), Tampering (changing data), Repudiation (denying you did something), Information disclosure (leaks), Denial of service (making the site unusable), Elevation of privilege (getting rights you should not have).
  • OWASP API Top 10: the list of the 10 most common API security risks (2023 edition), published by the OWASP foundation.
  • OTP: one-time password, here a 6-digit code sent by SMS or email.
  • MFA / 2FA: multi-factor login: a password plus a second proof (an authenticator app code (TOTP) or a passkey).
  • TOTP: time-based one-time password, the 6-digit code shown by apps such as Google Authenticator.
  • Passkey (WebAuthn): login with the phone or laptop's fingerprint or PIN; cannot be phished.
  • Session token: a random value that proves "this request comes from a signed-in user". Here created by allauth, kept by the Next.js server.
  • Cookie flags: HttpOnly (JavaScript cannot read it), Secure (only sent over HTTPS), SameSite (not sent with requests coming from other sites).
  • CSRF: cross-site request forgery: another site makes your browser send a request to ours.
  • Encryption at rest / in transit: data is unreadable on disk / on the network without a key.
  • Envelope encryption: data is encrypted with a data key; the data key is itself encrypted with a master key kept elsewhere.
  • HMAC: a hash mixed with a secret key; the same input always gives the same output, but nobody without the key can compute or reverse it.
  • Hash chain: each audit row stores the hash of the previous row, so deleting or changing a row breaks the chain visibly.
  • ClamAV: a free antivirus engine that scans uploaded files.
  • EXIF: hidden information inside photos (camera, date, GPS position).
  • DPIA: data protection impact assessment, a written study of the risks of a sensitive processing (here: ID documents).
  • Data subject: the person the data is about (guest, host, staff).
  • Controller / processor: the controller (BLADUS) decides why data is processed; a processor (hosting company, SMS provider) processes it on BLADUS's instructions.
  • RPO / RTO: how much data we may lose (recovery point) / how long we may be down (recovery time) after a disaster.

Inputs: 02-research.md sections C.3 and D, 03-requirements.md (ACC, STF, MED, PRV, NFR-05, NFR-11), 04-business-rules.md, 05-database-schema.md ADR-012 and ADR-014, 07-architecture.md.

2. Who might attack, and who must be trusted

Actor Motivation Typical attempts
Anonymous visitor / scraper Data, competition Bulk listing scraping, enumeration of ids, map scraping for exact addresses
Fraudster posing as host Money Fake listing with stolen photos, asks for a CCP transfer outside BLADUS, disappears
Fraudster posing as guest Money, harm Stolen identity, fake payment receipts sent to hosts, harassment
Account takeover attacker Money, data Password reuse, OTP brute force, SIM swap, phishing of staff
SMS pumping fraud Money (premium SMS revenue share) Mass OTP requests to number ranges they control
Competing host Ranking Fake reviews, calendar blocking with requests never confirmed
Malicious or careless staff member (insider) Curiosity, money Viewing KYC files without need, manual top-up to a friend's wallet, mass export
Compromised dependency or CI Wide access Malicious package, stolen deployment secrets
Hosting or infrastructure provider incident none (accident) Disk loss, data centre outage, misrouted backups

Trusted components: the Next.js servers (BFF), the Django API, workers, PostgreSQL, Redis, object storage, all in the private network in Algeria (02-containers). Trust boundaries: browser to proxy (internet), proxy to Next.js, Next.js to Django (private network, service authentication), Django to external providers (SMS, email, gateway in R2).

4. Authentication and sessions

4.1 Building blocks

django-allauth in headless mode, "app" client (research B.3): the API returns a session token; the Next.js server keeps it. allauth modules used: account (email and phone), mfa (TOTP, WebAuthn passkeys, recovery codes), usersessions (list and revoke sessions). Passwords hashed with Argon2id.

4.2 Cookies held by the Next.js servers

Cookie App Content Flags Lifetime
__Host-bladus_session Website allauth session token, encrypted (AES-256-GCM) with BLADUS_SESSION_COOKIE_KEY, plus active host account id HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; no Domain (the __Host- prefix forces this) 30 days sliding (BR-ACC-03)
__Host-bladus_admin Admin staff session token, encrypted with ADMIN_SESSION_COOKIE_KEY HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/ 8 h absolute, 30 min idle (BR-ACC-03)
bladus_locale Website en, fr or ar Secure; SameSite=Lax 1 year
  • SameSite=Lax plus an Origin check on every mutating route handler and server action protects against CSRF on the website; the admin uses Strict.
  • The Django API itself uses no cookies for the apps (token in header), so classic CSRF does not apply to it. The Django admin console uses Django's own session and CSRF cookies on its own host name.
  • These replace the current darna_session (website, HMAC-signed, built-in development secret in test mode) and darna_admin_session (admin, JWT that cannot be revoked). With test mode OFF the website must refuse to start without its key.

4.3 Sign-in rules

Topic Rule
Sign-up Email + password, or Algerian phone + OTP. Verification code before the first booking (DEC-012, BR-ACC-01)
Passwords Minimum 10 characters; refused if in a local list of the 100,000 most common breached passwords; no composition rules; change revokes all other sessions (ACC-04)
OTP 6 digits, valid 10 min, invalidated after 5 wrong tries, max 3 sends per phone per hour and 10 per IP per hour, same error for every failure (BR-ACC-02). Phone numbers outside Algeria need an extra check (CAPTCHA by a self-hosted provider, or email verification first) to limit SMS pumping
Lockout 5 failures in 15 min lock the account and the IP for 60 s, counters in Redis shared by all servers (BR-ACC-05). Repeated locks increase the wait (60 s, 5 min, 15 min)
Staff MFA Mandatory before any admin endpoint works (403 mfa_required); TOTP or passkey; 10 single-use recovery codes; passkeys recommended for super admins (BR-ACC-04)
Host MFA Mandatory before adding or changing payout or refund account details (BR-ACC-04, BR-PAY-09)
Step-up Sensitive actions (change email or phone, payout details, ownership transfer, staff role change, export) need a fresh authentication within the last 10 minutes
Session revocation Logout, password change, staff deactivation, ban: tokens deleted server-side immediately; the next API call returns 401 (ACC-03, STF-02)
New device Email or SMS notice on sign-in from a new device for hosts with a wallet and for staff
Staff invitation One-time link valid 48 h; staff sets password, then must enrol MFA before the first admin page (STF-02)

4.4 Account recovery and SIM swap

Phone-number recovery alone is not enough for hosts with payout details or for staff: they also need the email link or an MFA recovery code. After a phone or email change, payout changes are blocked for 72 h and the old contact is notified (BR-PAY-09, research D.2).

4.5 Service-to-service authentication

  • Next.js to Django: private network only, plus a header X-BFF-Key with a per-app secret (BFF_SERVICE_KEY_WEBSITE, BFF_SERVICE_KEY_ADMIN) checked by a Django middleware. A request to /api/v1/admin with the website key is refused even with a staff token.
  • Django to PostgreSQL and Redis: TLS on the private network, separate database roles (section 7.3).
  • Workers to providers (SMS, email): API keys from the secret store; outbound traffic through an egress proxy allowlist (SSRF protection, API7).

5. Authorisation

5.1 Three surfaces, deny by default

  1. Public and guest (/public, /me): object ownership checked in selectors (bookings_for_guest(user)); other people's objects return 404, not 403, so ids cannot be probed.
  2. Host (/host): every request names X-Host-Account; a permission class checks the user holds it (individual owner or active membership) and the organisation role permission (table 5.3). Lists are always filtered by that host account.
  3. Staff (/admin): staff token, MFA done, permission from the staff role (table 5.2). Field-level: personal data shown only to roles that need it (for example analysts see counts, not phone numbers).

Output fields per role are separate serializers (no "one serializer with hidden fields"). Writable fields are an explicit allowlist per endpoint (mass-assignment protection, API3).

7. Secrets, keys and encryption

7.1 Secrets management

Rule Detail
Where secrets live Production and staging secrets in an encrypted file per environment (SOPS with age keys) in a private operations repository; decrypted only on the servers at deploy time into files readable by the service user. Move to HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao when the team grows
Never In the application repository, Docker images, NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables, logs, error reports, tickets or chat
CI GitHub Actions environment secrets with required reviewers for production; CI never holds database or encryption keys, only deploy credentials
Access Two named people hold production key access; each access to the master encryption key is logged
Rotation See table 7.2. Rotation is rehearsed in staging first
Leak response Rotate, revoke, search logs for use, record in the incident register

7.2 Key and secret inventory

Secret Used for Rotation
DJANGO_SECRET_KEY Django signing (password reset links, Django admin console) Yearly, or on leak (supports a fallback list)
BLADUS_SESSION_COOKIE_KEY, ADMIN_SESSION_COOKIE_KEY Encrypt BFF cookies Yearly (two keys accepted during rotation)
BFF_SERVICE_KEY_WEBSITE, BFF_SERVICE_KEY_ADMIN Next.js to Django service authentication Every 6 months
FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEYS (master key, versioned) Envelope encryption of payout numbers Yearly; old versions kept to decrypt, data re-wrapped by a job
ID_HASH_PEPPER HMAC of document numbers and recipient hashes Never rotated casually (hashes would change); rotation needs a planned re-hash from the source documents, impossible after images are deleted, so guard it carefully
Database passwords (per role) PostgreSQL Every 6 months
Redis password Redis AUTH Every 6 months
Storage access keys Object storage Every 6 months
SMS, email, gateway API keys and webhook secrets Providers Yearly or per provider policy
Backup encryption key (age) Encrypt dumps and archives Yearly; private key stored offline by two people

7.3 Encryption

Layer How
In transit, public TLS 1.2 and 1.3 only, modern ciphers, HSTS max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload after a trial period, certificates by ACME (Let's Encrypt) through Caddy
In transit, private PostgreSQL sslmode=verify-full; Redis with TLS and AUTH; object storage over HTTPS even inside the network
At rest, disks Full-disk encryption (LUKS) on database, storage and backup volumes where the provider allows it; otherwise encrypted volumes on top of provider disks (VERIFY with ICOSNET / Djezzy Cloud what is offered)
At rest, backups Every dump and WAL archive encrypted with age before leaving the server (see 09-devops-hosting.md)
At rest, object storage Server-side encryption on private and quarantine buckets
Field level: payout numbers AES-256-GCM with a random data key per row; data key wrapped by the master key from FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEYS; stored as key_version + wrapped_key + nonce + ciphertext in payout_account.number_encrypted; only number_last4 in clear (ADR-014). The master key is never in the database or in backups
Field level: ID numbers Never stored in clear. Normalised (digits only, upper case), then HMAC-SHA256(ID_HASH_PEPPER, type + ":" + number) in host_document.number_hash, used to detect the same ID on two accounts (research D.2)
Recipients in logs delivery_log.recipient_hash is an HMAC of the phone or email, never the clear value
Database roles bladus_migrate (owner, used only by migrations), bladus_app (no UPDATE/DELETE on ledger, audit, booking_event), bladus_readonly (reports, replicas), bladus_backup

Control Detail Rule
