9. Rate limits

Two layers: coarse limits per IP at the proxy (Caddy) to stop floods, fine limits per user / IP / phone in Django (DRF throttles and allauth limits) stored in Redis db 2. Responses use 429 with Retry-After.

Scope Limit Layer
Any request per IP 30 per second burst, 600 per minute Proxy
Login attempts 5 failures in 15 min per account and per IP, then lock 60 s (growing) allauth + Redis (BR-ACC-05)
OTP send 3 per phone per hour, 10 per IP per hour, 20 per device id per day; every attempt (sent, failed, blocked_rate_limit) written to otp_send_log allauth + Redis (BR-ACC-02, ACC-02)
OTP verify 5 tries per code allauth
Password reset request 3 per account per hour, 10 per IP per hour allauth
Search and public reads 120 per minute per IP, 300 per minute per signed-in user DRF
Quote 60 per minute per user or IP DRF
Booking create 10 per hour per guest; max 5 open requests at once DRF + service (API6)
Messages 30 per minute per user; 200 per day to new conversations DRF
Message polling 1 per 3 seconds per user per conversation DRF
Upload slots 60 per hour per host account DRF
Reviews and reports 10 reports per day per user DRF
Admin API 600 per minute per staff user; exports 10 per hour DRF
SMS budget daily and monthly caps in settings, spend summed from otp_send_log.cost_minor and delivery_log.cost_minor; alert at 80%, stop non-critical SMS at 100%; abnormal volume per phone prefix or IP range raises a pumping alert job notifications.sms_budget_check (NFR-11)

10. Audit log with hash chain

  • What is logged (STF-03): every staff write; every host money action (top-up, commission override, payout details change); team changes (invite, role change, removal, ownership transfer); logins, failed logins, MFA changes and session revocations; every KYC file view; exports (filters and row count); settings and onboarding publishes; privacy requests and their handling.
  • Row content: occurred_at, actor_id, actor_kind, actor_role, action, object_type, object_id, host_account_id, before, after, ip, user_agent, request_id, prev_hash, hash (schema.dbml). before and after keep only changed fields and never contain secrets, full document numbers or message bodies.
  • Hash: hash = SHA-256(prev_hash || canonical_json(row without hash)), where canonical JSON has sorted keys and UTC timestamps. Rows are appended through one service which takes a short advisory lock so the chain has a single order.
  • Protection: insert-only for bladus_app (no UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE); monthly partitions; the job audit.verify_hash_chain recomputes yesterday's chain each night and stores the day's final hash as an anchor in a separate place (the backup bucket in the second data centre and an email to two named people). A break raises a critical alert.
  • Access: audit.view for reading; nobody can edit. Exports of the audit log are themselves audited.
  • Retention: 5 years for staff and security events, 10 years where linked to accounting (VERIFY).

pghistory row history (bookings, listings, memberships, settings) complements the audit log for "what did this row look like before" questions (ADR-012).

11. Fraud and trust controls

Pattern (research D.2) Signals Controls Rules
Off-platform payment push (CCP/RIP numbers, BaridiMob, WhatsApp links before confirmation) Regex and number patterns in messages Masked before confirmation; repeated attempts flag the thread; guest warning banner BR-MSG-01, MSG-04
Fake listing with stolen photos Perceptual hash match, reverse-image hits, new host with many listings Review before publishing; proof of property for the first listing; trust case on duplicates BR-LST-02, BR-MED-01, BR-HST-03
Duplicate accounts after a ban Same phone, same device id, same ID number hash Block sign-up or verification with a matching hash; case for staff BR-ACC-01, ADR-014
Account takeover via SIM swap Phone change then payout change; new device; new country Re-verification; MFA; 72 h hold on payout changes; notices to old contacts BR-PAY-09
Fake wallet top-up receipt Same receipt reference twice; large amounts Unique receipt per method; four-eyes above 500,000 DZD BR-PAY-07
Calendar blocking by fake requests Many open requests, no confirmations 24 h TTL; max open requests per guest; flags BR-BKG-04, API6
Fake reviews and review rings Reviews only from completed bookings; bursts; same IP/device Review eligibility in the database; burst and ring detection (R2) BR-REV-01, BR-MOD-04
SMS pumping Many OTP requests to sequential numbers or foreign ranges, visible in otp_send_log (by phone hash and IP) Limits per phone/IP/device; foreign numbers need extra checks; budget stop BR-ACC-02, ACC-02, NFR-11
Staff insider abuse Unusual KYC views, exports, top-ups Least privilege; four-eyes; every view audited; weekly review of KYC views and exports by a super admin BR-STF-01, 02, 04
Host with many cancellations 3 host cancellations in 12 months Moderation case BR-CAN-03

Principle: risk rules add friction (extra check, case for staff), they never silently block (BR-MOD-04, Airbnb "targeted friction", research A.1).

12.3 Consents

  • Stored in consent_record with document (terms, privacy, marketing), version, time, IP (BR-PRV-01).
  • Marketing is opt-in, never pre-ticked, withdrawable in one click from every message (NTF-03, BR-PRV-03). Critical service messages cannot be switched off.
  • A new version of the terms or privacy notice asks for acceptance again at the next sign-in.

12.4 DPIA for KYC (outline)

  1. Description: which documents per host type (table 3a in 04-business-rules.md), who sees them, how long.
  2. Necessity: why each document is needed (L4); can a check be done without keeping the image (keep decision + hash)?
  3. Risks: leak of ID images, insider viewing, identity theft, over-retention.
  4. Measures: private bucket, scan, 5-minute signed views, every view audited, weekly review, 90-day deletion, HMAC instead of numbers, encryption at rest, data in Algeria.
  5. Residual risk and sign-off by the responsible person; review yearly or on change.

12.7 Personal data breach runbook (5-day clock)

Law 25-11 requires notifying ANPDP within 5 days (research C.3, VERIFY the exact start of the clock and the content of the notice).

Time Action Who
Hour 0 Anyone who suspects a breach reports it in the incident channel; the on-call engineer creates an incident_record row (detected_at = time of discovery = start of the clock; personal_data_involved; the system sets anpdp_deadline_at = detected_at + 5 days) Anyone, on-call
Hour 0 to 4 Contain: revoke keys or sessions, block accounts or IPs, take affected systems offline if needed; preserve logs and evidence (no wiping) On-call + tech lead
Hour 4 to 24 Assess: which data, how many people, which categories (KYC, contacts, money), whether data left the system; severity (low / high) Tech lead + data protection contact
Day 1 to 2 Decide on notification with the lawyer; draft the ANPDP notice (nature of the breach, categories and number of people and records, likely consequences, measures taken, contact person) Data protection contact + lawyer
Day 2 to 4 If high risk to people: prepare messages to affected users in en, fr, ar (what happened, what to do, contact) Data protection contact
Before day 5 Send the notice to ANPDP; set anpdp_notified_at and attach the sending proof Data protection contact
Day 5+ Inform users if required (set users_notified_at); follow up; root cause analysis; fixes with deadlines; update this runbook; set closed_at Team

The incident register is the incident_record table (staff-only, every change audited in audit_event). It keeps every incident, even those not notified to ANPDP, with the reasoning in summary and actions_taken. The hourly job audit.incident_deadline_watch reminds the owner and super admins at day 2, day 4 and 12 hours before anpdp_deadline_at while anpdp_notified_at is empty.

13. Pre-launch security checklist

  • NEXT_PUBLIC_BLADUS_TEST_MODE=0 in the website production build; the build fails otherwise; demo accounts absent; no development secrets anywhere.
  • All DARNA_SESSION_SECRET / ADMIN_AUTH_SECRET mock auth code removed after the auth module migration.
  • manage.py check --deploy clean; DEBUG = False; ALLOWED_HOSTS exact; SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER set correctly; security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, frame-ancestors 'none') on both Next.js apps and Django admin console.
  • TLS A grade on an external test; HTTP redirects to HTTPS.
  • Django API not reachable from the internet except the webhook path; Redis, PostgreSQL, storage admin ports closed from outside (external port scan).
  • Database roles and grants applied; bladus_app cannot UPDATE or DELETE ledger, audit, booking_event (test).
  • Every staff account has MFA; super admins use passkeys; recovery codes stored offline.
  • Admin app reachable only through allowlisted IPs or a VPN, in addition to MFA.
  • Rate limits active and tested (section 9); SMS budget caps configured.
  • Secrets in the secret store only; repository scanned for secrets (gitleaks) including history.
  • Dependency scans clean or accepted (pip-audit, npm audit, image scan with Trivy).
  • Field encryption key and ID pepper generated, stored, backed up offline by two people; restore of an encrypted field tested.
  • Backups encrypted, in the second Algerian data centre; restore drill done once (see 09-devops-hosting.md).
  • Audit hash chain verification job running; anchor delivered.
  • ClamAV running with fresh signatures; EXIF strip verified on a phone photo with GPS.
  • Log and error scrubbing verified (no phone, email, token, document number in logs).
  • OWASP API Top 10 tests green (section 6); external penetration test done and high findings fixed.
  • Privacy notice and terms published in 3 languages; consent capture working.
  • ANPDP declarations or authorisations filed (VERIFY); processor contracts signed.
  • Breach runbook printed, contacts current, one tabletop exercise done (including creating a test incident_record and seeing the deadline reminders).
  • Incident on-call rota defined.

09. DevOps and hosting: where BLADUS runs and how we operate it

In plain words
BLADUS runs in three places: your laptop (dev), a test copy with fake data (staging), and the real site (production).
Production and every copy of personal data live in Algerian data centres (ICOSNET or Djezzy Cloud), with backups in a second Algerian site. This follows our reading of Law 18-05 art. 8 and Law 18-07/25-11: VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL.
We start simple: a few servers running Docker Compose. Every code change is checked automatically on GitHub (tests, types, API contract) before it can be deployed.
We can lose at most 15 minutes of data (RPO) and be back within 4 hours (RTO); a restore is practised every month.
This page also gives a rough monthly cost, step-by-step runbooks (deploy, rollback, incident, restore), and the list of settings each program needs.

Terms used here (see also glossary.md):

  • Environment: one complete copy of the system (dev, staging, production) with its own data and secrets.
  • Container / image: an image is a packaged program with everything it needs; a container is a running copy of it. Docker Compose starts several containers from one file.
  • Reverse proxy: the front door server (Caddy) that receives HTTPS traffic and passes it to the right program.
  • TLS certificate: the file that makes https:// work and proves the site's identity.
  • CDN: content delivery network, servers in many places that keep copies of static files close to users.
  • CI/CD: continuous integration (check every change automatically) and continuous delivery (deploy automatically after checks).
  • GitHub Actions: GitHub's service that runs these checks and deployments.
  • Migration: a versioned script that changes the database structure.
  • WAL / PITR: PostgreSQL writes every change first into a log (write-ahead log). Keeping that log lets us restore the database to any minute in the past: point-in-time recovery.
  • Replica: a second database server that continuously copies the main one.
  • RPO / RTO: recovery point objective (how much recent data we accept to lose) / recovery time objective (how long we accept to be down).
  • Observability: logs (what happened), metrics (numbers over time), traces and error reports, so we see problems before users report them.
  • Health check: a small URL that says "I am alive" (liveness) or "I can serve requests" (readiness).
  • Runbook: a written step-by-step procedure for an operation or an emergency.
  • Environment variable (env var): a named setting given to a program when it starts (for example DATABASE_URL).

Inputs: 02-research.md sections B.16, C.3, C.6; 03-requirements.md NFR-01 to NFR-13; 05-database-schema.md section 7; 07-architecture.md; 08-security-privacy.md; diagram 02-containers.

Name (proposal) Points to Purpose
bladus.com.dz and www.bladus.com.dz Caddy at site A Website (guests and hosts)

  • .com.dz registration goes through the Algerian registry (NIC.dz, run by CERIST) and normally requires a registered company (RC). Law 18-05 art. 8 mentions .com.dz for e-commerce. VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL (L1, L11 in 13-decisions-needed.md). Also register bladus.dz if available and bladus.com to protect the brand; redirect them to the main name.
  • The Django API has no public host name: only the Next.js servers reach it on the private network (BFF, 07-architecture.md section 10).
  • Email: send from notify.bladus.com.dz with SPF, DKIM and DMARC (p=quarantine, then reject).
  • DNS with two providers or a provider with anycast; low TTL (300 s) on records we may switch during an incident.

5. TLS

  • Caddy obtains and renews certificates automatically with ACME (Let's Encrypt; ZeroSSL as fallback). If the .com.dz registry or provider requires another certificate authority, use that one (VERIFY).
  • TLS 1.2 and 1.3 only; HSTS on after two weeks of stable HTTPS, then includeSubDomains and preload.
  • Internal traffic: TLS from Caddy to Next.js is optional on the same server; required between servers (Django to PostgreSQL with verify-full, Redis TLS, storage HTTPS) using a small internal certificate authority (step-ca) or provider private network plus TLS.

6. CDN

  • Launch without a foreign CDN. Next.js serves its static files with long cache headers (immutable), Caddy compresses (zstd, gzip), public photos are served from the storage server through Caddy with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable (keys are random and never reused).
  • If measurements show slow images or static files for users far from site A, options in order: (1) a second Caddy cache in another Algerian city; (2) Cloudflare or another CDN only for static. and media., after the lawyer confirms public photos and static files are not personal data subject to residency (VERIFY). Never route the website HTML, the admin or the API through a foreign CDN, because the CDN would decrypt personal data.

7.2 How deployment reaches Algeria

The deploy job runs on a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner inside the private network at site A (one for staging, one for production, separate machines). It only pulls signed images and runs Compose commands; it holds no database passwords (those are on the servers, decrypted from the secret store at deploy time). Alternative: a bastion host with SSH deploy keys restricted to one command.

8. Database operations

8.1 Migrations policy

  1. Expand, then contract. A release may only add things (columns nullable or with a constant default, new tables, new indexes). Removing or renaming happens in a later release, after no running code uses the old name. This keeps the previous app version working, so rollback never needs a down-migration.
  2. Large indexes use AddIndexConcurrently in a non-atomic migration; constraints on large tables are added NOT VALID then validated separately.
  3. Every migration sets lock_timeout = 5s; if it cannot get the lock it fails instead of freezing the site.
  4. Data migrations are separate from schema migrations and must be safe to run twice; big backfills run as Celery jobs in batches, not inside migrations.
  5. Migrations run as a one-off container (manage.py migrate) before the new app containers start, using the bladus_migrate role. The app role cannot change the schema.
  6. A pgBackRest incremental backup is taken right before any release that contains a migration flagged risky in review.
  7. Squash migrations only once a year, never across a release still deployed somewhere.

8.2 Backups, PITR and replica

Mechanism Tool Frequency Kept Target (NFR-04)
WAL archive pgBackRest, archive_timeout = 60 s, repository at site B, encrypted (repo-cipher-type = aes-256-cbc) continuous 7 days of PITR RPO 15 min (expected: about 1 min)
Full + differential backups pgBackRest full weekly (Sunday 02:00), differential daily 2 full cycles base for PITR
Streaming replica PostgreSQL physical replication to site B continuous live fast failover, RTO 4 h
Logical dump pg_dump -Fc, encrypted with age before leaving the server nightly 01:00 35 daily, 12 monthly protection against logical mistakes and tool bugs
Object storage MinIO bucket replication (or provider replication) to site B; versioning on private buckets continuous 30 days of versions documents and photos
Secrets and keys Offline copies of the backup decryption key and field encryption master key, held by two people on change always without them backups are useless

All backup copies stay in Algeria (BR-PRV-04). Backup jobs report a "last success" metric; an alert fires if older than 26 hours (dumps) or 10 minutes (WAL archive).

8.3 Monthly restore drill

On the first Tuesday of each month: restore the latest full backup plus WAL to a scratch server at site B to a chosen time 1 hour earlier; run manage.py check, row counts, ledger.reconcile_balances and audit.verify_hash_chain on the copy; open 3 random private documents from the storage replica; record the time taken (must be under 4 hours) and the result in the drill log; destroy the scratch server. A failed drill is a high-priority incident.

8.4 Routine care

pg_stat_statements reviewed weekly (top 20 queries by total time, compared with the query plan targets in 05-database-schema.md section 7); autovacuum tuned for hot tables (room_type_night, outbox_event, notification); minor PostgreSQL updates monthly, major upgrades yearly with a rehearsal in staging; disk alerts at 70% and 85%.

9. Observability

9.1 Logs

  • structlog writes one JSON object per line to stdout; Promtail or Vector ships them to Loki (in Algeria), searchable 90 days, archived 1 year.
  • Fields on every API log line: ts, level, event, request_id, user_id, host_account_id, staff (boolean), method, route (pattern, not raw path), status, duration_ms, db_queries, db_ms, ip_prefix (IPv4 /24 for analytics; full IP only in the audit log), app_version. Celery lines add task, task_id, queue, attempt.
  • Never logged: passwords, OTP codes, session tokens, Authorization or X-Session-Token headers, ID numbers, payout numbers, message bodies, full phone numbers or emails (masked as +213 5** ** ** 12). A scrubbing processor enforces this and has its own tests.

9.2 Errors

GlitchTip (Sentry-compatible, self-hosted in Algeria) with the Sentry SDKs in Django, Celery and both Next.js apps; send_default_pii = False; request bodies and headers scrubbed; release and environment tags; source maps uploaded for the Next.js apps but not served publicly.

Alert Condition Severity First action
Site down External probe fails 3 times in a row critical Incident runbook 11.3

Search slow p95 search > 500 ms for 10 min (NFR-02) high pg_stat_statements, indexes
Error rate 5xx > 1% of requests for 5 min critical GlitchTip, rollback if after a deploy

Beat stopped Heartbeat older than 3 min critical Restart beat (only one!)
Queue backlog critical queue > 100 for 5 min high Scale worker, check provider

Replica lag > 60 s for 10 min high Network to site B, disk
Disk > 85% on any server high Expand or clean
Certificate Expires in < 14 days high Check Caddy renewal
Restore drill Not recorded this month by day 10 medium Schedule it

Alerts go to a team chat channel and, for critical ones, by SMS to the on-call person (through a different provider than the user SMS, so a provider outage does not hide its own alert).

10. Capacity and cost (rough, VERIFY WITH QUOTES)

Expected launch traffic is far below these numbers; the sizes below leave headroom and can start smaller.

Ways to start cheaper: merge worker and monitoring onto the app server for the first months (saves about 25,000 DZD); use email or WhatsApp codes before SMS where users accept it (SMS is the largest variable cost); keep staging off outside working hours.

When to grow: second API server when CPU > 60% at peak for a week; Redis on its own server when memory > 2 GB; read replica for search when DB CPU > 60% at peak; external search only per 07-architecture.md section 7.

11. Runbooks

11.1 Deploy

  1. Check: CI green on the commit; release notes list migrations and flags; no open critical alert; not Thursday evening or Friday (Algerian weekend starts Friday; avoid deploying before it).
  2. Announce in the team channel with the release tag.
  3. Runner pulls images for the tag and verifies their digests.
  4. If the release has a risky migration: trigger a pgBackRest incremental backup and wait for success.
  5. Run the migration container (manage.py migrate --noinput) with the bladus_migrate role. On failure: stop here (nothing else changed); open an incident if the site is affected.
  6. Rolling update of api: start the new container, wait for /internal/readyz, remove one old container from Caddy, stop it gracefully (30 s), repeat.
  7. Restart workers with warm shutdown (SIGTERM, tasks finish), then start new ones. Restart beat last, making sure only one runs.
  8. Rolling update of website and admin the same way.
  9. Smoke tests: home page in 3 languages, search with dates, listing detail, login, host dashboard (staging account), admin login with MFA (staging only), /internal/readyz.
  10. Watch dashboards 15 minutes (error rate, latency, outbox). Announce success.

11.2 Rollback

  1. Decide fast: a new error rate above 1% or a broken key flow after a deploy means rollback first, analysis later.
  2. Redeploy the previous image tag with steps 6 to 9 of 11.1. Do not run down-migrations: the expand-then-contract rule keeps the previous code compatible with the new schema.
  3. If the bad release changed data (wrong postings, wrong statuses), stop the affected jobs (feature flag or scale the worker to 0), then write correcting transactions through services (ledger: reversing transactions). Never edit rows by hand.
  4. If a migration itself destroyed data (should be impossible under the policy): restore to a scratch server with PITR to the minute before the migration and copy back the affected rows with a reviewed script (runbook 11.4).
  5. Write a short incident note.

11.3 Incident

  1. Detect: alert or user report. The on-call person acknowledges within 15 minutes (business hours) or 30 minutes (night).
  2. Declare: open an entry in the incident register with severity (SEV1 site down or data at risk; SEV2 key feature broken; SEV3 degraded). Name one incident lead.
  3. Communicate: status page updated within 30 minutes for SEV1/SEV2 in en, fr, ar; staff informed in the admin app banner.
  4. Stabilise: rollback (11.2), switch off a feature flag, block abusive traffic at Caddy, scale workers, or fail over (step 5).
  5. Failover to site B (site A lost or database primary lost for more than 30 minutes): promote the replica at site B; switch DNS (TTL 300 s) to site B's proxy; start app, worker and beat containers there from the same images; verify readyz, the ledger reconcile and the audit chain; keep site A isolated until repaired, then rebuild it as the new replica. Target total time under 4 hours (RTO).
  6. Personal data involved? Start the breach runbook in 08-security-privacy.md section 12.7 at once: the 5-day ANPDP clock starts at discovery.
  7. Close: when stable for 1 hour. Within 5 working days: blameless review (timeline, cause, what worked, actions with owners and dates).

11.4 Restore (data loss or corruption)

  1. Freeze writes if corruption is spreading: put the platform in maintenance mode (maintenance_mode setting; the website shows a notice; staff read-only).
  2. Identify the target time (just before the bad event) from logs, booking_event, audit_event.
  3. Restore with pgBackRest to a scratch server at site B to that time (--type=time --target=...). Never restore over the live primary first.
  4. Verify on the scratch copy: row counts, ledger reconcile, audit chain up to the target time, sample bookings.
  5. Choose: (a) partial repair: export the affected rows from the scratch copy and re-apply them through a reviewed script or services (preferred, keeps later good data); (b) full restore: replace the primary with the restored copy (loses everything after the target time; users must be told; bookings after that time must be rebuilt from emails and logs).
  6. For object storage: restore object versions from the site B replica.
  7. Lift maintenance mode, monitor, record the restore in the drill/incident log. If personal data was lost or exposed, apply the breach runbook.

10. Testing and quality

In plain words
This page says how we prove the backend does what the rules say, before every deployment.
Most tests are small and fast; fewer are big and slow (the "test pyramid"). Money, refunds and dates are tested with thousands of random examples, not only a few hand-picked ones.
Double booking is tested by firing many requests at the same time against a real PostgreSQL database.
The API contract is checked automatically so the website and admin never break silently; speed is measured against the targets in NFR-01 and NFR-02.
Every business rule (BR-...) must have at least one test whose name contains the rule ID; the build fails if one is missing.

Terms used here (see also glossary.md):

  • Unit test: tests one small function alone, in milliseconds, often without a database.
  • Service test / integration test: tests a service function with a real database, inside a transaction that is rolled back afterwards.
  • API test: sends an HTTP request to an endpoint and checks the response (status, body, permissions).
  • End-to-end (E2E) test: drives a real browser through the website or admin (Playwright).
  • Test pyramid: many unit tests, fewer service and API tests, very few E2E tests.
  • pytest / pytest-django: the Python test runner and its Django plugin.
  • Factory (factory_boy): code that creates realistic test rows (a user, a listing, a booking) with one line.
  • Property-based test (hypothesis): instead of one example, you state a rule that must always hold ("refund never exceeds the total"), and the tool tries hundreds of random inputs, then shrinks any failure to the simplest example.
  • Concurrency test: starts many requests at the same moment to check that locks and constraints hold.
  • Contract test (schemathesis): reads openapi.yaml and sends many generated requests to every endpoint, checking the answers match the contract and the server never crashes.
  • Load / performance test (k6): simulates many users to measure response times.
  • Coverage: the share of code lines (or branches) executed by tests.
  • Mutation testing: the tool makes small bugs in the code on purpose; good tests should fail. Measures test strength.
  • Quality gate: a check in CI that must pass before code can be merged or deployed.
  • Definition of Done (DoD): the checklist a change must satisfy before it counts as finished.
  • Traceability: being able to go from a rule to its test and back.

Inputs: 03-requirements.md (NFR-01, 02, 06, 08, 10, 13), 04-business-rules.md, 05-database-schema.md sections 6 and 7, 07-architecture.md, 08-security-privacy.md, 09-devops-hosting.md section 7, research B.14.

1. Test strategy (pyramid)

Level Share of tests Tools Database Runs
Unit (pure functions: money, policies, date ranges, masking, transitions) about 45% pytest, hypothesis none every push, seconds
Service (one service or selector with real PostgreSQL + PostGIS) about 35% pytest-django, factory_boy, time-machine (frozen clock) real PostgreSQL in a rolled-back transaction every push
API (endpoint, permissions, serializers, error codes) about 15% pytest-django + DRF APIClient real PostgreSQL every push
Concurrency (parallel requests) small set, critical pytest with transaction=True, threads, barrier real PostgreSQL, committed every push (short) + nightly (repeated)
Contract all endpoints schemathesis, drf-spectacular, oasdiff, tsc in both apps seeded API every pull request
E2E (key journeys through the Next.js apps) about 5% (around 20 journeys) Playwright (admin already uses it) staging-like stack before deploy to production
Performance scenarios in section 7 k6 staging with 20,000 listings weekly and before major releases

Principles:

  • Real PostgreSQL always. No SQLite: exclusion constraints, daterange, PostGIS, partial indexes and triggers are part of the rules (BR-AVL-01, BR-PAY-02).
  • Test the rule where it is enforced. A DB-enforced rule is tested by trying to break it with raw ORM writes (bypassing the service) and expecting the database to refuse.
  • Frozen time. Services receive now from core.clock; tests freeze it in Africa/Algiers for date rules (BR-SYS-05).
  • No network. SMS, email, storage and gateway calls go to fakes that record what was sent; one contract test per provider runs against recorded responses.

2. What to test per app

App Must test Key rules

accounts Email unique case-insensitive; phone format; OTP limits and expiry; lockout shared via Redis; session revocation on logout and password change; staff MFA required; consent records; deletion anonymises and keeps legal records BR-ACC-01 to 05, BR-PRV-01, 02

catalog Listing state machine (every allowed and every forbidden move); revision under review keeps live version; hotel without room type cannot submit; reference rows cannot be hard-deleted; experience and trip types BR-LST-01 to 05

Security tests (from 08-security-privacy.md section 6) live in each app as test_api1_* to test_api10_*, plus one matrix test that calls every /api/v1/admin endpoint with each of the 5 staff roles and checks allow or deny against the permission table.

3. Property-based tests (hypothesis)

Pure functions for money, refunds and dates are written so they can be tested without a database. Example properties (the tests will name the rule they protect):

3.1 Money

Property Rule
For any list of price lines, total == sum(rounded lines); never a float anywhere BR-PAY-01
commission(base, rate_bp) is between floor(base x rate / 10,000) and that value + 1 centime, and 0 <= commission <= base BR-PAY-04
Commission is monotonic: a bigger base or rate never gives a smaller commission BR-PAY-04
Applying the discount: only the larger of weekly and monthly applies; result >= 0; 30 nights never uses the weekly rate BR-PRC-03
For any sequence of postings, every ledger transaction sums to zero per currency, and the wallet balance equals the sum of its entries BR-PAY-02, 03
Displayed whole dinars: display(amount) rounds half up and display(a) + display(b) may differ from display(a + b) by at most 1 DZD, which is why totals are summed from lines BR-PAY-01

Example (illustration only, no code files are created in this phase):

@given(base=st.integers(0, 10**12), rate_bp=st.integers(0, 10_000))
def test_br_pay_04_commission_bounds(base, rate_bp):
    c = commission_minor(base, rate_bp)
    exact_floor = base * rate_bp // 10_000
    assert exact_floor <= c <= exact_floor + 1
    assert 0 <= c <= base

3.2 Refunds and cancellations

Property Rule
0 <= refund <= total - already_refunded for any policy, any day, any amounts BR-CAN-04
Refund is non-decreasing with days before check-in (cancelling earlier never refunds less) BR-CAN-01
Before check-in, the cleaning fee and its taxes are always fully refunded BR-CAN-01, 02
Host cancellation: refund owed == total paid; commission reversal == commission posted BR-CAN-03, BR-PAY-05
Guest cancellation: commission kept == round(rate x non-refunded subtotal); kept + reversed == posted BR-PAY-05
Several partial staff refunds in any order: their sum never exceeds the total; the last one that would exceed is refused BR-CAN-04
Worked example 8a reproduces exactly: 31,750 DZD owed, 3,330 DZD back to the wallet BR-CAN-02 
@given(policy=st.sampled_from(POLICIES), b=bookings(), d1=st.integers(-2, 400), d2=st.integers(-2, 400))
def test_br_can_01_refund_never_decreases_when_cancelling_earlier(policy, b, d1, d2):
    early, late = max(d1, d2), min(d1, d2)
    assert refund_for(policy, b, days_before=early) >= refund_for(policy, b, days_before=late)

3.3 Date ranges

Property Rule
For [a, b), nights == b - a in days; a < b always; an empty range is refused BR-SYS-05, BR-AVL-01
Overlap is symmetric: overlaps(x, y) == overlaps(y, x); back-to-back ranges (x.end == y.start) never overlap BR-AVL-01
The Python overlap function agrees with PostgreSQL && on daterange for any pair (tested against the database) BR-AVL-01
largest_free_subrange(request, busy) is inside the request, contains no busy night, and no longer free sub-range exists BR-AVL-05
Day counting for policies uses Africa/Algiers calendar days; around midnight UTC (00:00 to 01:00 Algiers) the day count is still correct BR-CAN-01, BR-SYS-05
Weekend detection: Friday and Saturday only; week starts on Sunday BR-SYS-05
Pool reservation of n units over k nights changes exactly k counter rows or none BR-AVL-02

Hypothesis settings: max_examples = 200 on every push, 2,000 in the nightly run; the example database is kept in CI cache so a found failure is replayed until fixed.

4. Concurrency tests on real PostgreSQL

How: @pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True) (real commits), a ThreadPoolExecutor where each thread opens its own database connection, and a threading.Barrier so all threads call the service at the same instant. Each scenario runs 5 times on every push and 200 times in the nightly run. CI uses the same PostgreSQL and PostGIS versions as production.

Scenario Setup Expected Rule
Same nights, single unit 50 guests book the same home for the same nights Exactly 1 booking created; 49 get 409 dates_unavailable; no 500 BR-AVL-01
Back-to-back 2 guests book [1, 4) and [4, 6) at the same time Both succeed BR-AVL-01
Last hotel room Room type with 1 unit left; 20 parallel requests for 1 room Exactly 1 success; counters held + booked <= total BR-AVL-02
Last seats on a departure 3 seats left; 10 requests for 2 seats each Exactly 1 success; seats booked = 2 BR-TRP-02
Host blocks while guest books Host blocks night N while a guest books a stay including N One wins; never both BR-AVL-04
Same idempotency key 10 identical requests with one key 1 booking; others get the same response or 409 request_in_progress BR-SYS-01
Double confirmation Host clicks accept twice; job tries to expire at the same time One transition wins; commission posted once BR-PAY-04, BR-BKG-06
Credit floor race Wallet just above the floor; 2 instant bookings at once whose commissions together cross the floor Second one becomes pending, never both confirmed below the floor BR-PAY-10
Duplicate top-up receipt 2 finance users record the same receipt at once 1 succeeds, 1 refused BR-PAY-07
Outbox workers 3 dispatchers on the same pending events Each event handled once (SKIP LOCKED); one SMS per event BR-SYS-03
Expiry vs accept Request accepted at the exact second the expiry job runs Final status is either confirmed or expired, consistent with ledger and counters BR-BKG-04
Ownership transfer Two owners-to-be at once Exactly one active owner BR-ORG-04

A scenario passes only if the database ends in a consistent state: a final check runs the ledger reconciliation and counter sums after each run.

5. Contract tests

Check How Fails when
Schema is valid manage.py spectacular --validate --fail-on-warn An endpoint has no documented serializer, an enum is unnamed, a response is undocumented
No accidental breaking change oasdiff breaking main.yaml pr.yaml A field is removed or renamed, a type changes, a required parameter is added, an enum value disappears, without the api-breaking label and a version plan
API matches its contract schemathesis run openapi.yaml --checks all --stateful=links against the API with seed data, authenticated as guest, host and each staff role A response does not match the schema, a 500 occurs, an undocumented status code appears, a response is slower than 5 s
Error format Custom schemathesis check Any 4xx body without code and message (BR-SYS-04)
Frontend compile check openapi-typescript generates schema.d.ts; tsc --noEmit in frontend/ and admin/ A Next.js call uses a removed field or a wrong type
Adapter parity For each migrated lib/data module, a test feeds the same fixture through the mock and the API adapter and compares DTO shapes The website or admin would render different data after the switch (07-architecture.md section 10.4)
Provider contracts Recorded responses (SMS, email, later Chargily) replayed against our client code Our parser or signature check breaks

6. Migration tests

Check When Tool
No missing migrations every push makemigrations --check --dry-run
Migrate from zero every push fresh database, migrate, then load production seeds 1 to 8 (05-database-schema.md section 9)
Dangerous operations every push migration linter: refuses column drops or renames in the same release as code changes, non-concurrent index creation on large tables, NOT NULL without default on existing tables
Data migrations per data migration django-test-migrations: build the old state, insert rows, migrate forward, assert the new state; run twice to prove it is safe to repeat
Old code on new schema before release run the previous release's API test suite against the new schema (expand-then-contract proof, 09-devops-hosting.md section 8.1)
Duration on realistic size before release with a risky migration apply on the performance dataset (section 7) and record the time and locks taken; above 10 s of locking needs a different plan
Constraints exist every push test queries pg_constraint and pg_indexes for the constraints in 05-database-schema.md section 6 (exclusion, partial unique, checks, triggers, grants)

7. Performance tests

Tool: k6 (scripts in tests/performance/). Locust is an acceptable alternative if the team prefers Python. Dataset: generated by factories at the scale in 05-database-schema.md section 7: 20,000 listings across 69 wilayas, 2,000 room types with 18 months of nights, 1 million booking rows, 5 million messages. Run against staging (same server size as production app node), never production.

Scenario Mix Load Pass criteria
S1 Browse and search search with filters (60%), search with dates (25%), map box (15%) ramp to 50 requests/s, hold 10 min p95 < 500 ms, errors < 0.5% (NFR-02)
S2 Listing detail and calendar detail + 90-day calendar 50 requests/s p95 < 300 ms (NFR-01)
S3 Booking create quote then book on random free dates (some collisions on purpose) 10 bookings/s for 5 min p95 < 600 ms; zero double bookings; conflicts return 409 (NFR-01, BR-AVL-01)
S4 Message polling 2,000 open conversations polling every 10 s about 200 requests/s p95 < 100 ms (query Q7)
S5 Notifications badge 5,000 signed-in users polling every 30 s about 170 requests/s p95 < 50 ms (query Q8)
S6 Mixed day 70% S1/S2, 20% S4/S5, 5% S3, 5% host and admin lists 50 requests/s for 30 min all targets above; no growth in outbox lag
S7 Abuse OTP request flood, oversized page sizes, deep pagination as fast as possible from 5 IPs limits return 429; API latency for normal users unchanged

Also: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) snapshots for queries Q1 to Q16 on the dataset, stored with the results and compared release to release; django-assert-num-queries style assertions in API tests to stop N+1 queries (each list endpoint has a fixed maximum number of queries).

8. Accessibility and i18n checks for API messages

Check How Rule
Every error code has text in en, fr, ar A test lists every DomainError code from a registry and checks a translation exists in each .po file NFR-06, BR-SYS-04
No missing translations CI runs makemessages and fails on a diff; compilemessages with errors as failures; no empty msgstr NFR-06
Stable codes Snapshot test of the error code list: removing or renaming a code is a breaking change (the apps map codes to text) NFR-13
Language selection API tests with Accept-Language: ar, fr, en, unknown, and none: correct language or fr fallback NFR-06
Latin digits Messages and notifications with numbers in Arabic contain digits 0 to 9, never Arabic-Indic digits NFR-06, research C.7
Arabic plurals Messages with counts use plural forms (Arabic has 6); test values 0, 1, 2, 3, 11, 100 NFR-06
Templates render Every notification template renders in the 3 languages with sample data, no missing variables, no raw HTML in SMS BR-NTF-02
SMS length SMS texts measured: Arabic texts use UCS-2 (70 characters per segment); critical SMS must fit in 2 segments cost, NFR-11
Bidirectional text Mixed Arabic text with Latin values (booking reference, amounts) wrapped with Unicode isolation marks in SMS and email NFR-06
Plain language Host-facing reason texts (reason_code.host_text_*) reviewed by a native speaker per language before release MOD-03
Apps The website and admin keep their Playwright + axe checks for screen readers and right-to-left layout; API messages are shown inside those flows NFR-13

9. Test data and factories

  • One tests/factories.py per app with factory_boy factories: UserFactory, HostAccountFactory (traits individual, agency, hotel, hostel, approved), ListingFactory (traits per vertical, published), RoomTypeFactory (with nights), TripDepartureFactory, BookingFactory (traits pending, confirmed, completed), WalletFactory (with a top-up posted through the ledger service, never by inserting balance rows).
  • Factories that involve money or inventory call services, so test data always satisfies the rules (no impossible states created by shortcuts).
  • Algerian realism: custom Faker providers for +213 mobiles (^\+213[5-7]\d{8}$), wilaya and commune ids from the geo seed, Arabic and Latin names, DZD amounts in centimes.
  • Determinism: fixed random seed per test run (printed in the output); time frozen with time-machine; UUIDv7 generated from the frozen clock.
  • Demo data for staging (website demo users Yacine, Amina, Karim; admin staff Nadia; 18 listings, 4 trips) is a separate seed_demo command built on the same factories; it refuses to run when BLADUS_ENV=production (05-database-schema.md section 9).
  • Never production data in tests. Bugs found in production are reproduced with factories.

10. Definition of Done

A change is done when:

  • The requirement ID (BKG-03) and rule IDs (BR-BKG-04) are in the pull request description.
  • Logic is in services or selectors, not in views, serializers or signals; import-linter passes.
  • Every new or changed business rule has a test named test_br_<area>_<nn>_... (section 13).
  • Money, refund or date logic has property tests; booking, inventory or ledger changes have a concurrency test.
  • Database rules are in constraints where possible, with a test that bypasses the service and expects the database to refuse.
  • Permissions: tests for allowed and denied roles (guest, other guest, host, other host, each org role or staff role concerned).
  • API: OpenAPI updated (generated), no unplanned breaking change, error codes translated in en, fr, ar.
  • Migrations follow the expand-then-contract policy and pass the migration checks.
  • Audit events and outbox events written where the rules require them.
  • No personal data in logs; new personal data fields added to the register of processing and the retention table (08-security-privacy.md section 12).
  • Coverage gates pass (section 11); CI fully green.
  • Docs updated if behaviour changed (rules, requirements, this blueprint); no em dash characters in docs.
  • Reviewed and approved by one other developer (two for ledger, security or migrations marked risky).
  • Deployed to staging and checked there; flag state documented if behind a feature flag.

11. Coverage targets

Scope Line coverage Branch coverage Note
services.py in all apps 90% 85% NFR-10
ledger, pricing, bookings (money and availability) 95% 90% Plus mutation testing (mutmut) on core.money, pricing, cancellation policy functions each quarter: target 80% of mutants killed
selectors.py 85%
apis.py and permissions 85% Every endpoint has at least one allow and one deny test
Whole backend 85% Trend must not go down more than 0.5 point per pull request

Coverage is a floor, not a goal: a test without meaningful assertions does not count in review.

13. Traceability: every rule has a test

Naming convention: the test function name starts with the rule ID in lower case with underscores, then a short description:

BR-PAY-04  ->  test_br_pay_04_commission_posted_once_per_booking
BR-AVL-01  ->  test_br_avl_01_parallel_same_nights_only_one_succeeds
BR-CAN-01  ->  test_br_can_01_moderate_policy_half_refund_from_4_to_1_days
BR-ACC-02  ->  test_br_acc_02_sixth_attempt_with_right_code_fails

A test that covers several rules carries extra markers: @pytest.mark.rules("BR-PAY-05", "BR-CAN-03"). Requirements can be tagged the same way (@pytest.mark.req("BKG-10")) for the NFR and requirement report.

Checker (tests/traceability/check_rules.py, run in CI):

  1. Reads every rule ID from 04-business-rules.md (pattern BR-[A-Z]+-\d{2}).
  2. Collects test names and rules markers with pytest --collect-only.
  3. Fails if a rule has no test, unless the rule is marked R2 or Later and listed in an allowlist file with a target release.
  4. Writes traceability.csv (rule, tests, files) as a CI artifact, so the product owner can see which tests protect which rule.

Example of the report:

Rule Tests Kind
BR-AVL-01 test_br_avl_01_exclusion_constraint_refuses_overlap_in_raw_sql, test_br_avl_01_parallel_same_nights_only_one_succeeds, test_br_avl_01_back_to_back_allowed DB, concurrency
BR-PAY-02 test_br_pay_02_unbalanced_transaction_fails_at_commit, test_br_pay_02_app_role_cannot_update_entries, test_br_pay_02_any_posting_sequence_balances DB, property
BR-CAN-02 test_br_can_02_example_8a_moderate_three_days_before service
BR-SYS-01 test_br_sys_01_same_key_same_body_returns_same_booking, test_br_sys_01_same_key_other_body_422, test_br_sys_01_concurrent_same_key_409 API, concurrency

Check yourself

  • Why do we never use SQLite for backend tests?
  • Give one property that must hold for every refund, whatever the policy and dates.
  • In the "same nights" concurrency test, what exactly must happen to the 49 losing requests?
  • What does schemathesis do that hand-written API tests do not?
  • How does the frontend find out at build time that an API field was removed?
  • What must a test for rule BR-REV-01 be called, at minimum?
  • Which performance scenario checks NFR-02, and what is its pass criterion?
  • Name three items from the Definition of Done that concern personal data or languages.

11. Roadmap: how we build the BLADUS backend

In plain words
This is the build plan, in eight steps (M0 to M7) up to the public launch, then Release 2 and "Later".
Each step has a goal, the requirement IDs it delivers, a test to know it is finished, what it waits for, and a rough length in weeks.
The two apps keep working on demo data the whole time: in each step, a few of their data files switch to the real API, one at a time, behind a switch we can turn back.
Some steps cannot finish without an answer from a lawyer or an accountant. Those answers are shown as gates at the step that needs them.
With 2 backend developers and 1 part-time frontend developer, the MVP takes about 29 weeks of work plus 2 weeks of buffer (about 7 months).

Terms used here (see glossary.md):

  • Milestone (M0 to M7): a block of work that ends with a check anyone can run ("exit criteria").
  • Exit criteria: the yes/no checks that say a milestone is done.
  • Gate: an outside answer (lawyer, accountant, bank, product owner) without which a milestone may not finish. Gate IDs (L1, F3, Q21...) come from 14-open-questions.md and are explained in 13-decisions-needed.md.
  • lib/data module: a file in the website (frontend/lib/data/) or admin (admin/lib/data/) whose functions read and write demo data today. "Switching" it means its function bodies call the API instead.
  • Feature flag (data source flag): a setting per module, for example DATA_SOURCE_LISTINGS=mock|api, read on the Next.js server. It lets us switch one module at a time and switch back in seconds if something breaks.
  • Staging: a copy of the system with demo data only, used for testing. Production: the real system with real people's data.
  • Closed beta: real hosts and guests, invited by us, before the public can sign up.
  • Gantt chart: a bar chart of tasks over time.

Inputs: 03-requirements.md (147 requirements), 04-business-rules.md, 05-database-schema.md, 01-system-inventory.md section 4 (the lib/data bridge), 02-research.md section E. The API contract is written in parallel in 06-api-design.md and openapi.yaml; operations, security and testing details in 07 to 10. The full requirement-to-milestone list is in traceability.md.

1. Assumptions

# Assumption If it is wrong
A1 Team: 2 backend developers full-time (Django, PostgreSQL), 1 frontend developer half-time (Next.js, switches the lib/data modules), a product owner who answers within 3 working days, and one of the backend developers acting as tech lead. With 1 backend developer, multiply backend durations by about 1.8.
A2 Work starts Monday 2026-11-16. Dates in the chart are targets, not promises. Shift every date by the delay.
A3 Ramadan 2027 (about 8 February to 9 March, VERIFY the exact dates) and the two Eids lower capacity; M3 and M4 are planned a little longer for this. Add 1 week if the team works reduced hours.
A4 The 147 requirements and DEC-001 to DEC-015 do not change much. New ideas go to R2 by default (risk K-21 in 12-risks.md). Re-plan at each milestone review.
A5 Staging runs on any cloud with demo data only. No real personal data exists anywhere until production is hosted in Algeria (gates L1, L2). Real data abroad may break Law 18-07 (VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL).
A6 The money model stays M1 (prepaid commission) for the MVP (DEC-001). Collecting guest money (M2 to M4) is a separate project behind a licence gate. A different model adds 6 to 10 weeks and a legal track.
A7 Each milestone ends with a 1-hour review: demo on staging, exit criteria checked, next milestone confirmed.

2. How the apps move from demo data to the API

  1. Every lib/data module gets one flag (DATA_SOURCE_<MODULE>), default mock. On staging we turn modules to api one at a time, in the order of section 4.
  2. The API is seeded with the same demo cast (Yacine, Amina, Karim, Nadia...) and the same IDs mapped to UUIDs (decision T3), so a module still on demo data can point at records that already live in the API.
  3. A module is "switched" when: its functions call the typed API client (NFR-08), every page that uses it passes the frontend smoke test, and the flag has been api on staging for 5 working days without a rollback.
  4. Once all modules of an app are switched and the launch is done, the demo store and flags are deleted (in M7 for production builds).
  5. The website's listings.ts switches as a whole in M2 against a simple search endpoint; M3 then upgrades that same endpoint (filters, facets, availability, map) without a frontend change. This keeps "one module, one switch".

4. Milestones in detail

M0. Foundations (3 weeks)

  • Goal: an empty but production-shaped backend: repository, CI, Django 6.1 + DRF + PostgreSQL/PostGIS + Redis + Celery (R-1), sign-up and sign-in that the website can use, the 69 wilayas, platform settings, and the shared conventions (money, time, IDs, errors, languages).
  • Scope: ACC-01, ACC-02, ACC-03, ACC-04, ACC-07, PAY-12, SRC-04, CFG-01, PRV-01, NFR-05, NFR-06, NFR-07, NFR-08, NFR-09, NFR-10, NFR-11, NFR-12, NFR-13.
  • Exit criteria:
    • CI runs lint, type checks, tests with coverage gate, dependency scan and OpenAPI generation on every pull request; main branch deploys to staging automatically.
    • A visitor signs up on the website (staging) with email or +213 phone, gets a code, verifies, signs in, signs out; the session token is revoked on logout (ACC-03).
    • 69 wilayas and 1,541 communes are seeded with source and valid_from (BR-SRC-02); a test counts them.
    • platform_settings v1 holds the default commission rates (1,200 / 1,500 / 1,800 / 1,000 bp) and request TTL 24 h.
    • Error envelope has stable codes and en/fr/ar messages; money helper and UUIDv7 helper have property tests.
  • Dependencies: decisions T1 (staging host only), T2, T3, T4, T8, T9; Q22 (foreign phone numbers) for ACC-01.
  • lib/data switches: website auth.ts (sign-up, sign-in, profile read). Website lib/algeria.ts static wilaya list replaced by the geography endpoint (same flag pattern).
  • Gates: none blocking. Start the lawyer engagement now (L1, L2, L4, L5, L9, L11 take months).

M1. Accounts, staff and host verification (5 weeks)

  • Goal: staff can sign in to the admin with 2FA and the right permissions; a user can become a host (individual or organisation), upload documents, and be verified by a moderator; organisations have teams.
  • Scope: ACC-05, ACC-06, ACC-08, ORG-01 to ORG-07, HST-01, HST-02, HST-03, HST-04, HST-06, NTF-04, MED-02, MOD-01, MOD-02, MOD-03, MOD-08, STF-01 to STF-05, CFG-02, CFG-04.
  • Exit criteria:
    • A staff member is invited, sets a password and TOTP, signs in; a guest session is refused on /api/v1/admin/* (STF-05).
    • Every staff mutation writes one audit_event; the app's database role cannot UPDATE or DELETE that table (test).
    • A user completes the 12-step individual flow and the 5-step agency flow served from the published config; the draft resumes on another browser.
    • Documents go to the private bucket; a moderator approves them one by one; the host is approved only when all required documents are approved (BR-HST-03).
    • Invitations can be accepted; an organisation always has exactly one owner (DB constraint test).
    • The outbox sends the invitation email through the worker with retries.
  • Dependencies: M0; T6 (object storage); a draft KYC document list per host type from L4 (the list is data, so the final list can change later without code).
  • lib/data switches (in this order): admin credentials.ts, team.ts, audit.ts, settings.ts, users.ts, onboarding.ts, hosts.ts, approvals.ts; website organizations.ts, then the onboarding part of auth.ts (updateUserHostStatus).
  • Gates: L4 draft answer expected by the end of M1 (soft). KYC files on staging are fake files only (A5).

M2. Catalogue, trips and moderation (4 weeks)

  • Goal: approved hosts create listings of every vertical and agencies create trips with departures; everything goes through review before publication; photos are processed safely.
  • Scope: ACC-09, HST-07, LST-01 to LST-08, LST-10, LST-11, LST-12, TRP-01, TRP-02, TRP-03, TRP-04, TRP-07, AVL-03, MED-01, MED-03, MOD-06, CFG-05.
  • Exit criteria:
    • An individual host can only create home and vehicle listings; an agency only experiences and trips; a hotel only its property (API and database trigger tests, DEC-014).
    • A submitted listing is pending_review; it appears publicly only after approval; editing a key field returns it to review via listing_revision.
    • Photos are uploaded directly to quarantine, re-encoded, stripped of GPS data; a home needs 5 photos (Q19).
    • Suspending a host pauses all its listings and trips (MOD-06).
    • The demo catalogue (18 listings, 4 trips) is re-created through the API on staging.
  • Dependencies: M1 (host accounts, moderation queues); decisions Q16 (hostel vertical), Q19 (minimum photos), Q24 (moderation staffing), Q28 (verticals at launch).
  • lib/data switches: admin categories.ts, listings.ts; website favorites.ts, listings.ts (as a whole, against a basic published-only search), vehicles.ts, experiences.ts, trips.ts, calendar.ts.
  • Gates: L5 (whole-home rental by individuals) should be answered before M7; if the answer is negative, the home vertical for individuals is switched off by setting, not by code.

M3. Search, availability and quotes (3 weeks)

  • Goal: guests find what is free on their dates, in Arabic, French or English, on a list or a map, and get a server-computed price.
  • Scope: TRP-05, AVL-04, PRC-01, PRC-02, PRC-03, PRC-05, SRC-01, SRC-02, SRC-03, SRC-05, SRC-06.
  • Exit criteria:
    • Search filters and facet counts match the mock's behaviour on the demo catalogue (the website's existing filter tests pass against the API).
    • Searching "تيزي وزو", "Tizi Ouzou" and "tizi-ouzou" returns the same top results (SRC-03, decision T7).
    • A quote lists nights, per-day prices, discount, cleaning fee, total in whole dinars, has an ID and expires after 30 minutes.
    • First performance run: search p95 measured on 20,000 generated listings (target 500 ms is enforced in M6).
  • Dependencies: M2; T7 (Arabic search approach); Q17 (one room type per booking).
  • lib/data switches: none new on the website (the listings.ts endpoint gets richer); admin network.ts and command-palette.ts (global search).
  • Gates: none.

M4. Bookings, cancellations and the commission wallet (5 weeks)

  • Goal: the heart of the product: instant and request bookings that can never double-book, cancellations by policy, and the prepaid commission wallet on a double-entry ledger (model M1).
  • Scope: HST-05, AVL-01, AVL-02, AVL-05, BKG-01 to BKG-10, CAN-01 to CAN-04, PAY-01, PAY-02, PAY-03, PAY-04, PAY-05, PAY-07, PAY-08, NTF-01, NTF-02.
  • Exit criteria:
    • Concurrency test on real PostgreSQL: 50 parallel requests for the same home and nights give exactly one booking; for a 3-room hotel room type, exactly 3 (AVL-01, AVL-02).
    • Same Idempotency-Key twice returns the same booking (BKG-10).
    • Expiry and completion jobs run on schedule, not on read (BKG-03, BKG-04).
    • Ledger property test: every transaction sums to zero; the worked examples of 04-business-rules.md section 9 give the exact centimes.
    • A finance staff member records a top-up with a receipt; the same receipt is refused a second time; above the threshold a second person must approve (Q15).
    • Booking confirmed, declined, expired and cancelled each produce an in-app notification and an email or SMS in the user's language.
  • Dependencies: M3; decisions Q14 (credit floor), Q15 (four-eyes threshold), Q18 (deposit withdrawals), Q20 (host cancellation penalty), Q25 (minimum first deposit), Q26 (reply window for agencies); accountant answers F5, F6, F7 (how deposits and commissions are recorded and receipted); bank or CCP account opened for host top-ups.
  • lib/data switches (in this order): website wallet.ts, reservations.ts, notifications.ts; admin ledger.ts, finance.ts, bookings.ts.
  • Gates: if Q18 says hosts may withdraw unused deposit, L3 must confirm this is not a payment service before the withdrawal flow is switched on (VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL). The rest of M4 does not wait.

M5. Messaging and reviews (3 weeks)

  • Goal: guests and hosts talk before and after booking, with contact details masked until confirmation; guests review completed stays; ratings come from real reviews.
  • Scope: REV-01, REV-03, REV-04, REV-05, MSG-01, MSG-02, MSG-03, MSG-04.
  • Exit criteria:
    • Messages sync by cursor; a phone number or CCP number typed before confirmation is masked for the other side (MSG-04).
    • A review is accepted only for a completed booking within 14 days, once (REV-01); listing rating changes after publication.
    • The admin can hide and restore a reported review with a reason.
  • Dependencies: M4 (completed bookings).
  • lib/data switches: website conversations.ts, reviews.ts; admin reviews.ts.
  • Gates: L1 and L2 must be answered by the end of M5 so the Algerian hosting contract (T1) can be signed and set up during M6. This is the most important date in the plan.

M6. Reports, privacy and hardening (3 weeks)

  • Goal: the admin can run the business (KPIs, exports), users can exercise their data rights, and the system meets its speed and safety targets.
  • Scope: STF-06, RPT-01, RPT-03, PRV-02, PRV-04, PRV-05, NFR-01, NFR-02.
  • Exit criteria:
    • Load test: reads p95 under 300 ms and booking create under 600 ms at 50 requests per second on one app node; search p95 under 500 ms with 20,000 listings.
    • A user downloads their data as JSON and asks for deletion; the profile is anonymised while bookings and ledger stay (BR-PRV-02).
    • Retention job deletes ID images 90 days after a decision (period confirmed by L7).
    • Breach runbook written and rehearsed once (5-day ANPDP clock), incident register exists (T5).
    • External security review (OWASP API Top 10) with no open high findings.
  • Dependencies: M5; L7 (retention periods), L8 (terms and privacy notice texts), L10 (foreign email/SMS providers), L12 (consumer-law checks on the booking flow); Q23 (launch date).
  • lib/data switches: admin analytics.ts; the KPIs and exports read real data. All modules of both apps are now on api on staging.
  • Gates: L7, L8, L10, L12 answered. Production hosting (T1) provisioned in Algeria during this milestone.

M7. Production in Algeria, closed beta, launch (3 weeks + 2 weeks buffer)

  • Goal: run in production in Algeria with real data, first with invited hosts and guests, then open to the public.
  • Scope: PRV-03, NFR-03, NFR-04 (plus the launch checklist below).
  • Exit criteria:
    • Production and its backups run in Algerian data centres; a restore drill from the second location meets RPO 15 min and RTO 4 h.
    • Production builds of both apps have no mock store and no demo passwords (fixes the current leak).
    • Closed beta: at least 30 real hosts (mix of the four host types, Q21 wilayas) verified, at least 50 real bookings, no double booking, no ledger mismatch in the daily reconciliation.
    • Support channels and on-call rota ready (Q27); status page and uptime monitoring active.
    • Legal checklist signed by the lawyer: L1, L2, L4, L5, L9, L11 cleared (VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL).
  • Dependencies: M6; Q21 (launch wilayas), Q23 (launch date), Q27 (support).
  • lib/data switches: none new; flags and demo stores are removed from production builds.
  • Gates: no real personal data before L1 and L2 are cleared and production is in Algeria.

R2-A. Online money: gateway, invoices, taxes (about 6 weeks, after launch)

  • Goal: hosts top up online by CIB or Edahabia through Chargily; BLADUS issues monthly commission invoices; quotes show tourist tax and VAT where they apply.
  • Scope: PRC-04, PAY-06, PAY-09, PAY-11.
  • Exit criteria: a test-mode top-up is credited only after a verified webhook, once per event; invoice numbers have no gaps per year; tax lines match the rates in settings.
  • Dependencies: launch; Chargily contract signed (start the paperwork during M6, lead time is long).
  • lib/data switches: website wallet.ts gets the top-up call (same flag); admin finance.ts invoices, settings.ts tax rates.
  • Gates: F1 (VAT rate on commission), F2 (taxe de séjour), F3 (gateway contract and amount units), F4 (invoice numbering and retention). VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL.

R2-B. Trust and growth (about 8 weeks, in parallel with R2-A)

  • Goal: disputes, host reviews of guests, risk flags, bulk moderation, coupons, featured listings, attachments, notification preferences, onboarding field editor, departure cancellation, foreign guest fields.
  • Scope: LST-09, TRP-06, BKG-11, REV-02, MSG-05, MSG-06, NTF-03, MOD-04, MOD-05, MOD-07, CFG-03, PRM-01, PRM-02, RPT-02, PRV-06.
  • Exit criteria: each requirement's acceptance sentence passes on staging; no MVP regression (full test suite green).
  • Dependencies: launch; one backend developer each for R2-A and R2-B.
  • lib/data switches: admin promotions.ts (last mocked admin module); admin messages pages get a new lib/data module (none exists today).
  • Gates: L6 (foreign guest declaration) before PRV-06.

LATER. Behind a legal or business gate (not scheduled)

  • Scope: PAY-10 (guest payments, escrow, host payouts: money models M2 to M4), AVL-06 (iCal sync).
  • Gate for PAY-10: L3 (is it a payment service under Règlement 25-02?) and either a PSP licence (160 million DA minimum capital, 02-research.md C.1) or a licensed partner bank. VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL. The ledger accounts already exist (BR-PAY-11); the work is mostly integration, reconciliation and payouts (estimate 8 to 12 weeks once the gate opens).
  • AVL-06: needs a new table and SSRF-safe fetching; schedule when hosts ask for channel managers.

12. Risks: what could go wrong, and what we do about it

In plain words
This is the list of things that could hurt BLADUS while we build and launch the backend: legal, money, fraud, technical, operations, team and scope.
Each risk gets two marks from 1 to 5: how likely it is, and how bad it would be. Multiplied, they give a score from 1 to 25.
Each risk has an owner (a role, not a name), what we do to reduce it, and the early sign that tells us it is happening.
The heat map at the end shows the dangerous corner at a glance. We review this list at every milestone review (11-roadmap.md).
Legal and tax points are engineering reading, not advice: VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL.

Terms used here (see glossary.md):

  • Risk register: a table of risks, kept up to date, with owners and actions.
  • Likelihood (L): 1 rare, 2 unlikely, 3 possible, 4 likely, 5 almost certain (during the MVP build and first 6 months after launch).
  • Impact (I): 1 small annoyance, 2 a few days lost, 3 a feature late or a few unhappy users, 4 launch delayed or money lost, 5 legal stop, data breach or loss of trust.
  • Score: L x I. 15 to 25 high, 8 to 14 medium, 1 to 7 low.
  • Mitigation: what we do now to make the risk smaller or less harmful.
  • Trigger / early signal: what we would see first if the risk starts to happen.
  • SMS pumping: fraud where bots request many one-time codes to numbers that earn the attacker money.
  • SIM swap: a criminal gets a victim's phone number moved to a new SIM card and receives their codes.
  • Exclusion constraint: a PostgreSQL rule that refuses two rows whose ranges overlap (used against double booking).
  • PSP: payment service provider, a licensed company allowed to hold and move other people's money.

Owner roles: PO product owner, TL tech lead, BE backend developers, FE frontend developer, LAW external lawyer, ACC external accountant, FIN BLADUS finance staff, MOD moderation lead, SUP support lead.

13. Decisions needed: who must decide what, and by when

In plain words
Building the backend needs some answers we cannot invent: product choices, legal checks, tax rules and technical picks.
This page lists every decision still open, grouped by who decides: you (product owner), a lawyer, an accountant or bank, and the tech lead.
For each one: the options, our recommendation, the milestone it blocks, and what happens if nobody decides.
Decisions already taken (DEC-001 to DEC-015) are repeated first so you can see the whole picture.
Legal and tax items are questions, not advice: VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL.

Terms used here (see glossary.md):

  • Decision: a choice that changes what we build. Once taken it gets a DEC number in 03-requirements.md section 2.
  • Deadline (blocks): the roadmap milestone (11-roadmap.md) that cannot finish without the answer.
  • Default: what we build if nobody answers by the deadline. Every default here can be changed later by a setting or a data change unless marked "costly to change".
  • Setting: a value in platform_settings that staff can change without new code.
  • PSP: payment service provider (a licensed company allowed to move other people's money).
  • ANPDP: Algeria's personal data protection authority.

IDs: Q (product) and L (legal) and F (finance) come from 14-open-questions.md. T (tech lead) items are new on this page.

Traceability matrix: requirement to rule, table, API, test and milestone

In plain words
One line per requirement (all 147 from requirements.csv).
Each line says which business rules it follows, which database tables hold its data, which API calls serve it,
where its tests will live, in which roadmap milestone it is built, and which app data module stops using demo data.
Use it to answer "if we change X, what else moves?" and "is everything planned somewhere?".
This page and traceability.csv are generated by python _tools/build_traceability.py. Edit the script, not the tables.

Terms used here (see glossary.md):

  • Traceability: being able to follow one need from the request, through the rules and the database, to the test that proves it.
  • Milestone: a block of build work with an exit test, defined in 11-roadmap.md.
  • API area: the family of web addresses (endpoints) the apps call. Final paths are in 06-api-design.md and openapi.yaml (tagged with x-requirements); names here are plain REST guesses.
  • job: a scheduled background task (Celery). internal: a service called by other code, with no public address.
  • lib/data module: the file in the website (web:) or admin (admin:) app whose functions switch from demo data to the API, behind a per-module flag.

15. Readiness verdict and first build prompt

In plain words
This page answers one question: can the team start building the Django backend now?
Short answer: yes, start the first milestone (M0, foundations) now, with three conditions.
Real customer data must wait for the lawyer's answers on hosting and data transfer (before the end of M5).
Collecting guests' money must wait for a payment licence decision (not in the first release).
At the end you will find the exact prompt to give a developer or an AI coding assistant to start M0.

Terms used here (see glossary.md):

  • Milestone (M0 to M7): a block of work of 3 to 5 weeks with clear "done" criteria (11-roadmap.md).
  • Gate: a decision or legal answer that must exist before a milestone can finish.
  • Readiness verdict: our judgement of whether the plan is complete enough to start coding.

Date: 2026-11-09.

1. Verdict

Area Status Evidence
What exists today is understood Ready 01-system-inventory.md: every feature, entity and lib/data function of both apps, 22 spec disagreements resolved by decisions
Product scope Ready 147 requirements, 126 in the first release (03-requirements.md); 15 product decisions taken (DEC-001 to DEC-015)
Business rules Ready Testable rules with state machines and worked money examples (04-business-rules.md)
Database design Ready 77 tables, 35 enumerations, 156 foreign keys, database-level guarantees against double booking and unbalanced money (05-database-schema.md, schema.dbml, schema.sql)
API contract Ready 266 operations, valid OpenAPI 3.1 (lint: 0 errors, 0 warnings), every website and admin data function mapped (06-api-design.md, openapi.yaml)
Architecture, security, hosting, testing Ready 07, 08, 09, 10
Plan, risks, decisions Ready 11 milestones, 32 risks, 49 decisions listed with owners and deadlines (11, 12, 13); traceability for all 147 requirements (traceability.md)
Legal and tax answers Not ready (not needed to start) L1 to L16 and F1 to F7 open; they gate production data (end of M5), payments (R2) and the licence question (later)

Verdict: GO for M0 now. GO for production launch only after the gates in section 3.

2. Conditions to start M0 (answer in the first week)

# Decision Recommended answer Who
1 T2: where the backend code lives backend/ folder in this repository Tech lead
2 T3 and T9: how the apps switch from demo data to the API, and the typed client One flag per lib/data module, API seeded with the same demo cast; openapi-typescript + openapi-fetch Tech lead
3 T4: how the Next.js servers hold the session allauth headless session token in an httpOnly cookie on the Next.js server Tech lead
4 Q22: guests without an Algerian mobile number Email code for non-Algerian numbers, with stricter booking limits Product owner
5 T1 (staging only) and T8 (third-party processors) Staging anywhere with demo data only; prefer Algerian or self-hosted services for anything with personal data Tech lead, then lawyer (L10)

And one action that cannot wait: engage a lawyer now for L1, L2, L4, L5, L9 and L11. Their answers take months and block production (M5 to M7).

4. Known gaps carried into the build

These are small and tracked; none blocks M0.

  • Two R2 features have no endpoint yet: staff broadcast messages (MSG-06) and the foreign-guest declaration (PRV-06). Design them when R2-B starts.
  • 18 requirements are jobs or quality targets and have no endpoint by nature (for example BKG-04 automatic completion, NFR-01 response times); they are covered by jobs (07-architecture.md) and tests (10-testing-quality.md). See the "no endpoint" rows in traceability.csv.
  • Someone who is both a solo host and an organisation member cannot yet reach their solo workspace from the website's workspace switcher (the API supports it: GET /api/v1/me/workspaces lists every host account, including the solo one).
  • Dates, costs and SMS prices are estimates; legal and tax points are research, not advice (VERIFY WITH A PROFESSIONAL).

5. First build prompt (M0)

Give this prompt, unchanged, to the developer or AI coding assistant who starts the backend. It is self-contained but expects the docs/backend folder to be in the repository.

You are starting the BLADUS backend (Algerian travel marketplace: homes, hotels,
hostels, experiences, vehicles, agency trips). The full blueprint is in
docs/backend/ of this repository. Read, in this order, before writing code:
00-START-HERE.md, 03-requirements.md, 04-business-rules.md,
05-database-schema.md, 06-api-design.md, 07-architecture.md,
08-security-privacy.md, 09-devops-hosting.md, 10-testing-quality.md,
11-roadmap.md (section M0), 13-decisions-needed.md (T1 to T4, T8, T9, Q22).

Goal: deliver milestone M0 "Foundations" exactly as defined in 11-roadmap.md:
requirements ACC-01, ACC-02, ACC-03, ACC-04, ACC-07, PAY-12, SRC-04, CFG-01,
PRV-01, NFR-05 to NFR-13. Nothing from later milestones.

Build:
1. A Django 6.1 project in backend/ (Python 3.13) with the folder layout of
   07-architecture.md. Create only the apps M0 needs: core, accounts, geo,
   config, audit, notifications (outbox only). Use the services/selectors
   pattern and import-linter layers from 07-architecture.md.
2. PostgreSQL 17 + PostGIS, Redis, Celery worker and beat, all in Docker
   Compose for local development (09-devops-hosting.md). Settings with
   pydantic-settings; no secrets in code.
3. Tables for M0 only, matching docs/backend/schema.dbml exactly (names,
   types, enums, constraints): user, consent_record, staff_profile,
   staff_permission, staff_role_permission, wilaya, daira, commune,
   platform_settings, audit_event, outbox_event, delivery_log, otp_send_log,
   idempotency_record. Money is BIGINT centimes + currency; IDs are UUIDv7.
4. Accounts with django-allauth headless (session tokens, email and phone
   one-time codes, rate limits of BR-ACC-01, BR-ACC-02, BR-ACC-05) and the
   /api/v1/auth/* and /api/v1/me endpoints exactly as in
   docs/backend/openapi.yaml (same paths, schemas, error codes).
5. Geography seed: 69 wilayas and 1,541 communes from
   el-amin-dev/algeria-wilayas-communes (CC0) with coordinates from
   ihahachi/Algeria-Cities (MIT), keeping source and valid_from columns
   (BR-SRC-02), plus the read endpoints in openapi.yaml.
6. platform_settings v1 with the defaults of 05-database-schema.md section 9
   (commission bp 1200/1500/1800/1000, request TTL 24 h) and the error
   envelope of 06-api-design.md (stable codes, en/fr/ar messages).
7. drf-spectacular generates the schema in CI; CI fails if the generated
   schema differs from docs/backend/openapi.yaml for the M0 paths.
8. Tests (10-testing-quality.md): pytest-django, factory_boy, hypothesis for
   the Money and UUIDv7 helpers, one test per business rule named
   test_br_<area>_<nn>_..., a test that counts 69 wilayas and 1,541 communes,
   and the auth flow end to end. Coverage gate as in 10-testing-quality.md.
9. GitHub Actions: ruff, mypy with django-stubs, pytest with a PostGIS
   service, dependency scan, OpenAPI check.
10. Website integration for M0 only: behind the flag DATA_SOURCE_AUTH
    (default mock), make frontend/lib/data/auth.ts call the API through a
    typed client generated with openapi-typescript + openapi-fetch, using the
    BFF pattern (allauth session token in an httpOnly cookie on the Next.js
    server). Do not change any other frontend module.

Rules: follow the decisions DEC-001 to DEC-015; do not invent endpoints or
columns that are not in openapi.yaml or schema.dbml (if something is missing,
stop and write it in docs/backend/14-open-questions.md); no personal data
outside demo fixtures; never use the em dash character in code comments or
docs; keep internal "darna" identifiers that already exist. Finish with: the
M0 exit criteria of 11-roadmap.md checked one by one, test results, and a
CHANGELOG entry in docs/backend/CHANGELOG.md.

Check yourself

  • Can the team start coding today? Which milestone, and what must be decided in the first week?
  • Which two legal answers must arrive before production hosting can be signed, and by when?
  • Why is collecting guests' money not part of the first release?
  • Which two R2 features still have no API endpoint?
  • In the first build prompt, what must the developer do if a column or endpoint they need is missing from the blueprint?

Persistence today: lib/data/* over in-memory globalThis arrays (lib/data/_store.ts:14, lib/data/_tables.ts:31-62) seeded from lib/mock-data/*; some tables are seeded inline inside lib/data (calendar.ts:13, wallet.ts:16, reviews.ts:6, credentials in auth.ts:39).
