4. Business rules found in code

4.1 Money and pricing (lib/booking/pricing.ts, lib/booking/config.ts)

Rule Value / formula Ref
Currency integer DZD; single rounding rule Math.round (roundDzd) pricing.ts:56-58
Price bounds (listing, room type, trip, date override) 100 to 10,000,000 DZD, integer config.ts:58-68; _sanitize.ts:20-25; actions/calendar.ts:71; actions/trips.ts:84
Pricing model selection room type -> per_bed_night if bookingUnit bed else per_room_night; experience -> per_person; vehicle -> per_day; trip -> per_traveller; else per_night pricing.ts:95-105
Home (per night) subtotal = sum over each night of (override[night] ?? listing.price) pricing.ts:233-253
Vehicle (per day) same loop as home, nights = days between pickup and return pricing.ts:233-253
Experience (per person) subtotal = (override[startDate] ?? listing.price) x guests; nights = 1 pricing.ts:193-208
Hotel room subtotal = roomTypePrice x rooms x nights; no per-date overrides pricing.ts:212-231
Hostel bed subtotal = bedPrice x beds x nights; beds default to guests pricing.ts:214-217; server forces beds = guests (actions/bookings.ts:115-118)
Trip subtotal = pricePerPerson x travellers; cleaning 0; tax 0 pricing.ts:256-274
Room type price basePrice ?? price pricing.ts:72-76
Room type default selection first room type when none or unknown id pricing.ts:85-93
Cleaning fee once per booking, listing.cleaningFee ?? DEFAULT_CLEANING_FEES[vertical] (all 0), 0 valid pricing.ts:183-186; config.ts:40-46
Guest service fee 0 for every vertical; per-listing serviceFeeRate override ignored on purpose config.ts:28-34; pricing.ts:125-130
Taxes round((subtotal + cleaning) x taxRate), taxRate = clamp(listing.taxRate ?? PLATFORM_TAX_RATE), platform rate 0 pricing.ts:148,188-191; config.ts:52
Total subtotal + cleaning + serviceFee + taxes pricing.ts:159
Average unit price stored as nightlyPrice round(subtotal / (nights x quantity)) pricing.ts:158; reservations.ts:284
Search card quote quoted on overlap range, cheapest room type, 1 unit, max(1, guests) lib/data/listings.ts:194-214
Approval mode for listing bookings request if listing.bookingApprovalMode === "request" OR listing.instantBook === false pricing.ts:276-282
Approval mode for trips organization.bookingApprovalMode === "request" actions/bookings.ts:190-193
Client totals are display only; server recomputes pricing.ts:1-5; actions/bookings.ts:136-145
Zero total rejected quote.total <= 0 -> INVALID_DATES actions/bookings.ts:145

4.2 Commission by host type

Rule Value Ref

4.3 Host payout (display formula, lib/booking/payout.ts:17-34)

  • subtotal = res.subtotal ?? max(0, total - cleaning - serviceFee - taxes).
  • declined / expired -> net 0, commission 0.
  • refunded = refund >= total ? subtotal + cleaning : min(subtotal + cleaning, refund).
  • net = max(0, subtotal + cleaning - refunded - commissionAmount).
  • Taxes never go to the host in the formula (they are excluded from subtotal and not added back). Service fee never goes to the host.
  • Used by HostBookingsClient.tsx:589,842. KPIs instead use gross totalPrice (lib/host-kpis.ts:36-40).

4.6 Approval modes and request expiry

  • Request TTL: REQUEST_TO_BOOK_TTL_HOURS = 24 (config.ts:55); expiresAt = createdAt + 24h (reservations.ts:296-299).
  • Pending requests hold inventory until expiry (lifecycle.ts:40-43), payment status pending.
  • Expiry is lazy: applied whenever reservations are read (reservations.ts:51-62, :105, :128); sets status=expired, paymentStatus=voided, respondedAt=expiresAt. No background job, no notification.
  • Approval mode exists at three levels: Listing.bookingApprovalMode + instantBook (used for listings), Organization.bookingApprovalMode (used for trips only), User.bookingApprovalMode (written, never read by the engine).

4.7 Reservation status transitions

From To Trigger Who Side effects Ref
(new) confirmed create on instant listing / trip guest paymentStatus paid; commission charged reservations.ts:273,291,336
(new) pending create on request listing / trip guest paymentStatus pending; expiresAt +24h reservations.ts:273,291,296
pending confirmed accept host or any org member paymentStatus paid; respondedAt; commission charged reservations.ts:439-443; actions/bookings.ts:270-283
pending declined decline (optional reason <= 500) host or any org member paymentStatus voided; respondedAt; commission reversal (none charged) reservations.ts:444-447

Not allowed: host cancel of pending (RESERVATION_NOT_CANCELLABLE), accept/decline of non-pending (REQUEST_NOT_PENDING / REQUEST_EXPIRED), guest cancel of completed/declined/expired/cancelled (RESERVATION_NOT_CANCELLABLE), guest cancel after check-in time (CHECK_IN_PASSED; for trips the cut-off is 00:00 on departure day, actions/bookings.ts:237).

4.8 Cancellation policies and refunds (lib/booking/cancellation.ts)

Policy Tiers (days before check-in -> refund % of subtotal) Ref
flexible >= 1 day: 100%; arrival day before check-in time: 50% :49-55
moderate >= 5 days: 100%; 1 to 4 days: 50%; arrival day: 0% :56-63
strict >= 14 days: 100%; 7 to 13 days: 50%; 0 to 6 days: 0% :64-71
  • Days before = calendar days between today in Algeria and startDate (:154-157).
  • Guest refund = min(total, round(subtotal x pct/100) + cleaningFee + round(taxes x pct/100) + (pct == 100 ? serviceFee : 0)) (:199-205). Cleaning fee always refunded in full. (The header comment at :14-15 says the cleaning share of taxes is always refunded; code prorates all taxes: minor mismatch, irrelevant while tax rate is 0.)
  • Payment status after refund: refund >= total -> refunded; > 0 -> partially_refunded; else paid (:139-143).
  • Policy snapshot: reservation.cancellationPolicy ?? listing ?? trip (actions/bookings.ts:233-236); default flexible (:74-81).
  • Host cancel / decline: always full refund (:217-239).
  • Refund is only a number on the reservation: there is no refund transaction, no payment provider call.

4.9 Wallet / ledger behaviour (lib/data/wallet.ts)

  • Prepaid commission deposit model: hosts top up offline (CCP, BaridiMob, bank wire); admin credits via rechargeWallet with a note and adminUserId (:290-329); messages hostWallet.json (howItWorksBody, creditedManually).
  • Commission deductions are negative transactions, reversals are positive adjustment transactions; balance = sum of amounts, recomputed on each append (:246-248, :369-379).
  • Balance may go negative (seed wal_casbah_hostel -4200, :173). UI warns that listings could be paused; no code pauses anything.
  • Append-only in practice (no edit or delete functions).
  • payout transaction type defined but never produced.

4.10 Ratings and reviews

  • Reviews are read-only seed data (lib/data/reviews.ts:6-102), 5 rows.
  • Summary: overall = mean of rating; categories = mean of positive values of cleanliness, accuracy, communication, location, value; null when no reviews (show "New") (lib/reviews.ts:15-26).
  • Listing rating / reviewCount, org rating / reviewCount, trip rating / reviewsCount are stored numbers unrelated to the review rows (e.g. lst_tipaza_villa reviewCount 48 vs 2 rows).
  • Hotel UI relabels categories (communication = staff, value = value for money) (HotelHostelDetailClient.tsx:72).
  • No rule on who may review (no reservation link), no review window, no host response.
  • Search minRating filter compares stored rating (searchFacets.ts:374).

4.11 Favorites

  • Listing ids on User.favoriteIds; set semantics (lib/data/auth.ts:182-194).
  • Adding requires the listing to exist (any status), removing does not (actions/favorites.ts:13).
  • Optimistic UI with shared in-memory cache keyed by user (hook/useFavorite.ts:16-27).
  • Trips cannot be favorited (toast only).

4.12 Messaging

  • One conversation per (2 participants, subject) where subject = listing id or trip id or null (conversations.ts:112-137).
  • Recipient for org listings and trips = organization ownerUserId (not the team, not the listing creator) (actions/messages.ts:67-74).
  • Cannot message yourself (OWN_LISTING_MESSAGE); listing/trip must be public.
  • Text trimmed, 1 to 4000 chars (actions/messages.ts:30).
  • unreadCount[receiver] += 1 on send (only if the map exists), reset to 0 on read; messages read=true for receiver (conversations.ts:88-106).
  • lastMessage / lastMessageAt denormalized on the conversation.
  • No link between a reservation and a conversation; booking guestMessage is stored on the reservation only, not posted to the inbox.

4.13 Notifications

  • Per user, mark one (ownership checked) or all read (lib/data/notifications.ts).
  • No producer: booking created/confirmed/declined/expired/cancelled, new message, org verification do not create notifications. Types price and review imply price-drop alerts and review prompts that do not exist.
  • Stored English title / message text (not i18n keys).

Host type Creates Rules Ref

Permission owner admin manager

canEditSettings yes yes no

canChangeRoles yes no no
canTransferOwnership yes no no
canDeleteOrganization yes no no
  • Only the owner can grant admin on invite (actions/organizations.ts:105-108).
  • Owner role cannot be changed through role change (OWNER_ROLE_LOCKED), owner cannot be removed.
  • Transfer: target must be active with userId; all current owners demoted to admin; org.ownerUserId updated (organizations.ts:220-236).
  • Duplicate invite check by email among non-removed members (actions/organizations.ts:109-112).
  • Delete org: owner only, typed name must equal org name; memberships deleted; listings and trips set to draft; deleting user's organizationId cleared and session refreshed (actions/organizations.ts:72-88; organizations.ts:274-282). Other members keep hostType of an org type with no org and will be sent back to onboarding.
  • Ops actions (updateMyListingAction, deleteMyListingAction, calendar, respondToReservationAction, trip status/delete) check ownership only, not role, consistent with canManageOperations.
  • Trips are agency-only (AGENCY_ONLY, actions/trips.ts:73-78).

4.16 Search filters semantics

Base search (lib/data/listings.ts:18-218): active only; vertical=hotel matches businessCategory hotel/hostel, category hotel, or type containing "hotel"/"hostel"; vertical=home excludes hotels/hostels; category substring on type/amenities; destination substring on city, locationValue, country; minPrice/maxPrice on base price (not quoted total); guests filter only when > 1 and only on guestCount (listings without it pass); dates as in 4.4. instantBook in SearchParams is ignored by the data layer. Trips: destination substring on title/city/locationValue (trips.ts:34-42).

Side filters (components/search/searchFacets.ts), applied in-process on the base pool, same code client and server:

4.17 Algeria geography (lib/algeria.ts)

  • 58 wilayas with official codes incl. 2019 reform (49 to 58), French/Latin name, optional English (Alger -> Algiers), Arabic name (:14-73).
  • 13 communes with wilaya code (:81-95), "extend as hosts add places".
  • locatePlace: explicit commune first, else split city on &, ,, /, " et ", " and " and match commune or city->wilaya map (:97-155).
  • Wilaya filter accepts 1..58 (searchFacets.ts:278).

4.18 Auth and session

  • scrypt N default, 16-byte salt, 64-byte key, format scrypt$salt$hash (lib/data/auth.ts:18-36); timing-equalized unknown email (:46-47,76).
  • Password min length 8, no other complexity (lib/auth/password-rules.ts:2).
  • Cookie darna_session: HMAC-SHA256, httpOnly, SameSite lax, secure in production, 30 days, secret DARNA_SESSION_SECRET >= 32 chars (dev fallback secret) (lib/auth/session-token.ts:15-49,159-168).
  • Logout revokes sid in an in-memory map (lib/server/session.ts:22-32,109-116).
  • Open-redirect guard for callbackUrl (lib/auth/callback-url.ts:11-23).
  • CSRF: JSON content type + Origin host match for auth routes; server actions rely on Next's origin check (lib/server/request-guard.ts).
  • No rate limiting, no lockout, no email verification, no password reset.

Notes:

  • Finance has hosts.commission_override but NOT listings.view or users.view (lib/permissions.ts:71-82).
  • Support can refund and resolve disputes but cannot see wallets, so it cannot see the ledger effect of its own refunds.
  • resolveDispute with a refund outcome needs bookings.dispute AND bookings.refund (lib/actions/bookings.ts:36-38, lib/data/bookings.ts:291-292): only super_admin and support qualify.
  • Role labels: lib/permissions.ts:107-113.
  • Permissions are resolved from the CURRENT role in the store on every request (lib/auth/current-admin.ts:44-59), never from JWT claims. AdminUser.permissions? (lib/types/index.ts:137) exists but is unused (no per-user overrides).

Generator file comments say ">= 125 hosts", ">= 420 listings" etc. Actual loop bounds: 320 / 128 / 430 / 840 / 330 / 1550 / 215 / 14.

3. Function inventory: lib/data/* and lib/actions/*

Conventions:

  • Every lib/data function is server-only; every lib/actions function is "use server" and wraps the data call in runAction(permission, fn) (lib/auth/run-action.ts:24-45) which returns {ok,data}|{ok:false,code} with codes unauthenticated|forbidden|invalid|conflict|failed.
  • Read functions in lib/data do NOT call assertCan; protection relies on the action or on guardPage in the calling server page. Mutations call assertCan(actor.role, perm) again (defense in depth).
  • All mock functions await delay(100..200ms).
  • "Audit" column = calls logAudit/logExport.

4.3 Wallet recharge (lib/data/finance.ts:205-245, lib/actions/finance.ts:46-66)

  • Perm wallets.recharge; amount int 1..10,000,000; receiptReference required (trimmed, <=200 chars); method free string <=100 (UI sends values from PaymentsClient select or hardcoded ccp_transfer in HostsClient :411); reason free string, no minimum.
  • Writes wallet_recharge entry with description Admin manual recharge (<method>): <reason>, adminActor = actor NAME.
  • No idempotency: same receipt reference can be credited twice; no duplicate check, no four-eyes approval.
  • Audit WALLET_RECHARGE with balance before/after and txId.

4.4 Payouts (lib/data/finance.ts:281-385)

Step Rule
List pending first then newest (:287-291), no paging
Approve perm payouts.approve; only from pending (findPendingPayout :295-303); host must exist; amount positive int; refuse if getHostBalance < amount with "Insufficient wallet balance" DomainError (:322-327); writes host_payout -amount; sets status approved, processedAt, processedBy (name), transactionId (:335-342)
Double-debit protection status check + balance check + ledger write + status write in one synchronous block (:315-343); second call fails because status is no longer pending. No idempotency key, no DB lock (mock only).
Confirmation UI confirm dialog payoutToApprove, busy flag prevents double click (PaymentsClient.tsx:356-376)
Reject from pending only, reason >=3 chars, no ledger movement (:359-385)
processed type value exists; no code transitions approved -> processed (no bank-confirmation step)
Seed 14 requests; 2 of the 9 pending deliberately exceed balance (generator.ts:613-620)
Account display masked last 4 of ccpRip ?? rib ?? phone (DATA-MODEL s4)

4.5 Bookings, cancellations, refunds, disputes (lib/domain/transitions.ts:13-51, lib/data/bookings.ts)

  • BOOKING_TRANSITIONS: pending -> confirmed|cancelled; confirmed -> completed|cancelled|disputed|refunded; completed -> disputed|refunded; disputed -> confirmed|completed|refunded; cancelled -> refunded; refunded -> none (transitions.ts:13-20). Only cancel, refund and dispute-resolution transitions are reachable from the admin; confirm/complete/dispute-open are not.
  • Cancel: allowed from pending/confirmed, reason >=3; sets cancelledAt; no automatic refund, no ledger reversal (bookings.ts:165-197).
  • Refundable statuses: confirmed, completed, cancelled, disputed; payment must be paid or partially_refunded; remaining = total - refundedSoFar (transitions.ts:32-45).
  • Refund: int DZD, 0 < amount <= remaining; cumulative refundedAmountDzd; full -> status refunded + payment refunded, else payment partially_refunded (bookings.ts:205-249).
  • Host clawback: hostShare = round(amount * hostPayoutDzd / totalAmountDzd) written as negative booking_refund (bookings.ts:225-237). Platform keeps the commission share of a refund implicitly (commission never reversed).
  • Dispute resolve: only from disputed; note >=3 required; refund_full refunds remaining -> refunded; refund_partial requires amount < remaining -> back to completed if checkout passed else confirmed; declined no money -> lifecycle status; stores disputeResolution (bookings.ts:284-346).
  • Saved view "pending > 24h": status=pending && createdAt < now-24h (bookings.ts:72-78). Matches frontend REQUEST_TO_BOOK_TTL_HOURS = 24 (frontend/lib/booking/config.ts:55) but admin never expires anything.
  • Escrow (finance KPI): sum of total - refunded for confirmed/disputed paid bookings (finance.ts:443-448).
  • No idempotency on refunds: two concurrent identical refund calls in a real DB would both pass without a lock.

4.6 Host state machine (lib/domain/transitions.ts:55-71, lib/data/hosts.ts:221-302)

Action From To Reason Perm Audit
approve applied, under_review, rejected approved (+verification verified) no hosts.approve HOST_APPROVE
reject applied, under_review rejected yes hosts.reject HOST_REJECT
suspend approved suspended yes hosts.suspend HOST_SUSPEND
unsuspend suspended approved no hosts.suspend HOST_UNSUSPEND
ban approved, suspended, rejected, under_review, applied banned yes hosts.delete HOST_BAN
delete any except deleted deleted, stores statusBeforeDelete no hosts.delete HOST_DELETE
restore deleted statusBeforeDelete or under_review no hosts.delete HOST_RESTORE
  • No transition applied -> under_review (no "start review" action). Banned is terminal except via delete/restore.
  • Reasons appended to Host.adminNotes as text (hosts.ts:269-278).
  • Approve sets verification to verified without touching documents[].status.
  • Suspending/banning a host does NOT cascade to its listings or open bookings.
  • A second, contradictory transition table exists in lib/status.ts:58,68 (HOST_TRANSITIONS, LISTING_TRANSITIONS) that differs from lib/domain/transitions.ts (e.g. allows deleted -> approved|suspended, banned -> suspended). Only lib/domain/transitions.ts is enforced.

4.7 Listing state machine (lib/domain/transitions.ts:73-109, lib/data/listings.ts:233-387)

  • Transitions: draft -> pending_review|deleted; pending_review -> approved|changes_requested|rejected|deleted; changes_requested -> pending_review|approved|rejected|deleted; approved -> suspended|archived|changes_requested|pending_review|deleted; rejected -> pending_review|deleted; suspended -> approved|pending_review|deleted; archived -> approved|deleted; deleted -> only restoreListing (:83-93).
  • Reason (>=3 chars, MIN_REASON_LENGTH) required for rejected, suspended, changes_requested (:102-112); appended to adminNotes.
  • Permission by target: rejected -> listings.reject; suspended/archived -> listings.suspend; deleted -> listings.delete; anything else (approved, pending_review, changes_requested, draft) -> listings.approve (listings.ts:233-245).
  • Legacy aliases accepted on read and filter (matchListingStatus :39-66), folded on write.
  • Feature: only approved listings can be featured; unfeature always allowed (listings.ts:360-362). Featuring is a boolean only (no placement, no period, no ordering, no price).
  • Approval queue only picks literal pending_review (approvals.ts:33), not legacy pending.

4.8 Reviews (lib/data/reviews.ts)

  • No state machine: hide/restore/delete/dismiss can be applied from any status (e.g. restore a deleted review to published). No reason captured. Flags are a single flagReason string on the review (no flag entity, no reporter list). hostReply is display only.

4.9 Guests (lib/data/users.ts)

  • No state machine; updateUserStatus can move any status to any status; reason optional/empty for suspend and ban (action uses str, not reason, actions/users.ts:26-36). pending status exists but nothing explains its meaning.

Queue Source rows waitingDays from Priority rule Line
hosts status applied or under_review joinedAt high if >3 days 12-30
listings status pending_review createdAt (not submission time) high if >4 days 32-50
documents Host.documents[].status == pending uploadedAt high if >3 days 52-72

waitingDays = max(1, floor((now - t)/1 day)); sorted oldest first (:126-127). No low priority produced. No assignment/claiming, no SLA breach timestamps.

5.4 Guest-site counterpart (frontend/lib/onboarding-config.ts, frontend/types.ts:507-572)

Aspect Admin Frontend
Container OnboardingConfig.flows[hostType].steps + global version Record<HostType, OnboardingStepConfig[]>, optional HostTypeOnboardingConfig {hostType, steps, updatedAt?}
Storage server mock store hardcoded defaults + browser localStorage key darna_onboarding_config_<hostType> (onboarding-config.ts:1064-1091)
Step count individual 2, agency 1, hotel 1, hostel 1 individual 12 (:5-430), agency 5 (:433-605), hotel 7 (:607-840), hostel 7 (:842-1062)
Step ids step_ind_1, step_ag_1, ... , UI step_<ms> category_vertical, placement, location, ..., agency_basics, hotel_basics, hostel_basics; custom steps must start with custom_step_
Step required props stepNumber?, title?, isActive? optional stepNumber, title, isActive required
Field id id? or key? id required, order and required required
Field types text, textarea, number, select, multiselect, radio, file, location, amenities, boolean text, number, textarea, select, multi-select, image-upload, toggle
Field defaultValue absent present
Consumption none BecomeHostFlow.tsx:189 calls getOnboardingSteps(hostType); renders extra non-core fields of a step matched by step id (:192-200) and fully renders only custom steps whose id starts with custom_step_ (:2387-2389); progress bar counts isActive steps (:1035-1038)

Consequences for a shared backend:

  1. Admin-published steps would not match any frontend step id, so the guest wizard would ignore them except for the progress count; admin-created steps (step_<ms>) are never rendered because the prefix is not custom_step_.
  2. The admin "individual max 2 pages" rule contradicts the frontend 12-step individual flow.
  3. Field types need a canonical enum + mapping (multiselect/multi-select, file/image-upload, boolean/toggle; radio, location, amenities have no frontend renderer). docs/DATA-MODEL.md s5 documents the mapping.
  4. Core vs custom fields: frontend skips isCore fields and BUILT_IN_FIELD_IDS, i.e. the config can only ADD custom fields to built-in steps; it cannot reorder/remove built-in steps. Admin UI implies it can.
  5. Recommended contract: GET /api/v1/onboarding-config/{hostType} returns {hostType, version, publishedAt, steps:[{id, stepNumber, title{en,fr,ar}, description, isActive, isCore, fields:[{id, type, label, required, order, options?, placeholder?, helpText?, defaultValue?}]}]} with a per-host-type version; custom answers stored as JSON on the host application (custom_fields), validated server-side against the published version id the host started with.

2. Disagreements (spec vs frontend vs admin)

No winner is picked. "Impact" = what the backend has to decide.

ID Topic Spec says Frontend does Admin does Impact on backend design
D-1 Who is a host hostType on User; org types use Organization (DS 2.1) Single User.hostType + active org in session; same person can own an individual wallet and orgs (frontend/types.ts:10, frontend/lib/server/session.ts:68-75) One Host row per provider with hostType, optional organizationId (admin/lib/types/index.ts:255-280) Need a canonical "host account" (user-as-host vs organization) that both apps key wallets, listings, commission and moderation on. Decide whether one user can be individual host and org member at once.
D-2 Commission default rates Per type, values not given (DS 9.3) 12 / 15 / 18 / 10 (frontend/lib/booking/config.ts:15-20) Same values, duplicated (admin/lib/pricing.ts:19, plus hardcoded defaultRate in admin/lib/data/analytics.ts:69-74) One platform_settings row; analytics must read it, not constants.
D-3 Commission base "booking total x rate" (DS 9.3 l.153) Accommodation subtotal only, excl. cleaning and taxes (frontend/lib/data/reservations.ts:376-379) base x rate where base = price before fees (admin/lib/pricing.ts:76-90); no cleaning fee concept Pick one base; store commissionBase, commissionRate, commissionAmount on the booking at confirmation time.
D-4 Commission timing and reversal On every confirmed booking (DS 9.3) On confirm; reversed fully on decline, pro-rata on guest cancel, fully on host cancel (reservations.ts:417-447, wallet.ts:446-476) No automatic deduction; refunds write a proportional negative booking_refund (admin/docs/DATA-MODEL.md section 3) Ledger posting rules per booking event (confirm, cancel, refund, dispute) must be specified once.
D-5 Per-host commission override Not specified (per type only) Not supported Supported, audited (admin/lib/data/hosts.ts:332-364) Rate resolution order needed: host override, then type rate. Snapshot the rate on the booking.
D-6 Approval-mode storage Default on User/Org, optional per-listing override (DS 3) Listing decides (bookingApprovalMode and legacy instantBook, pricing.ts:276-282); User value derived from first listing; Org value used only for Trips (bookings.ts:190-193) Host.bookingApprovalMode (admin/lib/types/index.ts:274) plus a platform switch instantBookingPlatformWide (admin/lib/mock-data/store.ts:102) the frontend never reads Define resolution: platform switch, then listing override, then owner default. Drop one of instantBook / bookingApprovalMode.
D-7 Who can approve a request Host, or org member "with permission" (DS 3) Any active member, any role (frontend/lib/host-types.ts:19, frontend/lib/server/authz.ts:25-35) Admin can move pending -> confirmed (admin/lib/domain/transitions.ts:11) Need an explicit permission (e.g. bookings.respond) per org role, and whether staff may confirm on behalf of a host.
D-8 Request expiry "within a reasonable window" (DS 3) 24 h TTL, lazy expiry on read, payment voided (frontend/lib/booking/config.ts:55, lifecycle.ts:12-16) No expired status at all (admin/lib/types/index.ts:413-419) Need a scheduled job (not lazy-on-read) so expiries also fire notifications and appear in admin. TTL should be a setting.
D-9 Booking statuses pending, confirmed (DS 3) pending, confirmed, cancelled, completed, declined, expired (frontend/types.ts:198-204) pending, confirmed, cancelled, completed, disputed, refunded (admin/lib/types/index.ts:413-419) Union state machine needed: e.g. keep declined/expired, add disputed; model refunded as payment status, not booking status (the frontend already does).
D-10 Listing statuses and moderation Not specified; trips "live immediately" (DS 5.2) active, pending, suspended, draft; new listings and trips go live at once (frontend/lib/data/listings.ts:309, frontend/app/actions/trips.ts:67) 8 canonical statuses with review queue (admin/docs/DATA-MODEL.md section 1) Decide if publish requires approval. If yes, frontend create must write pending_review.
D-11 Trips model Separate Trip type owned by an agency (DS 5.1) Separate Trip table; reservation has tripId and reuses listingId = trip.id (reservations.ts:349); departures are a string array Trips are Listing rows with category: "trip" moderated like listings (admin/app/[locale]/(panel)/trips/TripsListClient.tsx:82,155) Choose: dedicated trips + trip_departures tables, or listings with a trip subtype. Reservation needs a proper polymorphic target (listing / room type / trip departure). Also rename the guest /trips page or the API resource to avoid the "Trips" collision.
D-12 Verticals 4: Homes, Experiences, Vehicles, Trips; hotels are "Homes-like" (DS 5.3, 8) 5 including hotel in the type, but hotels are created as category: "home" with businessCategory (frontend/types.ts:47-52; BecomeHostFlow.tsx:759,860) 5 with hotel as a real vertical (admin/lib/types/index.ts:300) Analytics "by vertical" will double-count or miss hotels unless one rule is fixed.
D-13 Onboarding field types and schema text, number, select, multi-select, image-upload, toggle (DS 7.1) Same as spec + textarea (frontend/types.ts:507-514) multiselect, file, boolean, radio, location, amenities + others; different key names (admin/lib/types/index.ts:603-650) One JSON schema for onboarding_flows with versioning; mapping table already in admin/docs/DATA-MODEL.md section 5.
D-14 Individual onboarding length 12 steps; "2 pages" applies to the host interface, not onboarding (DS 4.1, 7.1) 12 steps (frontend/lib/onboarding-config.ts) Capped at 2 steps, enforced on save (admin/lib/data/onboarding.ts:23-26, admin/README.md section 6) Admin rule likely misreads DS 4. If kept, the frontend flow cannot be config-driven from admin without losing 10 steps.
D-15 Onboarding config source of truth Admin config drives live flows (DS 7.2) Defaults + browser localStorage (frontend/lib/onboarding-config.ts:1064-1091) In-memory store, versioned (admin/lib/data/onboarding.ts) Backend must serve the published flow per host type; custom field answers need storage (e.g. JSONB on listing/org application).
D-16 Wallet model Prepaid: host pays platform offline, admin recharges, commission deducted (DS 9.2) Prepaid commission wallet only (frontend/lib/data/wallet.ts) Mixed: also booking_payment credits (host earnings) and host_payout debits (admin/lib/mock-data/generator.ts:492-501), i.e. an escrow/payout wallet Fundamental: does BLADUS collect guest money (escrow, payouts) or not (prepaid commission)? Determines payment integration, ledger accounts and payout flow. The spec itself is mixed: DS 3 "guest completes payment" vs DS 9.2 offline recharge.
D-17 Recharge input Amount + optional note (DS 9.2) rechargeWallet takes amount + note, any amount (frontend/lib/data/wallet.ts:290-327, admin-only, no caller) Receipt reference required; integer 1..10,000,000; method field (admin/lib/data/finance.ts:205-219) Adopt admin validation; keep adminUserId as an id, not a display name (admin stores adminActor name).
D-18 Transaction type names recharge / commission_deduction / payout (DS 9.1) Same + adjustment wallet_recharge / host_payout / booking_payment / booking_refund + commission_deduction, adjustment Single enum; commission reversal is adjustment in frontend vs booking_refund share in admin.
D-19 Room type fields "inventory count and availability" (DS 2.1) totalInventory, inventoryCount, availableInventory, basePrice, price (frontend/types.ts:92-108) totalInventory, availableInventory (admin/lib/types/index.ts:316-329) Keep one inventory column; availability is computed from bookings and blocks, not stored.
D-20 Hero switcher 4 segments (DS 5.3) 5 (Hotels added) n/a Search API must support a hotel vertical filter or a businessCategory filter consistently.
D-21 Trip creation steps 6 incl. cancellation step (DS 5.2) 5 (TripCreationClient.tsx:56-58) Admin trip wizard separate Minor; affects only validation order.
D-22 Analytics tabs Overview / By Host Type / By Vertical / Financial (DS 8) n/a overview / providers / services / wilayas / revenue / reports (StatsClient.tsx:36) Reporting API should expose dimensions (host type, vertical, wilaya, period) rather than fixed pages.

3. Policy change: no guest service fee, brand BLADUS

Current policy (confirmed in code): guests pay no platform fee; BLADUS earns only the host commission. Evidence: frontend/lib/booking/config.ts:22-34 (SERVICE_FEE_RATES all 0), frontend/lib/booking/pricing.ts:125-130 (per-listing override ignored), admin/lib/pricing.ts:14-16 (GUEST_SERVICE_FEE_PERCENT = 0). Brand is BLADUS; internal darna identifiers are intentionally kept (cookies darna_session, env DARNA_SESSION_SECRET, storage key darna_onboarding_config_, global store keys __darna_wallets__).

4. Usability-report findings that imply backend requirements

Source: docs/backend/_sources/usability-report.md (identical to admin-usability-report.md). The report describes the admin console as tested; several claims are UI-only in the code, so each one becomes a backend requirement.

# Report claim (section) Current code Backend requirement
U1 "Needs your attention" cards with counts and "oldest item has been waiting 2 days" (section 3) Counts are real (admin/lib/data/analytics.ts:161-203); oldest-waiting values are hardcoded 3/2/1 days (admin/app/[locale]/(panel)/DashboardClient.tsx:177-216) Queue endpoint returning count + oldestCreatedAt per queue (hosts, listings, flagged reviews, disputes, negative wallets, expiring requests). SLA timers need indexed submittedAt on each moderated entity.
U2 8-second Undo toast after approve / hide review (sections 2.1 task 7, 4.3) Undo only shows a toast "undo requested" (admin/app/[locale]/(panel)/approvals/ApprovalsClient.tsx:286-290) Reversible actions: either a delayed commit window or an inverse transition endpoint, both audited. Transition tables must allow the reverse move.
U3 Bulk approvals with progress "Approving 4 of 12" (section 4.3) Sequential client loop, no progress, partial failure leaves mixed state (ApprovalsClient.tsx:342-358) Bulk endpoint with per-item results, idempotency keys, and one audit entry per item.
U4 Live result counts "14 listings match in Oran"; hotels by wilaya (tasks 11, 12) Admin list functions return {rows,total,facets} from in-memory filtering (admin/lib/data/listings.ts:68-210, admin/README.md section 4) Server-side filtering, pagination and facet counts (wilaya, host type, status, price range) on indexed columns. Exports must cover the full filtered set (already the rule, admin/docs/DATA-MODEL.md section 8).
U5 Reject host with pre-set reasons; host "notified politely" (task 2) Reason required (>= 3 chars) per DATA-MODEL section 1-2; no notification is sent from admin to frontend (admin/lib/data/hosts.ts has no notify call) Reason catalogue table, and a notification/outbox service shared by both apps (email/SMS/in-app).
U6 Request changes on a listing with checkbox templates (task 4) changes_requested exists only in admin; frontend shows it as pending (admin/docs/DATA-MODEL.md section 1) Host-facing change-request object (items + notes) readable by the frontend, plus resubmission transition.
U7 Restore a deleted item (task 6) Soft delete with statusBeforeDelete in admin; frontend hard-deletes listings (frontend/lib/data/listings.ts:343-347) Soft delete everywhere (deletedAt, statusBeforeDelete), since admin restore cannot work on hard-deleted rows.
U8 Booking dispute with guest claim and host response side by side (task 8) Admin disputed state and outcomes; frontend has no dispute state or way to file one (D-9) Dispute entity with both parties' statements and attachments, created from the guest/host app.
U9 Recharge modal shows current and new balance (task 9) Admin computes from ledger (admin/lib/data/finance.ts:221-244) Balance read must be consistent with the write (transactional ledger insert with balanceAfter), and the frontend wallet must be the same ledger.
U10 Change commission rate in "Money > Commission tiers" (task 10) Admin store only; frontend has its own rates store (frontend/lib/data/wallet.ts:239-266) One shared settings table; rate snapshot on each booking.
U11 Edit onboarding steps with toggles and drag handles (task 13) Admin-only effect (R49) Published onboarding flow served to the frontend; versioned (see D-15).
U12 4 KPI cards with % change vs last month (section 3) Trends are hardcoded strings (admin/lib/data/analytics.ts:43-50) Period-over-period aggregates over real date ranges (materialized views or nightly rollups).
U13 "History of actions" (audit log) trusted (section 4.2) Server-side actor and IP, frozen entries (admin/docs/DATA-MODEL.md section 8; admin/lib/data/audit.ts) Persist the audit log append-only in the database (no update/delete grants); include host-side sensitive actions (org role changes, payouts) too.
U14 Filter chip "Suspended/Deleted" (task 6) Facets by status exist in admin Status filters must include soft-deleted rows only for permitted roles.
U15 Arabic with Latin digits; Sunday first day; Algerian weekend Fri-Sat (section 5.2) Formatting rule in admin/lib/utils/format.ts Store dates as date keys / UTC timestamps with Africa/Algiers business timezone; week-based reports start Sunday.
U16 Novice moderator vs power users (Nadia, Karim, Samir) RBAC roles in admin/lib/permissions.ts Role/permission model in the database with server enforcement (already intended in admin/README.md section 3).

5. Quick list of open questions for the blueprint

  1. Wallet model: prepaid commission (DS 9) vs escrow with payouts (admin seed). Drives payments, ledger accounts and payout flow (D-16).
  2. Commission base and rate resolution order, including per-host override (D-3, D-5).
  3. Approval mode resolution and who may respond to requests; request TTL as a setting with a real scheduler (D-6, D-7, D-8).
  4. Unified booking, listing and host status machines (D-9, D-10, admin docs/DATA-MODEL.md).
  5. Trips as their own table with departures vs listings subtype, and the /trips naming collision (D-11).
  6. Vertical taxonomy: is hotel a vertical or a business category of home (D-12, D-20)?
  7. Onboarding config schema and whether the 2-step individual cap is intended (D-13, D-14, D-15).
  8. Moderation before publish for listings and trips (D-10).

BLADUS backend research: comparable platforms and Django ecosystem

Status: working notes for the backend blueprint. Research date for every source: 2026-11-04 (all URLs accessed on that date). Scope: Airbnb-style marketplace for Algeria (homes, hotels with room types, hostels with per-bed booking, experiences, vehicle rentals, multi-day agency trips with departures). Two Next.js frontends (customer app, admin/partner app), backend Django + PostgreSQL.

Conventions in this file:

  • "Verified" means the fact was read from the cited page or from the package registry (PyPI, npm, GitHub API) on 2026-11-04.
  • "Unverified" or "secondary" means the fact comes from a third-party summary, not a primary source. Treat those as hints.
  • Version numbers come from the PyPI JSON API (https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/json), the npm registry, or GitHub releases, queried on 2026-11-04.

Part A. How comparable platforms are built

A.1 Airbnb engineering

Topic What Airbnb published Source
Monolith to SOA Airbnb moved from a Rails monolith ("Monorail") to services starting around 2016. Services were defined in a Thrift-based IDL with generated clients; request context and deadlines are propagated; load shedding via request deadlines; schema-based mocks for tests to avoid a "hidden monolith". InfoQ coverage notes a design rule: services own both reads and writes of their data, and the migration compared outputs between monolith and services by replaying traffic. Building Services at Airbnb, parts 1 to 4: https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/building-services-at-airbnb-part-1-c4c1d8fa811b , https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/building-services-at-airbnb-part-2-142be1c5d506 , https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/building-services-at-airbnb-part-3-ac6d4972fc2d , https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/building-services-at-airbnb-part-4-23c95e428064 ; InfoQ: https://www.infoq.com/news/2019/02/airbnb-monolith-migration-soa/
Search and ranking Ranking started with gradient boosted decision trees, then moved to neural networks when gains plateaued; later papers cover diversity in ranking and embedding-based retrieval (2026). arXiv 1810.09591 https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.09591 ; blog https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/applying-deep-learning-to-airbnb-search-7ebd7230891f ; follow-ups https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.05515 , https://arxiv.org/pdf/2210.07774 , https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.06873
Pricing Smart Pricing suggests a price for every check-in date from demand, supply and listing features, and models booking lead time per date and location. https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/learning-market-dynamics-for-optimal-pricing-97cffbcc53e3
Availability / calendar No primary Airbnb engineering post describing the calendar/availability service architecture was found. Unverified, so not used. (none)
Payments idempotency "Orpheus" idempotency library: client sends an idempotency key per new request and reuses it on retries; request split into pre-RPC, RPC, post-RPC phases with a row-level lock on the key; errors must be classified retryable vs non-retryable; idempotency data read and written on the primary DB (never replicas) to avoid duplicate payments. https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/avoiding-double-payments-in-a-distributed-payments-system-2981f6b070bb
Ledger / financial reporting Financial data is modeled as accounting events producing a double-entry subledger (accounts such as receivables, payables/host liabilities, revenue, taxes). The old approach (reverse-engineering finance from audit trails and DB triggers) was error-prone. https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/tracking-the-money-scaling-financial-reporting-at-airbnb-6d742b80f040 ; https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/scaling-airbnbs-payment-platform-43ebfc99b324
Messaging "Messaging sync": clients fetch only changed threads/messages since last sync instead of full refetch; messaging is tightly coupled to the booking flow (status changes appear in threads). https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/messaging-sync-scaling-mobile-messaging-at-airbnb-659142036f06
Trust and safety ML risk scores (e.g. chargeback model) drive targeted friction: only risky users get extra verification steps, so good users are not penalized; effect measured via experiments. https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/fighting-financial-fraud-with-targeted-friction-82d950d8900e
Reviews Homes: both guest and host have 14 days after checkout; reviews are published when both submitted or when the 14 days end, whichever comes first (double-blind). https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/13 ; https://airbnb.com/help/article/995
Cancellation policies Third-party (secondary) sources report Airbnb restructured standard policies on 2025-10-01 to Flexible / Moderate / Limited / Firm with a 24 h grace period and optional non-refundable rate. Not verified on an Airbnb primary page. secondary: https://www.hostfully.com/blog/airbnb-cancellation-policy/

A.2 Booking.com, Expedia, Vrbo, GetYourGuide

Platform Pattern Source
Booking.com Inventory model = room type x rate plan ("roomrate"). Rooms-to-sell is set per room type per date and shared across all rate plans of that room type; prices and most restrictions (min stay, closed to arrival, etc.) are per room-type + rate-plan + date. Child rate plans can derive from a parent. They recommend loading 12 months ahead. https://developers.booking.com/connectivity/docs/ari.md ; https://developers.booking.com/connectivity/docs/b_xml-availability ; https://developers.booking.com/connectivity/docs/room-type-and-rate-plan-management/managing-roomrates ; https://developers.booking.com/connectivity/docs/room-type-and-rate-plan-management/managing-rate-plans
Booking.com reviews Only people who booked through the platform can review (includes no-shows and bookers for others); written reviews are moderated; reviews remain visible 36 months; removal conditions are enumerated. https://partner.booking.com/en-us/help/guest-reviews/general/guest-review-process-and-conditions ; https://www.booking.com/reviews_guidelines.html
Expedia Rapid Cancellation policy is data, not text: each rate has refundable + cancel_penalties[] (time windows with amount/percent/nights) + nonrefundable_date_ranges; since Feb 2025 also current_refundability (refundable / non_refundable / partially_refundable). Booking page must show the policy before confirmation. https://developers.expediagroup.com/rapid/lodging/shopping/constructing-cancellation-policies ; https://developers.expediagroup.com/rapid/setup/launch-requirements/lodging-launch-reqs
GetYourGuide Activities inventory = time-slotted vacancies per product option; flow is availability then reserve (hold) then confirm; supplier systems push availability updates; they rebuilt inventory on Kafka Streams when DB tables and stale availability caused booking errors. https://www.getyourguide.careers/posts/scaling-the-inventory-parts-of-our-system-using-kafka-streams ; https://github.com/getyourguide/partner-api-spec ; https://www.getyourguide.supply/connectivity/partners-faqs
Vrbo No primary engineering or API documentation could be retrieved (developer portal did not respond). Unverified; not used. (none)

A.3 Open-source projects and reference models worth studying

Project Stack What is useful for BLADUS Link
pretix Django Best Django reference for quota-based inventory: an item can belong to several quotas, all must be available; availability = limit minus paid orders, pending orders within payment period, unexpired cart holds, blocking vouchers, waiting list. Directly maps to experiences, trip departures and hostel beds. Active (pushed 2026-11-04). https://github.com/pretix/pretix ; https://docs.pretix.eu/dev/development/concepts.html ; https://docs.pretix.eu/dev/development/implementation/models.html
Saleor Django + GraphQL Order/payment state machines, checkout, channels, multi-currency, webhooks, permission groups. BSD-3. https://github.com/saleor/saleor
django-oscar Django Mature domain-driven e-commerce: baskets, offers, order/payment events, app overriding pattern. https://github.com/django-oscar/django-oscar
QloApps PHP (PrestaShop-based) Open-source hotel booking + channel manager concepts: hotel, room type, room, booking per date, demand-based pricing. Data model reference only. OSL-3.0. https://github.com/Qloapps/QloApps
django-hordak Django Double-entry accounting models (accounts, transactions, legs) enforced with DB constraints; good reference for the payouts ledger. Last push 2026-04-02, small project. https://github.com/adamcharnock/django-hordak
TigerBeetle Zig DB Purpose-built double-entry ledger DB; worth reading its design docs on debits/credits and pending (two-phase) transfers even if we do not adopt it. https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle
Modern Treasury "Accounting for developers" Article series Clear explanation of double-entry for engineers. https://www.moderntreasury.com/journal/accounting-for-developers-part-i
Chargily Pay v2 Algerian gateway EDAHABIA (Algerie Poste) and CIB (SATIM) checkouts; HMAC signature header on webhooks; test and live modes; Python SDK exists. Likely the first local payment integration. https://dev.chargily.com/pay-v2/introduction ; https://dev.chargily.com/pay-v2/webhooks

A.4 Domain model summary for BLADUS (derived)

Unifying idea: every bookable product reduces to an inventory unit + a time shape + a capacity.

Vertical Listing Sellable unit Time shape Capacity per slot Comparable model
Home Property the whole property nightly date range 1 Airbnb
Hotel Property RoomType (pool of N physical Rooms) + RatePlan nightly date range N per date (rooms-to-sell) Booking.com roomrate
Hostel Property BedType / Dorm (pool of beds), optionally specific Bed nightly date range beds per date Booking.com room type with count
Experience Activity Option time slot (start datetime) seats per slot GetYourGuide, pretix quota
Vehicle Vehicle (or vehicle class pool) Vehicle datetime range (pickup/return) 1 per vehicle, N per class car rental
Agency trip Trip Departure (fixed dates) fixed multi-day departure seats per departure pretix quota per departure

Core entities: Organization (host or agency, with members and roles), Listing (polymorphic by vertical), InventoryUnit, RatePlan, DailyRate/PriceRule, AvailabilityBlock, CancellationPolicy (structured), Booking + BookingLine + state machine, Hold (short TTL), Payment, Refund, Payout, LedgerAccount + LedgerEntry, Review (bound to a completed booking), Thread + Message, Report/ModerationCase, AuditEvent.

A.5 Hard problems and what we decide

Hard problem What the platforms show BLADUS decision
Double booking Airbnb publishes nothing primary on calendars; Django/PostgreSQL offer native exclusion constraints on ranges (ExclusionConstraint + RangeOperators.OVERLAPS, requires btree_gist). For capacity-1 units (home, specific vehicle, specific room or bed when assigned): store stay = DateRangeField (half-open [checkin, checkout)) and add an ExclusionConstraint(unit WITH =, stay WITH &&) WHERE status IN active states. The DB is the last line of defense; the service layer catches IntegrityError and returns a 409. For pooled capacity (hotel room types, hostel beds, experience slots, trip departures): an InventoryDay/SlotInventory row per unit per date with total, held, booked and a CHECK (held + booked <= total); reserve with UPDATE ... SET held = held + n WHERE ... AND held + booked + n <= total (atomic, row-locked) inside a transaction. Holds expire via a scheduled job (pretix cart-hold idea).
Availability search at scale Booking.com precomputes ARI per date; GetYourGuide moved to streaming when DB-backed inventory became stale and slow. Phase 1: query PostgreSQL directly (PostGIS bounding box + filters + NOT EXISTS overlapping bookings / InventoryDay min availability over the range), with GiST and B-tree indexes. Keep a denormalized ListingSearchDoc row per listing updated by signals/tasks. Only add an external engine when measured latency demands it (Algeria-scale catalog is small). Never trust search results for booking: re-check inside the booking transaction.
Pricing Booking.com: price per room-type x rate-plan x date; Airbnb: per-date suggestions. Store explicit nightly prices per unit/date (DailyRate) materialized from rules (base, weekend, season, length-of-stay discount). Price quote is computed server side, returned with a signed quote_id and expiry, and re-validated at booking.
Payments, escrow, payouts Airbnb: idempotency keys with row lock on primary DB; double-entry subledger from accounting events. Every money-moving endpoint requires an Idempotency-Key header (IETF draft https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header/ , Stripe pattern https://stripe.com/docs/api/idempotent_requests ). Immutable double-entry ledger in PostgreSQL: LedgerTransaction with LedgerEntry legs whose sum is zero per currency (enforced by a deferred constraint trigger or by service + check). Accounts: guest_receivable, platform_escrow (funds held until check-in + N hours), host_payable, platform_revenue (fees), tax_payable, refunds. Balances derived from entries, never edited. Payouts are batch jobs that move host_payable to paid. Gateway webhooks (Chargily HMAC) are stored raw, verified, deduplicated by event id, then processed idempotently.
Cancellation policies Expedia models policies as penalty windows; Airbnb has named tiers. Store CancellationPolicy as named templates with structured windows[] (hours_before_start, refund_percent, fee_nights); snapshot the policy onto the booking at confirmation (policy changes never affect existing bookings). Refund calculation is a pure function tested with hypothesis.
Fraud and fake listings Airbnb: risk scores plus targeted friction; a single decision model applies to users, listings and reservations (secondary source https://dmitry.pt/2023/detecting-risk-in-real-time-technology ). Listing goes draft -> pending_review -> published; admin moderation queue in the back-office. KYC for hosts and agencies (ID + registre de commerce for agencies) before payout enablement. Rule-based risk flags (new account + high value, many failed payments, duplicate photo hashes via perceptual hash, off-platform contact info in messages) that trigger friction (phone OTP, manual review) instead of blanket blocks. All decisions recorded as ModerationCase with audit trail.
Review integrity Booking.com: only bookers can review, moderation, fixed visibility window. Airbnb: 14-day window, double-blind reveal. Review requires a Booking in completed state, one review per booking per direction, window of 14 days after end, double-blind reveal (publish when both submitted or window closes), no edits after reveal, host may reply once, moderation for abuse with reasons logged. Aggregate ratings stored denormalized on the listing and recomputed by task.
Messaging Airbnb sync model: only fetch changes. Thread per booking/inquiry; cursor-based "changes since" endpoint so polling is cheap; realtime push is an optimization layered on top (see B.6). Mask phone numbers/emails before booking confirmation.
Architecture Airbnb SOA was a response to hundreds of engineers on one codebase. Start as a modular monolith (one Django project, bounded-context apps, services/selectors, no cross-app model writes). Services are a later option, not a starting point.

Part B. Django ecosystem decisions

Baseline versions (PyPI, 2026-11-04): Django 6.1.3 (latest), 6.0.10, 5.2.19 LTS (extended support until April 2028); next LTS 6.2 scheduled April 2027 (https://www.djangoproject.com/download/). Django 6.0 (released 2025-12-03) added built-in Tasks framework and CSP support (https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2025/dec/03/django-60-released/ , https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.0/releases/6.0/). psycopg 3.3.7.

Recommendation for baseline: Django 6.1 on Python 3.13, plan upgrade to 6.2 LTS in 2027. Rationale: 5.2 LTS lacks django.tasks and CSP; 6.1 is supported until December 2027, overlapping 6.2 LTS. Alternative if the team prefers fewer upgrades: 5.2 LTS + django-tasks backport. Note the user brief says the frontends are Next.js 14; npm next latest is 16.4.5, which matters for SSR auth patterns below.

B.1 PostgreSQL + PostGIS, range types and exclusion constraints

Option Pros Cons
PostGIS + GeoDjango (django.contrib.gis) Real geography types, ST_DWithin distance queries with GiST index, bounding-box map search, polygon areas (wilayas, communes). First-class in Django ORM. Needs GDAL/GEOS/PROJ system libs in containers; managed PG must offer PostGIS.
Plain lat/lng floats + Haversine or earthdistance/cube No system libs. No polygon support, weaker indexing, reinventing GIS.

Range types + exclusion: django.contrib.postgres.fields.DateRangeField / DateTimeRangeField, ExclusionConstraint with RangeOperators.OVERLAPS and RangeOperators.EQUAL, optional condition=Q(...) (partial), BtreeGistExtension migration op required for the equality part (verified in docs: https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.0/ref/contrib/postgres/constraints/ , https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.0/ref/contrib/postgres/fields/ , https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/rangetypes.html , https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/btree-gist.html).

Recommendation: PostGIS + GeoDjango (https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.0/ref/contrib/gis/ , https://postgis.net/). Store location = PointField(geography=True, srid=4326) and public "fuzzed" point for homes (exact address revealed after booking). Use DateRangeField + ExclusionConstraint for capacity-1 units and CHECK-constrained inventory counters for pooled units (see A.5). Note: violation of an exclusion constraint surfaces as IntegrityError on save; violation_error_code only applies to model validation.

B.2 API layer: DRF vs Django Ninja

Django REST Framework Django Ninja
Latest 3.18.3 (2026-10-06) 1.7.3 (2026-10-29)
Activity Very active releases in 2026; maintainers state it is "considered feature-complete" (https://www.django-rest-framework.org/community/release-notes/) Active (pushed 2026-11-04), 9.2k stars
Pros Largest ecosystem (drf-spectacular, guardian/rules integration, throttling, filters, SimpleJWT, standardized errors); every Django dev knows it; browsable API. Pydantic schemas, type hints drive validation and OpenAPI automatically, fast, async-friendly, less boilerplate.
Cons Serializer verbosity, OpenAPI via add-on, sync-first. Smaller ecosystem: permissions, throttling, filtering patterns are thinner; fewer battle-tested auth/permission libs.

Recommendation: DRF, used in the HackSoft style (thin APIView + input/output serializers + services). Reason: the permission, throttling, audit and OpenAPI tooling we need is mature around DRF, and the hiring pool in Algeria will know DRF. Ninja is a fine choice if the team values Pydantic typing more; allauth headless supports both.

B.3 Auth

django-allauth (headless) dj-rest-auth + SimpleJWT
Latest 65.21.1 (2026-10-30), very active dj-rest-auth 7.2.0 (2026-03-15); SimpleJWT 5.5.1 (2025-07-21)
Features Headless API for SPA/mobile with session tokens or JWT strategies, OpenAPI spec, email + phone login and SMS verification (adapter implements send_verification_code_sms), social login, built-in MFA (TOTP, recovery codes, WebAuthn/passkeys), rate limits. REST endpoints for login/registration/password reset, JWT or tokens; social via allauth underneath.
Cons Opinionated flow model; headless docs are spread across pages. Two libraries glued together, slower release cadence, no built-in MFA or phone OTP.

Sources: https://docs.allauth.org/en/latest/headless/index.html , https://docs.allauth.org/en/latest/headless/token-strategies/index.html , https://docs.allauth.org/en/latest/account/phone.html , https://docs.allauth.org/en/latest/mfa/index.html , https://github.com/iMerica/dj-rest-auth , https://github.com/jazzband/djangorestframework-simplejwt

Phone OTP: allauth phone support needs us to provide phone storage and an SMS sender. SMS provider choice for Algeria (local aggregators vs Twilio/Vonage) was not researched here; unverified. Store numbers with django-phonenumber-field 9.0.0 (E.164).

Sessions vs JWT for Next.js SSR: server components run on the Next.js server, so they cannot read browser localStorage; they can forward cookies. Next.js docs describe cookie-based session management for the App Router (https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/authentication). Two workable patterns:

  1. Same-site deployment (app.bladus.dz + api.bladus.dz): Django session cookie with Domain=.bladus.dz, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, CSRF token for mutations. Server components forward the incoming cookie header to the API.
  2. Next.js as BFF: Next.js stores an encrypted httpOnly cookie containing the allauth session token (app client flow, X-Session-Token) and attaches it on server-side fetches.

Recommendation: django-allauth headless with session-token strategy, Next.js BFF pattern (2) for the customer app, short sessions plus mandatory MFA (allauth MFA TOTP/WebAuthn) for staff in the admin app. Avoid long-lived JWTs in the browser (revocation is hard). django-otp 1.7.5 is the alternative if we keep Django admin login separate; prefer one MFA system (allauth MFA) unless Django admin is exposed, in which case add django-otp on the admin site only.

B.4 Permissions (object-level, org roles owner/admin/manager)

DRF permissions (custom classes) django-guardian django-rules
Latest built into DRF 3.18.3 3.5.2 (2026-10-20), active rules 3.5 (2024-09-02); repo pushed 2025-10
Model has_permission / has_object_permission per view per-object permission rows in DB (user/group x perm x object) predicates (Python functions) composed with &, `
Pros Simple, no deps Fine-grained grants, admin integration Expressive, testable, zero storage, integrates with Django's perm API and DRF
Cons Logic scattered per view Row explosion (every listing x member x perm), sync burden when memberships change Release cadence slow (stable, small codebase); queryset filtering must be written separately

Sources: https://www.django-rest-framework.org/api-guide/permissions/ , https://django-guardian.readthedocs.io/ , https://github.com/dfunckt/django-rules

Recommendation: Org-scoped RBAC in our own tables (Membership(user, organization, role)), predicates in django-rules (is_org_owner, is_org_manager_of(listing)), exposed through thin DRF permission classes; plus selectors that always filter querysets by the caller's organizations (permissions alone do not protect list endpoints). Skip guardian: our grants derive from org membership, not per-object ACLs.

B.5 Background jobs

Option Latest Notes
Celery + Redis/RabbitMQ celery 5.6.3 (2026-03-26) De facto standard; beat scheduler, retries, chords, Flower monitoring. Heavier config, many knobs. https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/
Dramatiq 2.2.1 (2026-09-02) Simpler, reliable defaults (acks late), LGPL. https://dramatiq.io/
Django-Q2 1.11.1 (2026-08-26) Can use the DB as broker, admin integration; smaller community. https://django-q2.readthedocs.io/
Huey 3.5.4 (2026-11-01) Lightweight, Redis or SQLite, periodic tasks. https://huey.readthedocs.io/
Django django.tasks (Django 6.0+) built-in DEP 14 "Background workers" status Accepted, implemented in 6.0. Django provides definition, queuing and results only; built-in backends (ImmediateBackend, DummyBackend) are for dev/test; production needs a third-party backend with a worker, e.g. django-tasks-db 0.13.0 (2026-08-28) or django-tasks-rq 0.12.0. Arguments must be JSON-serializable; enqueue inside transaction.on_commit. https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.0/topics/tasks/ , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/django/deps/main/final/0014-background-workers.rst , https://github.com/RealOrangeOne/django-tasks

Recommendation: Celery 5.6 + Redis for now (needs: hold expiry, payout batches, scheduled reminders, image processing, search doc refresh, webhooks retry with backoff). Write tasks as thin wrappers around services and enqueue via transaction.on_commit, so moving to django.tasks later is mechanical once its worker backends mature. Use celery beat with django-celery-beat (not version-checked here) or a code-defined schedule.

B.6 Realtime messaging

Option Pros Cons
Django Channels + channels-redis Same codebase and auth; channels 4.3.2 (2025-11-20), channels-redis 4.3.0 (2025-07-22). https://channels.readthedocs.io/ Needs ASGI servers and sticky long-lived connections managed by us; release cadence slowed in 2025.
Centrifugo (self-hosted, Go) v6.10.2 (2026-10-23). Handles WebSocket/SSE/HTTP-streaming connections; Django only publishes over HTTP API and issues expiring JWT connection tokens; positions itself as a self-hosted alternative to Pusher/Ably. https://centrifugal.dev/docs/getting-started/comparisons Another service to run. Some features only in paid PRO.
Pusher / Ably (managed) Zero ops Data leaves to foreign SaaS, per-message cost, not self-hostable. Pricing not researched here.
Polling / SSE Simplest; works with "changes since cursor" endpoint (Airbnb messaging sync idea). Latency and wasted requests at scale.

Recommendation: Launch with cursor-based polling (every 5 to 15 s while a thread is open, slower in inbox) over a sync endpoint, plus push notifications/email. Add Centrifugo when realtime matters (keeps Django WSGI-only, simpler than running Channels). Channels is the fallback if we want everything in Python.

B.7 Search

Option Latest Pros Cons
PostgreSQL FTS + pg_trgm + PostGIS built in One datastore, transactional consistency with availability, Django SearchVector, TrigramSimilarity, GiST/GIN indexes. https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.0/ref/contrib/postgres/search/ , https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/pgtrgm.html Arabic stemming support in PostgreSQL FTS is limited (no built-in Arabic snowball config verified here); relevance tuning is manual.
Meilisearch server v1.56.1 (2026-11-02), py client 0.43.0 Typo tolerance, facets, geosearch (_geoRadius, _geoBoundingBox), easy ops. https://www.meilisearch.com/docs/learn/filtering_and_sorting/geosearch Separate index to keep in sync; availability must still be checked in PG.
Typesense v30.2 (2026-04-19), py client 2.1.1 Similar feature set, geo search, in-memory speed. https://typesense.org/docs/guide/ Same sync burden; RAM-bound.
OpenSearch 3.9.0 (2026-09-29) Most powerful (analyzers incl. Arabic, aggregations). Heavy to operate for our scale.

Recommendation: PostgreSQL first (PostGIS distance/bbox + filters + unaccent + pg_trgm for place/title autocomplete, FTS for descriptions). Keep a ListingSearchDoc table that is engine-agnostic. Add Meilisearch later if multilingual typo-tolerant text search (especially Arabic and Latin transliterations like "Tizi Ouzou" vs "تيزي وزو") becomes a product need. Availability filtering always stays in PostgreSQL.

B.8 Files and images

django-storages + S3-compatible Cloudinary
Latest django-storages 1.14.6 (2025-04-02; no release since, repo should be watched) (SaaS; Python SDK not version-checked)
Pros Vendor-neutral; Cloudflare R2 has no egress fees for S3 API / public access (https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/), supports presigned URLs (https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/s3/presigned-urls/); B2, Scaleway, OVH also S3-compatible. On-the-fly transforms, CDN, moderation add-ons in one product.
Cons We build the resize pipeline. Cost scales with transformations and bandwidth; lock-in.

Pipeline options: Pillow 13.0.0 in a Celery task (generate fixed renditions, strip EXIF/GPS), or imgproxy v4.0.21 (2026-11-02) / thumbor (active) as on-the-fly resizer behind the CDN with signed URLs (https://docs.imgproxy.net/ , https://github.com/thumbor/thumbor). Virus scanning: ClamAV 1.5.4 (2026-08-07) via clamd in a worker for documents (KYC PDFs); images are re-encoded by Pillow, which neutralizes most payloads (https://docs.clamav.net/).

Recommendation: django-storages (S3 backend) + Cloudflare R2, private bucket for KYC documents, public bucket behind CDN for listing photos. Uploads via presigned PUT from the browser to a quarantine/ prefix, then a task validates MIME + size, re-encodes with Pillow to WebP/AVIF + JPEG fallback renditions, computes a perceptual hash (duplicate/fake listing detection), and moves to public/. Consider imgproxy later. Data residency for Algerian law on personal data (Law 18-07) was not researched here and must be checked before storing KYC abroad.

B.9 Content translations fr/en/ar

django-modeltranslation django-parler
Latest 0.20.6 (2026-09-07), active 2.4 (2026-05-14), active
Storage Extra columns per language on the same table (title_fr, title_en, title_ar) Separate translation table per model
Pros Simple queries, easy indexing/FTS per language, no joins, works with admin. Unlimited languages without migrations, clean schema.
Cons Adding a language = migration; wide tables. Joins/prefetch on every read, harder filtering and ordering.

Sources: https://django-modeltranslation.readthedocs.io/ , https://django-parler.readthedocs.io/

Recommendation: django-modeltranslation for platform-owned taxonomy (amenities, categories, wilayas, policy names): fixed 3 languages, fast reads, per-language search columns. For user-generated text (listing titles/descriptions) store the host's original text + source_language, plus optional translated fields filled by humans or machine translation later; do not force hosts to write three versions.

B.10 Back-office

Custom Next.js admin (existing) Django admin + Unfold
Latest existing app django-unfold 0.110.1 (2026-11-01), very active (https://unfoldadmin.com/)
Pros Product-quality UX for partners and ops, same design system, same API (dogfooding). Free CRUD on every model, filters, actions, inline history; minutes to add a screen.
Cons Every internal tool must be built through the API. Not for partners/hosts; risk of bypassing service-layer rules if admins edit models directly.

Recommendation: Both, with clear roles. The Next.js admin is the product (partner dashboards, moderation queue, payouts review, support). Django admin + Unfold is a staff-only, MFA-protected, IP-restricted engineering/support console, mostly read-only for financial models (ledger entries never editable), with admin actions calling services.

B.11 Audit logging

django-simple-history django-auditlog django-pghistory
Latest 3.13.0 (2026-07-22), django-commons 3.4.1 (2025-12-18), jazzband 3.9.2 (2026-02-17), AmbitionEng
Mechanism Python signals, full historical table per model Python signals, single LogEntry table with JSON diffs PostgreSQL triggers (django-pgtrigger), event tables, context (user, request) attached
Pros Point-in-time snapshots, admin integration Simple, one table Captures bulk updates, raw SQL and queryset.update() that signals miss; reliable
Cons Misses update()/bulk ops Same; diffs only PostgreSQL only (fine for us), triggers in migrations

Sources: https://django-simple-history.readthedocs.io/en/stable/ , https://django-auditlog.readthedocs.io/ , https://django-pghistory.readthedocs.io/

Recommendation: django-pghistory for bookings, payments, payouts, listings, memberships, policies (bulk updates in inventory and payouts would escape signal-based tools). Plus an explicit domain AuditEvent/activity log written by services for human-readable "who did what" in the back-office. The ledger is itself append-only and needs no history.

B.12 Rate limiting, caching, idempotency

  • DRF throttling (built in; scoped throttles per endpoint, Redis cache backend) https://www.django-rest-framework.org/api-guide/throttling/ . django-ratelimit 4.1.0 is from 2023-07-24 with repo last pushed 2024-07: stable but inactive. allauth has its own rate limits for auth endpoints. Recommendation: DRF scoped throttles for API, allauth limits for auth, plus edge limits at the reverse proxy/CDN.
  • Caching: Redis via Django's built-in RedisCache. django-cachalot 2.9.1 (2026-08-10) auto-caches ORM queries and invalidates per table; on write-heavy tables (inventory, bookings) invalidation is constant, so value is low. Recommendation: explicit caching of computed results (search facets, listing detail, quote) with versioned keys; no cachalot.
  • Idempotency keys: django-idempotency-key 1.3.0 last released 2023-05-02 (inactive). Recommendation: small in-house implementation following Airbnb Orpheus and the IETF draft: IdempotencyRecord(key, user, endpoint, request_hash, status, response, locked_at, expires_at) on the primary DB, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, replay the stored response for repeats, 409 for concurrent in-flight, 422 for same key different body.

  • TS generators (npm, 2026-11-04):

orval 8.46.0 (2026-10-30) Clients + TanStack Query hooks + MSW mocks + Zod Very active, heavier
@hey-api/openapi-ts 0.99.0 (2026-06-22) SDK, types, Zod, TanStack plugins Pre-1.0 (breaking changes possible)

Recommendation: drf-spectacular -> openapi.json committed in CI -> openapi-typescript + openapi-fetch shared package used by both Next.js apps (fits server components and route handlers; no hooks runtime required). Consider orval only if the apps standardize on TanStack Query in client components.

B.14 Testing

Tool Latest Role

Recommendation: pytest-django + factory_boy (explicit, readable domain factories) + hypothesis for money and date-range logic + schemathesis in CI against the generated schema. Concurrency tests for double booking using real PostgreSQL (transaction=True tests with threads), never SQLite.

B.15 Project structure

  • HackSoft Django Styleguide: business logic in services (writes) and selectors (reads), thin APIs, models without heavy logic, explicit input/output serializers (https://github.com/HackSoftware/Django-Styleguide). Last pushed 2025-09.
  • cookiecutter-django: production template (Docker, Celery, allauth, django-environ, Sentry, pytest), release 2026.11.3 on 2026-11-04, very active (https://github.com/cookiecutter/cookiecutter-django).
  • Two Scoops of Django: book; no current edition for Django 6 was verified, so treat as general guidance only.

Recommendation: Bootstrap from cookiecutter-django ideas (not necessarily the generator), organize as a modular monolith with apps per bounded context: accounts, organizations, catalog (listings, units, media, amenities), inventory (availability, holds), pricing, bookings, payments (gateway, ledger, payouts), reviews, messaging, trust (moderation, risk, KYC), notifications, geo, search, audit. Follow HackSoft services/selectors; cross-app calls go through services, never through another app's models directly. Enforce boundaries with import-linter (not version-checked here).

B.17 Money handling

  • ISO 4217 List One gives DZD numeric 012, minor unit 2 (verified via copies of List One: SAP documentation https://help.sap.com/doc/saphelp_pos22/2.2/en-US/4f/efa63a9bb04d94a0ae4c32fd6cd827/content.htm?no_cache=true , Adyen currency table https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/currency-codes ; ISO's own page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; the maintenance agency is SIX https://www.six-group.com/en/products-services/financial-information/data-standards.html). Wikipedia notes centimes rarely circulate (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algerian_dinar).
  • Options:
Integer minor units (BigIntegerField, centimes) DecimalField(max_digits=14, decimal_places=2) / django-money
Pros Exact, fast, matches gateway APIs that use minor units, trivial sums in ledger, no rounding surprises. Human-readable in DB; django-money 3.6.2 adds a Money type and currency field.
Cons Must format at the edges. Decimal context/rounding discipline required; django-money's GitHub repo was archived and the project is migrating to Codeberg (notice dated 2026-06-07), https://codeberg.org/django-money/django-money , so its maintenance path is in transition.

Recommendation: Store integer minor units (centimes) in BigIntegerField + currency CHAR(3) on every amount column, wrapped in a small in-house Money value object (amount_minor, currency) with explicit rounding rules. Business rule: prices shown and charged in whole dinars (amounts are multiples of 100 centimes), but fees, commissions and tax splits are computed in centimes and rounded with a documented rule (round half up at the line level, remainder assigned to platform), so the ledger always balances exactly. This keeps us ISO-correct (minor unit 2) while matching practical whole-dinar pricing. Chargily's amount unit (dinars vs centimes) must be confirmed against its API reference before integration; not verified here.
